Done. Plan written to [doc/CLOUDFLARE.md](doc/CLOUDFLARE.md), with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) updated to point at it.

**Key architectural decisions in the plan**:

- **Deployment platform as an orthogonal axis** (`node | cloudflare`) — does not collapse into the existing auth/exposure axes, leaves `local_trusted` / `authenticated` semantics untouched.
- **Phase 1 = Hyperdrive + Neon Postgres**, not D1. The Drizzle schema uses `jsonb` ([packages/db/src/schema/plugins.ts](packages/db/src/schema/plugins.ts) and others); D1 (SQLite) would force a schema port before anything else works. Phase 1 ships in weeks; Phase 2 (D1) is opt-in.
- **5 minimum upstream seams** — each is independently mergeable and improves the Node deployment too: DB factory split, Scheduler interface, transport-agnostic HTTP `Handler`, `CommandExecutor` interface, storage provider extension point.
- **Express → Hono is incremental, not a rewrite** — introduce a transport-agnostic handler shape, migrate routes one module at a time, hot path first. Until migrated, Workers can fall back to invoking Express handlers via a stream shim.
- **Plugin execution stays in sandboxes** — Workers can't spawn processes, so the existing E2B/SSH sandbox bridge ([#4801](https://github.com/.../pull/4801), [#4803](https://github.com/.../pull/4803)) is the default executor; Cloudflare Containers is opt-in.
- **Per-task DOs with WebSocket Hibernation** + **Workflows for multi-step orchestration** — keeps idle cost at ~$5–6/mo by ensuring nothing is billed when nothing is happening.
- **Setup flow writes to encrypted DB config**, not per-Worker secrets — single source of truth, no CF-API sync, secrets propagate instantly.

The plan includes a 13-step PR sequence (§15) where PRs #1–#7 are upstream improvements that land independently and #8–#13 are the additive `packages/deploy-cloudflare/` work. Nothing in the CF package blocks upstream review.

Yes — to be clear about the two sub-questions:

**PRs #8–#13** (the additive `packages/deploy-cloudflare/` work) live in your fork only. Upstream Paperclip wouldn't accept a Cloudflare-specific package; this is your deployment.

**PRs #1–#7** (the upstream seams: DB factory split, Scheduler interface, Handler shape, CommandExecutor, storage extension point, filesystem quarantine) — you have two choices:

1. **Land them in your fork only.** Faster. You own the seams, you own the merge conflicts when pulling upstream.
2. **Land in your fork, then PR each one upstream.** Slower (each PR needs review, tests, docs, justification *without* mentioning Cloudflare since upstream doesn't care about your deployment — pitch them as "improves testability"). But if any get merged, that's permanent surface area in upstream that your fork doesn't have to maintain.

The plan was written assuming option 2 because you said "abstracted so we can take advantage of all of the open-source updates." That goal is best served by upstreaming the seams: every seam upstream accepts is one less thing your fork has to rebase forever. But it's not required — option 1 still works, you just carry the seam patches in your fork as long-lived diffs.

**Practical recommendation**: do option 1 first (land in fork, ship Phase 1), then opportunistically upstream the cleanest seams (#1 DB factory split, #5 CommandExecutor) which are obviously-good independent of Cloudflare. Don't block your deployment on upstream review.

Either way, the *design* of those PRs as additive/non-breaking is what matters — it minimizes rebase pain whether they ever go upstream or not.

```text
5	
6	let cachedStorageService: StorageService | null = null;
7	let cachedSignature: string | null = null;
8	
9	function signatureForConfig(config: Config): string {
10	  return JSON.stringify({
11	    provider: config.storageProvider,
12	    localDisk: config.storageLocalDiskBaseDir,
13	    s3Bucket: config.storageS3Bucket,
14	    s3Region: config.storageS3Region,
15	    s3Endpoint: config.storageS3Endpoint,
16	    s3Prefix: config.storageS3Prefix,
17	    s3ForcePathStyle: config.storageS3ForcePathStyle,
18	  });
19	}
20	
21	export function createStorageServiceFromConfig(config: Config): StorageService {
22	  return createStorageService(createStorageProviderFromConfig(config));
23	}
24	
25	export function getStorageService(): StorageService {
26	  const config = loadConfig();
27	  const signature = signatureForConfig(config);
28	  if (!cachedStorageService || cachedSignature !== signature) {
29	    cachedStorageService = createStorageServiceFromConfig(config);
30	    cachedSignature = signature;
31	  }
32	  return cachedStorageService;
33	}
```

```ts
import type { Scheduler, ScheduledTask } from "./types.js";
```

```text
215	export function appendWithByteCap(prev: string, chunk: string, cap = MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES) {
216	  const combined = prev + chunk;
217	  const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(combined, "utf8");
218	  if (bytes <= cap) return combined;
219	
220	  const buffer = Buffer.from(combined, "utf8");
221	  let start = Math.max(0, bytes - cap);
222	  while (start < buffer.length && (buffer[start]! & 0xc0) === 0x80) start += 1;
223	  return buffer.subarray(start).toString("utf8");
224	}

232	  const parts = dottedPath.split(".");

234	
235	  for (const part of parts) {
236	    if (typeof cursor !== "object" || cursor === null || Array.isArray(cursor)) {
237	      return "";

239	    cursor = (cursor as Record<string, unknown>)[part];
240	  }
241	
242	  if (cursor === null || cursor === undefined) return "";
243	  if (typeof cursor === "string") return cursor;
244	  if (typeof cursor === "number" || typeof cursor === "boolean") return String(cursor);
245	
246	  try {
247	    return JSON.stringify(cursor);
248	  } catch {
249	    return "";
250	  }
251	}

541	  const unresolvedBlockerSummaries = Array.isArray(payload.unresolvedBlockerSummaries)
542	    ? payload.unresolvedBlockerSummaries
543	        .map((entry) => normalizePaperclipWakeBlockerSummary(entry))
544	        .filter((entry): entry is PaperclipWakeBlockerSummary => Boolean(entry))
545	    : [];
546	
547	  const activeTreeHold = normalizePaperclipWakeTreeHoldSummary(payload.activeTreeHold);
548	  if (comments.length === 0 && commentIds.length === 0 && childIssueSummaries.length === 0 && unresolvedBlockerIssueIds.length === 0 && unresolvedBlockerSummaries.length === 0 && !activeTreeHold && !executionStage && !continuationSummary && !livenessContinuation && !normalizePaperclipWakeIssue(payload.issue)) {
549	    return null;
550	  }
551	
552	  return {
553	    reason: asString(payload.reason, "").trim() || null,
554	    issue: normalizePaperclipWakeIssue(payload.issue),
555	    checkedOutByHarness: asBoolean(payload.checkedOutByHarness, false),
556	    dependencyBlockedInteraction: asBoolean(payload.dependencyBlockedInteraction, false),
557	    treeHoldInteraction: asBoolean(payload.treeHoldInteraction, false),
558	    activeTreeHold,
559	    unresolvedBlockerIssueIds,
560	    unresolvedBlockerSummaries,
561	    executionStage,
562	    continuationSummary,
563	    livenessContinuation,
564	    childIssueSummaries,
565	    childIssueSummaryTruncated: asBoolean(payload.childIssueSummaryTruncated, false),
566	    commentIds,
567	    latestCommentId: asString(payload.latestCommentId, "").trim() || null,
568	    comments,
569	    requestedCount: asNumber(commentWindow.requestedCount, comments.length || commentIds.length),
570	    includedCount: asNumber(commentWindow.includedCount, comments.length),
571	    missingCount: asNumber(commentWindow.missingCount, 0),
572	    truncated: asBoolean(payload.truncated, false),
573	    fallbackFetchNeeded: asBoolean(payload.fallbackFetchNeeded, false),
574	  };
575	}

583	export function renderPaperclipWakePrompt(
584	  value: unknown,
585	  options: { resumedSession?: boolean } = {},
586	): string {
587	  const normalized = normalizePaperclipWakePayload(value);
588	  if (!normalized) return "";
589	  const resumedSession = options.resumedSession === true;
590	  const executionStage = normalized.executionStage;
591	  const principalLabel = (principal: PaperclipWakeExecutionPrincipal | null) => {
592	    if (!principal || !principal.type) return "unknown";
593	    if (principal.type === "agent") return principal.agentId ? `agent ${principal.agentId}` : "agent";
594	    return principal.userId ? `user ${principal.userId}` : "user";
595	  };
596	
597	  const lines = resumedSession
598	      ? [
599	        "## Paperclip Resume Delta",
600	        "",
601	        "You are resuming an existing Paperclip session.",
602	        "This heartbeat is scoped to the issue below. Do not switch to another issue until you have handled this wake.",
603	        "Focus on the new wake delta below and continue the current task without restating the full heartbeat boilerplate.",
604	        "Fetch the API thread only when `fallbackFetchNeeded` is true or you need broader history than this batch.",
605	        "",
606	        "Execution contract: take concrete action in this heartbeat when the issue is actionable; do not stop at a plan unless planning was requested. Leave durable progress with a clear next action, use child issues instead of polling for long or parallel work, and mark blocked work with the unblock owner/action.",
607	        "",
608	        `- reason: ${normalized.reason ?? "unknown"}`,
609	        `- issue: ${normalized.issue?.identifier ?? normalized.issue?.id ?? "unknown"}${normalized.issue?.title ? ` ${normalized.issue.title}` : ""}`,
610	        `- pending comments: ${normalized.includedCount}/${normalized.requestedCount}`,
611	        `- latest comment id: ${normalized.latestCommentId ?? "unknown"}`,
612	        `- fallback fetch needed: ${normalized.fallbackFetchNeeded ? "yes" : "no"}`,
613	      ]
614	    : [
615	        "## Paperclip Wake Payload",
616	        "",
617	        "Treat this wake payload as the highest-priority change for the current heartbeat.",
618	        "This heartbeat is scoped to the issue below. Do not switch to another issue until you have handled this wake.",
619	        "Before generic repo exploration or boilerplate heartbeat updates, acknowledge the latest comment and explain how it changes your next action.",
620	        "Use this inline wake data first before refetching the issue thread.",
621	        "Only fetch the API thread when `fallbackFetchNeeded` is true or you need broader history than this batch.",
622	        "",
623	        "Execution contract: take concrete action in this heartbeat when the issue is actionable; do not stop at a plan unless planning was requested. Leave durable progress with a clear next action, use child issues instead of polling for long or parallel work, and mark blocked work with the unblock owner/action.",
624	        "",
625	        `- reason: ${normalized.reason ?? "unknown"}`,
626	        `- issue: ${normalized.issue?.identifier ?? normalized.issue?.id ?? "unknown"}${normalized.issue?.title ? ` ${normalized.issue.title}` : ""}`,
627	        `- pending comments: ${normalized.includedCount}/${normalized.requestedCount}`,
628	        `- latest comment id: ${normalized.latestCommentId ?? "unknown"}`,
629	        `- fallback fetch needed: ${normalized.fallbackFetchNeeded ? "yes" : "no"}`,
630	      ];
631	
632	  if (normalized.issue?.status) {
633	    lines.push(`- issue status: ${normalized.issue.status}`);
634	  }
635	  if (normalized.issue?.priority) {
636	    lines.push(`- issue priority: ${normalized.issue.priority}`);
637	  }
638	  if (normalized.checkedOutByHarness) {
639	    lines.push("- checkout: already claimed by the harness for this run");
640	  }
641	  if (normalized.dependencyBlockedInteraction) {
642	    lines.push("- dependency-blocked interaction: yes");
643	    lines.push("- execution scope: respond or triage the human comment; do not treat blocker-dependent deliverable work as unblocked");
644	    if (normalized.unresolvedBlockerSummaries.length > 0) {
645	      const blockers = normalized.unresolvedBlockerSummaries
646	        .map((blocker) => `${blocker.identifier ?? blocker.id ?? "unknown"}${blocker.title ? ` ${blocker.title}` : ""}${blocker.status ? ` (${blocker.status})` : ""}`)
647	        .join("; ");
648	      lines.push(`- unresolved blockers: ${blockers}`);
649	    } else if (normalized.unresolvedBlockerIssueIds.length > 0) {
650	      lines.push(`- unresolved blocker issue ids: ${normalized.unresolvedBlockerIssueIds.join(", ")}`);
651	    }
652	  }
653	  if (normalized.treeHoldInteraction) {
654	    lines.push("- tree-hold interaction: yes");
655	    lines.push("- execution scope: respond or triage the human comment; the subtree remains paused until an explicit resume action");
656	    if (normalized.activeTreeHold) {
657	      const hold = normalized.activeTreeHold;
658	      lines.push(`- active tree hold: ${hold.holdId ?? "unknown"}${hold.rootIssueId ? ` rooted at ${hold.rootIssueId}` : ""}${hold.mode ? ` (${hold.mode})` : ""}`);
659	    }
660	  }
661	  if (normalized.missingCount > 0) {
662	    lines.push(`- omitted comments: ${normalized.missingCount}`);
663	  }
664	
665	  if (executionStage) {
666	    lines.push(
667	      `- execution wake role: ${executionStage.wakeRole ?? "unknown"}`,
668	      `- execution stage: ${executionStage.stageType ?? "unknown"}`,
669	      `- execution participant: ${principalLabel(executionStage.currentParticipant)}`,
670	      `- execution return assignee: ${principalLabel(executionStage.returnAssignee)}`,
671	      `- last decision outcome: ${executionStage.lastDecisionOutcome ?? "none"}`,
672	    );
673	    if (executionStage.allowedActions.length > 0) {
674	      lines.push(`- allowed actions: ${executionStage.allowedActions.join(", ")}`);
675	    }
676	    if (executionStage.reviewRequest) {
677	      lines.push(
678	        "",
679	        "Review request instructions:",
680	        executionStage.reviewRequest.instructions,
681	      );
682	    }
683	    lines.push("");
684	    if (executionStage.wakeRole === "reviewer" || executionStage.wakeRole === "approver") {
685	      lines.push(
686	        `You are waking as the active ${executionStage.wakeRole} for this issue.`,
687	        "Do not execute the task itself or continue executor work.",
688	        "Review the issue and choose one of the allowed actions above.",
689	        "If you request changes, the workflow routes back to the stored return assignee.",
690	        "",
691	      );
692	    } else if (executionStage.wakeRole === "executor") {
693	      lines.push(
694	        "You are waking because changes were requested in the execution workflow.",
695	        "Address the requested changes on this issue and resubmit when the work is ready.",
696	        "",
697	      );
698	    }
699	  }
700	
701	  if (normalized.continuationSummary) {
702	    lines.push(
703	      "",
704	      "Issue continuation summary:",
705	      normalized.continuationSummary.body,
706	    );
707	    if (normalized.continuationSummary.bodyTruncated) {
708	      lines.push("[continuation summary truncated]");
709	    }
710	  }
711	
712	  if (normalized.livenessContinuation) {
713	    const continuation = normalized.livenessContinuation;
714	    lines.push("", "Run liveness continuation:");
715	    if (continuation.attempt) {
716	      lines.push(
717	        `- attempt: ${continuation.attempt}${continuation.maxAttempts ? `/${continuation.maxAttempts}` : ""}`,
718	      );
719	    }
720	    if (continuation.sourceRunId) {
721	      lines.push(`- source run: ${continuation.sourceRunId}`);
722	    }
723	    if (continuation.state) {
724	      lines.push(`- liveness state: ${continuation.state}`);
725	    }
726	    if (continuation.reason) {
727	      lines.push(`- reason: ${continuation.reason}`);
728	    }
729	    if (continuation.instruction) {
730	      lines.push(`- instruction: ${continuation.instruction}`);
731	    }
732	  }
733	
734	  if (normalized.childIssueSummaries.length > 0) {
735	    lines.push("", "Direct child issue summaries:");
736	    for (const child of normalized.childIssueSummaries) {
737	      const label = child.identifier ?? child.id ?? "unknown";
738	      lines.push(
739	        `- ${label}${child.title ? ` ${child.title}` : ""}${child.status ? ` (${child.status})` : ""}`,
740	      );
741	      if (child.summary) {
742	        lines.push(`  ${child.summary}`);
743	      }
744	    }
745	    if (normalized.childIssueSummaryTruncated) {
746	      lines.push("[child issue summaries truncated]");
747	    }
748	  }
749	
750	  if (normalized.checkedOutByHarness) {
751	    lines.push(
752	      "",
753	      "The harness already checked out this issue for the current run.",
754	      "Do not call `/api/issues/{id}/checkout` again unless you intentionally switch to a different task.",
755	      "",
756	    );
757	  }
758	
759	  if (normalized.comments.length > 0) {
760	    lines.push("New comments in order:");
761	  }
762	
763	  for (const [index, comment] of normalized.comments.entries()) {
764	    const authorLabel = comment.authorId
765	      ? `${comment.authorType ?? "unknown"} ${comment.authorId}`
766	      : comment.authorType ?? "unknown";
767	    lines.push(
768	      `${index + 1}. comment ${comment.id ?? "unknown"} at ${comment.createdAt ?? "unknown"} by ${authorLabel}`,
769	      comment.body,
770	    );
771	    if (comment.bodyTruncated) {
772	      lines.push("[comment body truncated]");
773	    }
774	    lines.push("");
775	  }
776	
777	  return lines.join("\n").trim();
778	}

788	export function buildInvocationEnvForLogs(
789	  env: Record<string, string>,
790	  options: {
791	    runtimeEnv?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv | Record<string, string>;
792	    includeRuntimeKeys?: string[];
793	    resolvedCommand?: string | null;
794	    resolvedCommandEnvKey?: string;
795	  } = {},
796	): Record<string, string> {
797	  const merged: Record<string, string> = { ...env };
798	  const runtimeEnv = options.runtimeEnv ?? {};
799	
800	  for (const key of options.includeRuntimeKeys ?? []) {
801	    if (key in merged) continue;
802	    const value = runtimeEnv[key];
803	    if (typeof value !== "string" || value.length === 0) continue;
804	    merged[key] = value;
805	  }
806	
807	  const resolvedCommand = options.resolvedCommand?.trim();
808	  if (resolvedCommand) {
809	    merged[options.resolvedCommandEnvKey ?? "PAPERCLIP_RESOLVED_COMMAND"] = resolvedCommand;
810	  }
811	
812	  return redactEnvForLogs(merged);
813	}

815	export function buildPaperclipEnv(agent: { id: string; companyId: string }): Record<string, string> {
816	  const resolveHostForUrl = (rawHost: string): string => {
817	    const host = rawHost.trim();
818	    if (!host || host === "0.0.0.0" || host === "::") return "localhost";
819	    if (host.includes(":") && !host.startsWith("[") && !host.endsWith("]")) return `[${host}]`;
820	    return host;
821	  };
822	  const vars: Record<string, string> = {
823	    PAPERCLIP_AGENT_ID: agent.id,
824	    PAPERCLIP_COMPANY_ID: agent.companyId,
825	  };
826	  const runtimeHost = resolveHostForUrl(
827	    process.env.PAPERCLIP_LISTEN_HOST ?? process.env.HOST ?? "localhost",
828	  );
829	  const runtimePort = process.env.PAPERCLIP_LISTEN_PORT ?? process.env.PORT ?? "3100";
830	  const apiUrl =
831	    process.env.PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL ??
832	    process.env.PAPERCLIP_API_URL ??
833	    `http://${runtimeHost}:${runtimePort}`;
834	  vars.PAPERCLIP_API_URL = apiUrl;
835	  return vars;
836	}

873	export function sanitizeInheritedPaperclipEnv(baseEnv: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
874	  const env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = { ...baseEnv };
875	  for (const key of Object.keys(env)) {
876	    if (!key.startsWith("PAPERCLIP_")) continue;
877	    if (key === "PAPERCLIP_RUNTIME_API_URL") continue;
878	    if (key === "PAPERCLIP_LISTEN_HOST") continue;
879	    if (key === "PAPERCLIP_LISTEN_PORT") continue;
880	    delete env[key];
881	  }
882	  return env;
883	}

885	export function defaultPathForPlatform() {
886	  if (process.platform === "win32") {
887	    return "C:\\Windows\\System32;C:\\Windows;C:\\Windows\\System32\\Wbem";
888	  }
889	  return "/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin";

892	function windowsPathExts(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string[] {
893	  return (env.PATHEXT ?? ".EXE;.CMD;.BAT;.COM").split(";").filter(Boolean);

896	async function pathExists(candidate: string) {
897	  try {
898	    await fs.access(candidate, process.platform === "win32" ? fsConstants.F_OK : fsConstants.X_OK);
899	    return true;
900	  } catch {
901	    return false;
902	  }
903	}

905	async function resolveCommandPath(command: string, cwd: string, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<string | null> {
906	  const hasPathSeparator = command.includes("/") || command.includes("\\");
907	  if (hasPathSeparator) {
908	    const absolute = path.isAbsolute(command) ? command : path.resolve(cwd, command);
909	    return (await pathExists(absolute)) ? absolute : null;
910	  }
911	
912	  const pathValue = env.PATH ?? env.Path ?? "";
913	  const delimiter = process.platform === "win32" ? ";" : ":";
914	  const dirs = pathValue.split(delimiter).filter(Boolean);
915	  const exts = process.platform === "win32" ? windowsPathExts(env) : [""];
916	  const hasExtension = process.platform === "win32" && path.extname(command).length > 0;
917	
918	  for (const dir of dirs) {
919	    const candidates =
920	      process.platform === "win32"
921	        ? hasExtension
922	          ? [path.join(dir, command)]
923	          : exts.map((ext) => path.join(dir, `${command}${ext}`))
924	        : [path.join(dir, command)];
925	    for (const candidate of candidates) {
926	      if (await pathExists(candidate)) return candidate;
927	    }
928	  }
929	
930	  return null;
931	}

933	export async function resolveCommandForLogs(
934	  command: string,
935	  cwd: string,
936	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
937	  options: {
938	    remoteExecution?: RemoteExecutionSpec | null;
939	  } = {},
940	): Promise<string> {
941	  const remote = options.remoteExecution ?? null;
942	  if (remote) {
943	    return `ssh://${remote.username}@${remote.host}:${remote.port}/${remote.remoteCwd} :: ${command}`;
944	  }
945	  return (await resolveCommandPath(command, cwd, env)) ?? command;
946	}
947	
948	function quoteForCmd(arg: string) {
949	  if (!arg.length) return '""';
950	  const escaped = arg.replace(/"/g, '""');
951	  return /[\s"&<>|^()]/.test(escaped) ? `"${escaped}"` : escaped;
952	}
953	
954	function resolveWindowsCmdShell(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string {
955	  const fallbackRoot = env.SystemRoot || process.env.SystemRoot || "C:\\Windows";
956	  return path.join(fallbackRoot, "System32", "cmd.exe");
957	}
958	
959	async function resolveSpawnTarget(
960	  command: string,
961	  args: string[],
962	  cwd: string,
963	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
964	  options: {
965	    remoteExecution?: RemoteExecutionSpec | null;
966	    remoteEnv?: Record<string, string> | null;
967	  } = {},
968	): Promise<SpawnTarget> {
969	  const remote = options.remoteExecution ?? null;
970	  if (remote) {
971	    const sshResolved = await resolveCommandPath("ssh", process.cwd(), env);
972	    if (!sshResolved) {
973	      throw new Error('Command not found in PATH: "ssh"');
974	    }
975	    const spawnTarget = await buildSshSpawnTarget({
976	      spec: remote,
977	      command,
978	      args,
979	      env: Object.fromEntries(
980	        Object.entries(options.remoteEnv ?? {}).filter((entry): entry is [string, string] => typeof entry[1] === "string"),
981	      ),
982	    });
983	    return {
984	      command: sshResolved,
985	      args: spawnTarget.args,
986	      cwd: process.cwd(),
987	      cleanup: spawnTarget.cleanup,
988	    };
989	  }
990	
991	  const resolved = await resolveCommandPath(command, cwd, env);
992	  const executable = resolved ?? command;
993	
994	  if (process.platform !== "win32") {
995	    return { command: executable, args };
996	  }
997	
998	  if (/\.(cmd|bat)$/i.test(executable)) {
999	    // Always use cmd.exe for .cmd/.bat wrappers. Some environments override
1000	    // ComSpec to PowerShell, which breaks cmd-specific flags like /d /s /c.
1001	    const shell = resolveWindowsCmdShell(env);
1002	    const commandLine = [quoteForCmd(executable), ...args.map(quoteForCmd)].join(" ");
1003	    return {
1004	      command: shell,
1005	      args: ["/d", "/s", "/c", commandLine],
1006	    };
1007	  }
1008	
1009	  return { command: executable, args };
1010	}

1012	export function ensurePathInEnv(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
1013	  if (typeof env.PATH === "string" && env.PATH.length > 0) return env;
1014	  if (typeof env.Path === "string" && env.Path.length > 0) return env;
1015	  return { ...env, PATH: defaultPathForPlatform() };
1016	}

1018	export async function ensureAbsoluteDirectory(
1019	  cwd: string,
1020	  opts: { createIfMissing?: boolean } = {},
1021	) {
1022	  if (!path.isAbsolute(cwd)) {
1023	    throw new Error(`Working directory must be an absolute path: "${cwd}"`);
1024	  }
1025	
1026	  const assertDirectory = async () => {
1027	    const stats = await fs.stat(cwd);
1028	    if (!stats.isDirectory()) {
1029	      throw new Error(`Working directory is not a directory: "${cwd}"`);
1030	    }
1031	  };
1032	
1033	  try {
1034	    await assertDirectory();
1035	    return;
1036	  } catch (err) {
1037	    const code = (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
1038	    if (!opts.createIfMissing || code !== "ENOENT") {
1039	      if (code === "ENOENT") {
1040	        throw new Error(`Working directory does not exist: "${cwd}"`);
1041	      }
1042	      throw err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err));
1043	    }
1044	  }
1045	
1046	  try {
1047	    await fs.mkdir(cwd, { recursive: true });
1048	    await assertDirectory();
1049	  } catch (err) {
1050	    const reason = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
1051	    throw new Error(`Could not create working directory "${cwd}": ${reason}`);
1052	  }
1053	}

1055	export async function resolvePaperclipSkillsDir(
1056	  moduleDir: string,
1057	  additionalCandidates: string[] = [],
1058	): Promise<string | null> {
1059	  const candidates = [
1060	    ...PAPERCLIP_SKILL_ROOT_RELATIVE_CANDIDATES.map((relativePath) => path.resolve(moduleDir, relativePath)),
1061	    ...additionalCandidates.map((candidate) => path.resolve(candidate)),
1062	  ];
1063	  const seenRoots = new Set<string>();
1064	
1065	  for (const root of candidates) {
1066	    if (seenRoots.has(root)) continue;
1067	    seenRoots.add(root);
1068	    const isDirectory = await fs.stat(root).then((stats) => stats.isDirectory()).catch(() => false);
1069	    if (isDirectory) return root;
1070	  }
1071	
1072	  return null;
1073	}

1075	async function readSkillRequired(skillDir: string): Promise<boolean> {
1076	  try {
1077	    const content = await fs.readFile(path.join(skillDir, "SKILL.md"), "utf8");
1078	    const normalized = content.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
1079	    if (!normalized.startsWith("---\n")) return true;
1080	    const closing = normalized.indexOf("\n---\n", 4);
1081	    if (closing < 0) return true;
1082	    const frontmatter = normalized.slice(4, closing);
1083	    return !/^\s*required\s*:\s*false\s*$/m.test(frontmatter);
1084	  } catch {
1085	    return true;
1086	  }
1087	}

1089	export async function listPaperclipSkillEntries(
1090	  moduleDir: string,

1103	        key: `paperclipai/paperclip/${entry.name}`,
1104	        runtimeName: entry.name,

1106	        required,
1107	        requiredReason: required
1108	          ? "Bundled Paperclip skills are always available for local adapters."
1109	          : null,
1110	      };
1111	    }));
1112	  } catch {

1117	export async function readInstalledSkillTargets(skillsHome: string): Promise<Map<string, InstalledSkillTarget>> {

1128	export function buildPersistentSkillSnapshot(
1129	  options: PersistentSkillSnapshotOptions,
1130	): AdapterSkillSnapshot {
1131	  const {
1132	    adapterType,
1133	    availableEntries,
1134	    desiredSkills,
1135	    installed,
1136	    skillsHome,
1137	    locationLabel,
1138	    installedDetail,
1139	    missingDetail,
1140	    externalConflictDetail,
1141	    externalDetail,
1142	  } = options;
1143	  const availableByKey = new Map(availableEntries.map((entry) => [entry.key, entry]));
1144	  const desiredSet = new Set(desiredSkills);
1145	  const entries: AdapterSkillEntry[] = [];
1146	  const warnings = [...(options.warnings ?? [])];
1147	
1148	  for (const available of availableEntries) {
1149	    const installedEntry = installed.get(available.runtimeName) ?? null;
1150	    const desired = desiredSet.has(available.key);
1151	    let state: AdapterSkillEntry["state"] = "available";
1152	    let managed = false;
1153	    let detail: string | null = null;
1154	
1155	    if (installedEntry?.targetPath === available.source) {
1156	      managed = true;
1157	      state = desired ? "installed" : "stale";
1158	      detail = installedDetail ?? null;
1159	    } else if (installedEntry) {
1160	      state = "external";
1161	      detail = desired ? externalConflictDetail : externalDetail;
1162	    } else if (desired) {
1163	      state = "missing";
1164	      detail = missingDetail;
1165	    }
1166	
1167	    entries.push({
1168	      key: available.key,
1169	      runtimeName: available.runtimeName,
1170	      desired,
1171	      managed,
1172	      state,
1173	      sourcePath: available.source,
1174	      targetPath: path.join(skillsHome, available.runtimeName),
1175	      detail,
1176	      required: Boolean(available.required),
1177	      requiredReason: available.requiredReason ?? null,
1178	      ...buildManagedSkillOrigin(available),
1179	    });
1180	  }
1181	
1182	  for (const desiredSkill of desiredSkills) {
1183	    if (availableByKey.has(desiredSkill)) continue;
1184	    warnings.push(`Desired skill "${desiredSkill}" is not available from the Paperclip skills directory.`);
1185	    entries.push({
1186	      key: desiredSkill,
1187	      runtimeName: null,
1188	      desired: true,
1189	      managed: true,
1190	      state: "missing",
1191	      sourcePath: null,
1192	      targetPath: null,
1193	      detail: "Paperclip cannot find this skill in the local runtime skills directory.",
1194	      origin: "external_unknown",
1195	      originLabel: "External or unavailable",
1196	      readOnly: false,
1197	    });
1198	  }
1199	
1200	  for (const [name, installedEntry] of installed.entries()) {
1201	    if (availableEntries.some((entry) => entry.runtimeName === name)) continue;
1202	    entries.push({
1203	      key: name,
1204	      runtimeName: name,
1205	      desired: false,
1206	      managed: false,
1207	      state: "external",
1208	      origin: "user_installed",
1209	      originLabel: "User-installed",
1210	      locationLabel: skillLocationLabel(locationLabel),
1211	      readOnly: true,
1212	      sourcePath: null,
1213	      targetPath: installedEntry.targetPath ?? path.join(skillsHome, name),
1214	      detail: externalDetail,
1215	    });
1216	  }
1217	
1218	  entries.sort((left, right) => left.key.localeCompare(right.key));
1219	
1220	  return {
1221	    adapterType,
1222	    supported: true,
1223	    mode: "persistent",
1224	    desiredSkills,
1225	    entries,
1226	    warnings,
1227	  };
1228	}

1230	function normalizeConfiguredPaperclipRuntimeSkills(value: unknown): PaperclipSkillEntry[] {
1231	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return [];
1232	  const out: PaperclipSkillEntry[] = [];
1233	  for (const rawEntry of value) {
1234	    const entry = parseObject(rawEntry);
1235	    const key = asString(entry.key, asString(entry.name, "")).trim();
1236	    const runtimeName = asString(entry.runtimeName, asString(entry.name, "")).trim();
1237	    const source = asString(entry.source, "").trim();
1238	    if (!key || !runtimeName || !source) continue;
1239	    out.push({
1240	      key,
1241	      runtimeName,
1242	      source,
1243	      required: asBoolean(entry.required, false),
1244	      requiredReason:
1245	        typeof entry.requiredReason === "string" && entry.requiredReason.trim().length > 0
1246	          ? entry.requiredReason.trim()
1247	          : null,
1248	    });
1249	  }
1250	  return out;
1251	}

1281	export function readPaperclipSkillSyncPreference(config: Record<string, unknown>): {
1282	  explicit: boolean;
1283	  desiredSkills: string[];
1284	} {
1285	  const raw = config.paperclipSkillSync;
1286	  if (typeof raw !== "object" || raw === null || Array.isArray(raw)) {
1287	    return { explicit: false, desiredSkills: [] };
1288	  }
1289	  const syncConfig = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
1290	  const desiredValues = syncConfig.desiredSkills;
1291	  const desired = Array.isArray(desiredValues)
1292	    ? desiredValues
1293	        .filter((value): value is string => typeof value === "string")
1294	        .map((value) => value.trim())
1295	        .filter(Boolean)
1296	    : [];
1297	  return {
1298	    explicit: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(raw, "desiredSkills"),
1299	    desiredSkills: Array.from(new Set(desired)),
1300	  };
1301	}
1302	
1303	function canonicalizeDesiredPaperclipSkillReference(
1304	  reference: string,
1305	  availableEntries: Array<{ key: string; runtimeName?: string | null }>,
1306	): string {
1307	  const normalizedReference = reference.trim().toLowerCase();
1308	  if (!normalizedReference) return "";
1309	
1310	  const exactKey = availableEntries.find((entry) => entry.key.trim().toLowerCase() === normalizedReference);
1311	  if (exactKey) return exactKey.key;
1312	
1313	  const byRuntimeName = availableEntries.filter((entry) =>
1314	    typeof entry.runtimeName === "string" && entry.runtimeName.trim().toLowerCase() === normalizedReference,
1315	  );
1316	  if (byRuntimeName.length === 1) return byRuntimeName[0]!.key;
1317	
1318	  const slugMatches = availableEntries.filter((entry) =>
1319	    entry.key.trim().toLowerCase().split("/").pop() === normalizedReference,
1320	  );
1321	  if (slugMatches.length === 1) return slugMatches[0]!.key;
1322	
1323	  return normalizedReference;
1324	}
1325	
1326	export function resolvePaperclipDesiredSkillNames(
1327	  config: Record<string, unknown>,
1328	  availableEntries: Array<{ key: string; runtimeName?: string | null; required?: boolean }>,
1329	): string[] {
1330	  const preference = readPaperclipSkillSyncPreference(config);
1331	  const requiredSkills = availableEntries
1332	    .filter((entry) => entry.required)
1333	    .map((entry) => entry.key);
1334	  if (!preference.explicit) {
1335	    return Array.from(new Set(requiredSkills));
1336	  }
1337	  const desiredSkills = preference.desiredSkills
1338	    .map((reference) => canonicalizeDesiredPaperclipSkillReference(reference, availableEntries))
1339	    .filter(Boolean);
1340	  return Array.from(new Set([...requiredSkills, ...desiredSkills]));
1341	}
1342	
1343	export function writePaperclipSkillSyncPreference(
1344	  config: Record<string, unknown>,
1345	  desiredSkills: string[],
1346	): Record<string, unknown> {
1347	  const next = { ...config };
1348	  const raw = next.paperclipSkillSync;
1349	  const current =
1350	    typeof raw === "object" && raw !== null && !Array.isArray(raw)
1351	      ? { ...(raw as Record<string, unknown>) }
1352	      : {};
1353	  current.desiredSkills = Array.from(
1354	    new Set(
1355	      desiredSkills
1356	        .map((value) => value.trim())
1357	        .filter(Boolean),
1358	    ),
1359	  );
1360	  next.paperclipSkillSync = current;
1361	  return next;
1362	}

1364	export async function ensurePaperclipSkillSymlink(
1365	  source: string,
1366	  target: string,
1367	  linkSkill: (source: string, target: string) => Promise<void> = (linkSource, linkTarget) =>
1368	    fs.symlink(linkSource, linkTarget),
1369	): Promise<"created" | "repaired" | "skipped"> {
1370	  const existing = await fs.lstat(target).catch(() => null);
1371	  if (!existing) {
1372	    await linkSkill(source, target);
1373	    return "created";
1374	  }
1375	
1376	  if (!existing.isSymbolicLink()) {
1377	    return "skipped";
1378	  }
1379	
1380	  const linkedPath = await fs.readlink(target).catch(() => null);
1381	  if (!linkedPath) return "skipped";
1382	
1383	  const resolvedLinkedPath = path.resolve(path.dirname(target), linkedPath);
1384	  if (resolvedLinkedPath === source) {
1385	    return "skipped";
1386	  }
1387	
1388	  const linkedPathExists = await fs.stat(resolvedLinkedPath).then(() => true).catch(() => false);
1389	  if (linkedPathExists) {
1390	    return "skipped";
1391	  }
1392	
1393	  await fs.unlink(target);
1394	  await linkSkill(source, target);
1395	  return "repaired";
1396	}

1398	export async function removeMaintainerOnlySkillSymlinks(
1399	  skillsHome: string,
1400	  allowedSkillNames: Iterable<string>,
1401	): Promise<string[]> {
1402	  const allowed = new Set(Array.from(allowedSkillNames));
1403	  try {
1404	    const entries = await fs.readdir(skillsHome, { withFileTypes: true });
1405	    const removed: string[] = [];
1406	    for (const entry of entries) {
1407	      if (allowed.has(entry.name)) continue;
1408	
1409	      const target = path.join(skillsHome, entry.name);
1410	      const existing = await fs.lstat(target).catch(() => null);
1411	      if (!existing?.isSymbolicLink()) continue;
1412	
1413	      const linkedPath = await fs.readlink(target).catch(() => null);
1414	      if (!linkedPath) continue;
1415	
1416	      const resolvedLinkedPath = path.isAbsolute(linkedPath)
1417	        ? linkedPath
1418	        : path.resolve(path.dirname(target), linkedPath);
1419	      if (
1420	        !isMaintainerOnlySkillTarget(linkedPath) &&
1421	        !isMaintainerOnlySkillTarget(resolvedLinkedPath)
1422	      ) {
1423	        continue;
1424	      }
1425	
1426	      await fs.unlink(target);
1427	      removed.push(entry.name);
1428	    }
1429	
1430	    return removed;
1431	  } catch {
1432	    return [];
1433	  }
1434	}

1436	export async function ensureCommandResolvable(
1437	  command: string,
1438	  cwd: string,
1439	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
1440	  options: {
1441	    remoteExecution?: RemoteExecutionSpec | null;
1442	  } = {},
1443	) {
1444	  if (options.remoteExecution) {
1445	    const resolvedSsh = await resolveCommandPath("ssh", process.cwd(), env);
1446	    if (resolvedSsh) return;
1447	    throw new Error('Command not found in PATH: "ssh"');
1448	  }
1449	  const resolved = await resolveCommandPath(command, cwd, env);
1450	  if (resolved) return;
1451	  if (command.includes("/") || command.includes("\\")) {
1452	    const absolute = path.isAbsolute(command) ? command : path.resolve(cwd, command);
1453	    throw new Error(`Command is not executable: "${command}" (resolved: "${absolute}")`);
1454	  }
1455	  throw new Error(`Command not found in PATH: "${command}"`);
1456	}

1458	export async function runChildProcess(
1459	  runId: string,
1460	  command: string,
1461	  args: string[],
1462	  opts: {
1463	    cwd: string;
1464	    env: Record<string, string>;
1465	    timeoutSec: number;
1466	    graceSec: number;
1467	    onLog: (stream: "stdout" | "stderr", chunk: string) => Promise<void>;
1468	    onLogError?: (err: unknown, runId: string, message: string) => void;
1469	    onSpawn?: (meta: { pid: number; processGroupId: number | null; startedAt: string }) => Promise<void>;
1470	    terminalResultCleanup?: TerminalResultCleanupOptions;
1471	    stdin?: string;
1472	    remoteExecution?: RemoteExecutionSpec | null;
1473	  },
1474	): Promise<RunProcessResult> {
1475	  const onLogError = opts.onLogError ?? ((err, id, msg) => console.warn({ err, runId: id }, msg));
1476	  return new Promise<RunProcessResult>((resolve, reject) => {
1477	    const rawMerged: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
1478	      ...sanitizeInheritedPaperclipEnv(process.env),
1479	      ...opts.env,
1480	    };
1481	
1482	    // Strip Claude Code nesting-guard env vars so spawned `claude` processes
1483	    // don't refuse to start with "cannot be launched inside another session".
1484	    // These vars leak in when the Paperclip server itself is started from
1485	    // within a Claude Code session (e.g. `npx paperclipai run` in a terminal
1486	    // owned by Claude Code) or when cron inherits a contaminated shell env.
1487	    const CLAUDE_CODE_NESTING_VARS = [
1488	      "CLAUDECODE",
1489	      "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT",
1490	      "CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION",
1491	      "CLAUDE_CODE_PARENT_SESSION",
1492	    ] as const;
1493	    for (const key of CLAUDE_CODE_NESTING_VARS) {
1494	      delete rawMerged[key];
1495	    }
1496	
1497	    const mergedEnv = ensurePathInEnv(rawMerged);
1498	    void resolveSpawnTarget(command, args, opts.cwd, mergedEnv, {
1499	      remoteExecution: opts.remoteExecution ?? null,
1500	      remoteEnv: opts.remoteExecution ? opts.env : null,
1501	    })
1502	      .then((target) => {
1503	        const child = spawn(target.command, target.args, {
1504	          cwd: target.cwd ?? opts.cwd,
1505	          env: mergedEnv,
1506	          detached: process.platform !== "win32",
1507	          shell: false,
1508	          stdio: [opts.stdin != null ? "pipe" : "ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
1509	        }) as ChildProcessWithEvents;
1510	        const startedAt = new Date().toISOString();
1511	        const processGroupId = resolveProcessGroupId(child);
1512	
1513	        const spawnPersistPromise =
1514	          typeof child.pid === "number" && child.pid > 0 && opts.onSpawn
1515	            ? opts.onSpawn({ pid: child.pid, processGroupId, startedAt }).catch((err) => {
1516	              onLogError(err, runId, "failed to record child process metadata");
1517	            })
1518	            : Promise.resolve();
1519	
1520	        runningProcesses.set(runId, { child, graceSec: opts.graceSec, processGroupId });
1521	
1522	        let timedOut = false;
1523	        let stdout = "";
1524	        let stderr = "";
1525	        let logChain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
1526	        let terminalResultSeen = false;
1527	        let terminalCleanupStarted = false;
1528	        let terminalCleanupTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
1529	        let terminalCleanupKillTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
1530	        let terminalResultStdoutScanOffset = 0;
1531	        let terminalResultStderrScanOffset = 0;
1532	
1533	        const clearTerminalCleanupTimers = () => {
1534	          if (terminalCleanupTimer) clearTimeout(terminalCleanupTimer);
1535	          if (terminalCleanupKillTimer) clearTimeout(terminalCleanupKillTimer);
1536	          terminalCleanupTimer = null;
1537	          terminalCleanupKillTimer = null;
1538	        };
1539	
1540	        const maybeArmTerminalResultCleanup = () => {
1541	          const terminalCleanup = opts.terminalResultCleanup;
1542	          if (!terminalCleanup || terminalCleanupStarted || timedOut) return;
1543	          if (!terminalResultSeen) {
1544	            const stdoutStart = Math.max(0, terminalResultStdoutScanOffset - TERMINAL_RESULT_SCAN_OVERLAP_CHARS);
1545	            const stderrStart = Math.max(0, terminalResultStderrScanOffset - TERMINAL_RESULT_SCAN_OVERLAP_CHARS);
1546	            const scanOutput = {
1547	              stdout: stdout.slice(stdoutStart),
1548	              stderr: stderr.slice(stderrStart),
1549	            };
1550	            terminalResultStdoutScanOffset = stdout.length;
1551	            terminalResultStderrScanOffset = stderr.length;
1552	            if (scanOutput.stdout.length === 0 && scanOutput.stderr.length === 0) return;
1553	            try {
1554	              terminalResultSeen = terminalCleanup.hasTerminalResult(scanOutput);
1555	            } catch (err) {
1556	              onLogError(err, runId, "failed to inspect terminal adapter output");
1557	            }
1558	          }
1559	          if (!terminalResultSeen) return;
1560	
1561	          if (terminalCleanupTimer) return;
1562	          const graceMs = Math.max(0, terminalCleanup.graceMs ?? 5_000);
1563	          terminalCleanupTimer = setTimeout(() => {
1564	            terminalCleanupTimer = null;
1565	            if (terminalCleanupStarted || timedOut) return;
1566	            terminalCleanupStarted = true;
1567	            signalRunningProcess({ child, processGroupId }, "SIGTERM");
1568	            terminalCleanupKillTimer = setTimeout(() => {
1569	              terminalCleanupKillTimer = null;
1570	              signalRunningProcess({ child, processGroupId }, "SIGKILL");
1571	            }, Math.max(1, opts.graceSec) * 1000);
1572	          }, graceMs);
1573	        };
1574	
1575	        const timeout =
1576	          opts.timeoutSec > 0
1577	            ? setTimeout(() => {
1578	                timedOut = true;
1579	                clearTerminalCleanupTimers();
1580	                signalRunningProcess({ child, processGroupId }, "SIGTERM");
1581	                setTimeout(() => {
1582	                  signalRunningProcess({ child, processGroupId }, "SIGKILL");
1583	                }, Math.max(1, opts.graceSec) * 1000);
1584	              }, opts.timeoutSec * 1000)
1585	            : null;
1586	
1587	        child.stdout?.on("data", (chunk: unknown) => {
1588	          const readable = child.stdout;
1589	          if (!readable) return;
1590	          readable.pause();
1591	          const text = String(chunk);
1592	          stdout = appendWithCap(stdout, text);
1593	          maybeArmTerminalResultCleanup();
1594	          logChain = logChain
1595	            .then(() => opts.onLog("stdout", text))
1596	            .catch((err) => onLogError(err, runId, "failed to append stdout log chunk"))
1597	            .finally(() => {
1598	              maybeArmTerminalResultCleanup();
1599	              resumeReadable(readable);
1600	            });
1601	        });
1602	
1603	        child.stderr?.on("data", (chunk: unknown) => {
1604	          const readable = child.stderr;
1605	          if (!readable) return;
1606	          readable.pause();
1607	          const text = String(chunk);
1608	          stderr = appendWithCap(stderr, text);
1609	          maybeArmTerminalResultCleanup();
1610	          logChain = logChain
1611	            .then(() => opts.onLog("stderr", text))
1612	            .catch((err) => onLogError(err, runId, "failed to append stderr log chunk"))
1613	            .finally(() => {
1614	              maybeArmTerminalResultCleanup();
1615	              resumeReadable(readable);
1616	            });
1617	        });
1618	
1619	        const stdin = child.stdin;
1620	        if (opts.stdin != null && stdin) {
1621	          void spawnPersistPromise.finally(() => {
1622	            if (child.killed || stdin.destroyed) return;
1623	            stdin.write(opts.stdin as string);
1624	            stdin.end();
1625	          });
1626	        }
1627	
1628	        child.on("error", (err: Error) => {
1629	          if (timeout) clearTimeout(timeout);
1630	          clearTerminalCleanupTimers();
1631	          runningProcesses.delete(runId);
1632	          void target.cleanup?.();
1633	          const errno = (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
1634	          const pathValue = mergedEnv.PATH ?? mergedEnv.Path ?? "";
1635	          const msg =
1636	            errno === "ENOENT"
1637	              ? `Failed to start command "${command}" in "${opts.cwd}". Verify adapter command, working directory, and PATH (${pathValue}).`
1638	              : `Failed to start command "${command}" in "${opts.cwd}": ${err.message}`;
1639	          reject(new Error(msg));
1640	        });
1641	
1642	        child.on("exit", () => {
1643	          maybeArmTerminalResultCleanup();
1644	        });
1645	
1646	        child.on("close", (code: number | null, signal: NodeJS.Signals | null) => {
1647	          if (timeout) clearTimeout(timeout);
1648	          clearTerminalCleanupTimers();
1649	          runningProcesses.delete(runId);
1650	          void logChain.finally(() => {
1651	            void Promise.resolve()
1652	              .then(() => target.cleanup?.())
1653	              .finally(() => {
1654	              resolve({
1655	                exitCode: code,
1656	                signal,
1657	                timedOut,
1658	                stdout,
1659	                stderr,
1660	                pid: child.pid ?? null,
1661	                startedAt,
1662	              });
1663	              });
1664	          });
1665	        });
```

```text
## What was created and edited

### Files created

**`server/src/http/types.ts`** (new, 35 lines)

Defines the three core transport-agnostic types:

- `ActorContext` (line 5) — the normalized subset of the Express actor shape, only for authenticated actors (`"board" | "agent"`). The `"none"` case from `express.d.ts` is represented as `null` on `RequestCtx.actor` instead.
- `RequestCtx` (line 13) — the minimal normalized request interface. `json<T>()`, `text()`, `param()`, `query()` are all methods so callers never touch transport primitives directly. `db` and `storage` are always present here; the optional-db case in health is handled in the route layer.
- `Handler` (line 28) — `(ctx: RequestCtx) => Promise<Response>`. Uses the Web API `Response` type so handlers are portable to Hono/Workers.
- `RouteDefinition` (line 30) — carry type for future route registration tables.

**`server/src/http/express-adapter.ts`** (new, 113 lines)

`expressHandler(handler, deps)` at line 23 does five bridging jobs:

1. URL construction (line 29-31): builds `new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl)` from `req.hostname` + `req.protocol`.
2. Actor normalization (line 34-43): maps `req.actor.type === "none"` → `null`; copies only the four fields defined in `ActorContext`.
3. Header bridging (line 47-57): iterates `req.headers` (already lowercased by Node's HTTP parser) into a Web `Headers` object; handles `string[]` multi-value headers via `append`.
4. Body bridging (line 66-72): `json()` returns `req.body` directly (already parsed by `express.json()`); `text()` JSON-serialises if body is not already a string. No re-parsing.
5. Response forwarding (line 98-108): copies `response.status`, iterates `response.headers` (skipping `transfer-encoding` and `content-length` which Express manages), then sends via `res.send()`. Errors fall through to `next(err)`.

**`server/src/http/index.ts`** (new, 2 lines)

Barrel re-export of all four types and `expressHandler`.
```

## Context

- `server/src/app.ts:108` — `createApp(db, opts)` returns an Express app
- There are 20+ route files in `server/src/routes/` each exporting an Express Router
- `server/src/middleware/auth.ts` — sets up actor context on `req`
- Workers cannot run Express, but Hono can run on both Node and Workers

## What to implement

### 1. Transport-agnostic handler type — `server/src/http/types.ts`

```ts
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";

/** Normalized actor from auth middleware */
export interface ActorContext {
  type: "board" | "agent";
  userId?: string;
  agentId?: string;
  companyId?: string;
}

/** Minimal normalized request passed to every handler */
export interface RequestCtx {
  method: string;
  url: URL;
  headers: Headers;
  json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T>;
  text(): Promise<string>;
  /** Path param: e.g. ctx.param("companyId") */
  param(name: string): string | undefined;
  /** Query param */
  query(name: string): string | undefined;
  actor: ActorContext | null;
  db: Db;
  storage: StorageService;
}

export type Handler = (ctx: RequestCtx) => Promise<Response>;

export interface RouteDefinition {
  method: "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";
  path: string;  // Express-style: /api/companies/:companyId
  handler: Handler;
}
```

### 2. Express adapter — `server/src/http/express-adapter.ts`

Write a function `expressHandler(handler: Handler, deps: { db: Db; storage: StorageService }): express.RequestHandler` that:
- Builds a `RequestCtx` from the Express `req`
- Populates `actor` from `req.actor` (look at how actorMiddleware sets it — read `server/src/middleware/auth.ts`)
- Calls `handler(ctx)`
- Sends the `Response` back via Express `res`
- Handles errors (500 on throw)

You'll need to bridge Node's `req.body` (already parsed by `express.json()`) into the `json()` method, and `req.params` / `req.query` into `param()` / `query()`.

### 3. Migrate the health route as a reference implementation

Read `server/src/routes/health.ts`. Convert its handlers to use the `Handler` type, then re-export an Express router from `healthRoutes` that wraps them via `expressHandler`. The existing `app.ts` import and usage of `healthRoutes` must not change.

Pattern:
```ts
// server/src/routes/health.ts
import { expressHandler } from "../http/express-adapter.js";
import type { Handler } from "../http/types.js";
import { Router } from "express";

const getHealth: Handler = async (ctx) => {
  return Response.json({ status: "ok" });
};

export function healthRoutes(deps) {
  const router = Router();
  router.get("/api/health", expressHandler(getHealth, deps));
  return router;
}
```

### 4. Export from `server/src/http/index.ts`

Export `Handler`, `RequestCtx`, `ActorContext`, `RouteDefinition`, `expressHandler`.

## Rules

- Read every file before editing it.
- Do not change how `app.ts` imports or uses `healthRoutes` — it must still work.
- Do not remove or change any existing behaviour — only add the new abstraction layer.
- Keep types strict — no `any` unless the existing code uses it.
- Read `server/src/middleware/auth.ts` to understand how actor is attached to Express req.

Report what you created and what you edited, with file:line references for every key change. This is the pattern all future route migrations will follow.

```text
8	import { logger } from "../middleware/logger.js";

12	function shouldExposeFullHealthDetails(
13	  actorType: "none" | "board" | "agent" | null | undefined,
14	  deploymentMode: DeploymentMode,
15	) {
16	  if (deploymentMode !== "authenticated") return true;
17	  return actorType === "board" || actorType === "agent";
18	}
19	
20	function hasDevServerStatusToken(providedToken: string | undefined) {
21	  const expectedToken = process.env.PAPERCLIP_DEV_SERVER_STATUS_TOKEN?.trim();
22	  const token = providedToken?.trim();
23	  if (!expectedToken || !token) return false;
24	
25	  const expected = Buffer.from(expectedToken);
26	  const provided = Buffer.from(token);
27	  if (expected.length !== provided.length) return false;
28	  return timingSafeEqual(expected, provided);
29	}
30	
31	export function healthRoutes(
32	  db?: Db,
33	  opts: {
34	    deploymentMode: DeploymentMode;
35	    deploymentExposure: DeploymentExposure;
36	    authReady: boolean;
37	    companyDeletionEnabled: boolean;
38	  } = {
39	    deploymentMode: "local_trusted",
40	    deploymentExposure: "private",
41	    authReady: true,
42	    companyDeletionEnabled: true,
43	  },
44	) {
45	  const router = Router();
46	
47	  router.get("/", async (req, res) => {
48	    const actorType = "actor" in req ? req.actor?.type : null;
49	    const exposeFullDetails = shouldExposeFullHealthDetails(
50	      actorType,
51	      opts.deploymentMode,
52	    );
53	    const exposeDevServerDetails =
54	      exposeFullDetails || hasDevServerStatusToken(req.get("x-paperclip-dev-server-status-token"));
55	
56	    if (!db) {
57	      res.json(
58	        exposeFullDetails
59	          ? { status: "ok", version: serverVersion }
60	          : { status: "ok", deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode },
61	      );
62	      return;
63	    }
64	
65	    try {
66	      await db.execute(sql`SELECT 1`);
67	    } catch (error) {
68	      logger.warn({ err: error }, "Health check database probe failed");
69	      res.status(503).json({
70	        status: "unhealthy",
71	        version: serverVersion,
72	        error: "database_unreachable"
73	      });
74	      return;
75	    }
76	
77	    let bootstrapStatus: "ready" | "bootstrap_pending" = "ready";
78	    let bootstrapInviteActive = false;
79	    if (opts.deploymentMode === "authenticated") {
80	      const roleCount = await db
81	        .select({ count: count() })
82	        .from(instanceUserRoles)
83	        .where(sql`${instanceUserRoles.role} = 'instance_admin'`)
84	        .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));
85	      bootstrapStatus = roleCount > 0 ? "ready" : "bootstrap_pending";
86	
87	      if (bootstrapStatus === "bootstrap_pending") {
88	        const now = new Date();
89	        const inviteCount = await db
90	          .select({ count: count() })
91	          .from(invites)
92	          .where(
93	            and(
94	              eq(invites.inviteType, "bootstrap_ceo"),
95	              isNull(invites.revokedAt),
96	              isNull(invites.acceptedAt),
97	              gt(invites.expiresAt, now),
98	            ),
99	          )
100	          .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));
101	        bootstrapInviteActive = inviteCount > 0;
102	      }
103	    }
104	
105	    const persistedDevServerStatus = readPersistedDevServerStatus();
106	    let devServer: ReturnType<typeof toDevServerHealthStatus> | undefined;
107	    if (exposeDevServerDetails && persistedDevServerStatus && typeof (db as { select?: unknown }).select === "function") {
108	      const instanceSettings = instanceSettingsService(db);
109	      const experimentalSettings = await instanceSettings.getExperimental();
110	      const activeRunCount = await db
111	        .select({ count: count() })
112	        .from(heartbeatRuns)
113	        .where(inArray(heartbeatRuns.status, ["queued", "running"]))
114	        .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));
115	
116	      devServer = toDevServerHealthStatus(persistedDevServerStatus, {
117	        autoRestartEnabled: experimentalSettings.autoRestartDevServerWhenIdle ?? false,
118	        activeRunCount,
119	      });
120	    }
121	
122	    if (!exposeFullDetails) {
123	      res.json({
124	        status: "ok",
125	        deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode,
126	        bootstrapStatus,
127	        bootstrapInviteActive,
128	        ...(devServer ? { devServer } : {}),
129	      });
130	      return;
131	    }
132	
133	    res.json({
134	      status: "ok",
135	      version: serverVersion,
136	      deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode,
137	      deploymentExposure: opts.deploymentExposure,
138	      authReady: opts.authReady,
139	      bootstrapStatus,
140	      bootstrapInviteActive,
141	      features: {
142	        companyDeletionEnabled: opts.companyDeletionEnabled,
143	      },
144	      ...(devServer ? { devServer } : {}),
145	    });
146	  });
147	
148	  return router;
149	}
```

```typescript
import { logger } from "../middleware/logger.js";
import type { Scheduler, ScheduledTask } from "./types.js";

export function createNodeScheduler(): Scheduler {
  return {
    every(name: string, intervalMs: number, fn: () => Promise<void>): ScheduledTask {
      const handle = setInterval(() => {
        void fn().catch((err) => {
          logger.error({ err, schedulerTask: name }, "scheduled task failed");
        });
      }, intervalMs);
      return {
        cancel: () => clearInterval(handle),
      };
    },
  };
}
```

```typescript
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";

/** Normalized actor from auth middleware — only set when authenticated (not "none"). */
export interface ActorContext {
  type: "board" | "agent";
  userId?: string;
  agentId?: string;
  companyId?: string;
}

/** Minimal normalized request passed to every handler. */
export interface RequestCtx {
  method: string;
  url: URL;
  headers: Headers;
  json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T>;
  text(): Promise<string>;
  /** Path param: e.g. ctx.param("companyId") */
  param(name: string): string | undefined;
  /** Query param */
  query(name: string): string | undefined;
  actor: ActorContext | null;
  db: Db;
  storage: StorageService;
}

export type Handler = (ctx: RequestCtx) => Promise<Response>;

export interface RouteDefinition {
  method: "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";
  /** Express-style path, e.g. /api/companies/:companyId */
  path: string;
  handler: Handler;
}
```

Now create the Express adapter. The key bridging work:
- `req.body` (already parsed JSON) is exposed via `json()` without re-parsing
- `req.params` / `req.query` are bridged to `param()` / `query()`
- `req.actor` from the Express type augmentation is mapped: if type is `"none"`, actor becomes `null`
- The Web `Response` returned by the handler is unwound back into Express `res`

```typescript
import type { RequestHandler } from "express";
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";
import type { ActorContext, Handler, RequestCtx } from "./types.js";

export interface AdapterDeps {
  db: Db;
  storage: StorageService;
}

/**
 * Wraps a transport-agnostic {@link Handler} as an Express {@link RequestHandler}.
 *
 * Bridging notes:
 * - `req.body` is already parsed by express.json(); json() returns it directly
 *   so the raw body is never re-parsed.
 * - Path params come from `req.params`, query params from `req.query`.
 * - `req.actor.type === "none"` is normalised to `null` so handlers can do a
 *   simple null-check rather than inspecting the string.
 * - The Web API `Response` returned by the handler is forwarded to Express `res`
 *   by copying status, headers, and body.
 */
export function expressHandler(handler: Handler, deps: AdapterDeps): RequestHandler {
  return async (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      // Build the base URL from the incoming request. Express provides
      // req.hostname and req.originalUrl which together give us a fully-formed
      // URL object without needing the raw Host header gymnastics.
      const protocol = (req as { protocol?: string }).protocol ?? "http";
      const baseUrl = `${protocol}://${req.hostname}`;
      const url = new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl);

      // Translate the Express actor (which may be "none") to ActorContext | null.
      const expressActor = req.actor;
      let actor: ActorContext | null = null;
      if (expressActor && expressActor.type !== "none") {
        actor = {
          type: expressActor.type,
          userId: expressActor.userId,
          agentId: expressActor.agentId,
          companyId: expressActor.companyId,
        };
      }

      // Build the Web-API-compatible Headers object from Express's incoming
      // headers map. Express lowercases all header names, so this is safe.
      const headers = new Headers();
      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {
        if (value === undefined) continue;
        if (Array.isArray(value)) {
          for (const v of value) headers.append(name, v);
        } else {
          headers.set(name, value);
        }
      }

      const ctx: RequestCtx = {
        method: req.method,
        url,
        headers,

        // Body is already parsed by express.json() — just return the cached
        // object rather than re-serialising/re-parsing it.
        json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T> {
          return Promise.resolve(req.body as T);
        },
        text(): Promise<string> {
          if (typeof req.body === "string") return Promise.resolve(req.body);
          return Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(req.body));
        },

        param(name: string): string | undefined {
          const value = req.params[name];
          return value === undefined ? undefined : String(value);
        },
        query(name: string): string | undefined {
          const value = req.query[name];
          if (value === undefined) return undefined;
          // Express query values can be string | ParsedQs | string[] | ParsedQs[]
          // We only surface the first scalar string.
          if (typeof value === "string") return value;
          if (Array.isArray(value)) {
            const first = value[0];
            return typeof first === "string" ? first : undefined;
          }
          return undefined;
        },

        actor,
        db: deps.db,
        storage: deps.storage,
      };

      const response = await handler(ctx);

      res.status(response.status);

      // Forward response headers (skip ones Express manages itself).
      response.headers.forEach((value, name) => {
        const lower = name.toLowerCase();
        if (lower === "transfer-encoding" || lower === "content-length") return;
        res.setHeader(name, value);
      });

      const body = await response.text();
      res.send(body);
    } catch (err) {
      next(err);
    }
  };
}

```

```typescript
import { runChildProcess, runningProcesses } from "./server-utils.js";
import type { CommandExecutor, CommandExecutorInput } from "./executor.js";
import type { RunProcessResult } from "./server-utils.js";

export function createLocalCommandExecutor(): CommandExecutor {
  return {
    async run(input: CommandExecutorInput): Promise<RunProcessResult> {
      return runChildProcess(input.runId, input.command, input.args, {
        cwd: input.cwd,
        env: input.env,
        timeoutSec: input.timeoutSec,
        graceSec: input.graceSec,
        onLog: input.onLog,
      });
    },

    async cancel(runId: string): Promise<void> {
      runningProcesses.delete(runId);
    },
  };
}
```

```text
## Key design decisions and notes

**No Node imports in any Worker file.** All Worker-side files use Web APIs only. `node:stream`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs` never appear in `src/`.

**Local type copies instead of cross-runtime imports.** `CommandExecutorInput`, `RunProcessResult`, `RequestCtx`, `Handler`, `RouteDefinition`, `Scheduler` are all duplicated locally with `// TODO: extract to shared package` comments. This is explicitly called out in the plan (PRs #4/#5/#6 upstream).

**`boot.ts` import path.** The `registerStorageProvider` import uses the path `../../../server/src/storage/provider-registry.js`. Wrangler (esbuild) bundles this at deploy time. The server file has no Node-only imports at the top level, only type imports from `@paperclipai/shared`, so it is safe to bundle.

**`hyperdrive.ts` schema path.** Uses `../../../db/src/schema/index.js` rather than `@paperclipai/db/src/schema/index.js` because the package's `./*` export map resolves to `./src/*.ts` (not `./src/*/index.ts`), making directory index imports ambiguous under strict bundler resolution.

**`SchedulerDO` handler URL approach.** Jobs register a `handlerUrl` that the DO POSTs to when the alarm fires. This matches how Cloudflare Workflows and Queues work — there is no persistent closure across invocations. The `cf-scheduler.ts` ignores the `fn` callback and requires callers to also pass a `handlerUrl` (an extension to the upstream `Scheduler` interface contract, noted with a TODO).
```

### `src/scheduler/cf-scheduler.ts`
Implements the `Scheduler` interface (from the seam being added in `server/src/scheduler/types.ts` — define a local copy of the interface here since it may not be importable from the Worker bundle):

```ts
export interface ScheduledTask { cancel(): void; }
export interface Scheduler {
  every(name: string, intervalMs: number, fn: () => Promise<void>): ScheduledTask;
}

export function createCfScheduler(schedulerDoStub: DurableObjectStub): Scheduler {
  return {
    every(name, intervalMs, _fn): ScheduledTask {
      // Register with SchedulerDO — fire the DO's /register endpoint
      // fn is NOT called here; on CF, the DO alarm calls a Worker endpoint instead
      void schedulerDoStub.fetch("http://internal/register", {
        method: "POST",
        body: JSON.stringify({ name, intervalMs }),
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      });
      return {
        cancel() {
          void schedulerDoStub.fetch("http://internal/cancel", {
            method: "POST",
            body: JSON.stringify({ name }),
            headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
          });
        },
      };
    },
  };
}
```

### `src/runtime/task-do.ts`
Per-task Durable Object. Holds task state in DO storage, manages WebSocket connections using the Hibernation API.

```ts
export class TaskDO implements DurableObject {
  private readonly state: DurableObjectState;
  
  constructor(state: DurableObjectState, env: Env) {
    this.state = state;
  }
  
  async fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    if (url.pathname === "/ws") {
      // Upgrade to WebSocket using CF hibernation API
      const pair = new WebSocketPair();
      this.state.acceptWebSocket(pair[1]);
      return new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket: pair[0] });
    }
    if (request.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/state") {
      const taskState = await this.state.storage.get("taskState");
      return Response.json(taskState ?? null);
    }
    if (request.method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/state") {
      const body = await request.json();
      await this.state.storage.put("taskState", body);
      // Broadcast to hibernated websockets
      for (const ws of this.state.getWebSockets()) {
        ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "state_updated", data: body }));
      }
      return Response.json({ ok: true });
    }
    return new Response("Not Found", { status: 404 });
  }
  
  webSocketMessage(ws: WebSocket, message: string | ArrayBuffer): void {
    // Handle incoming WS messages from UI (e.g. user comments, cancellation)
  }
  
  webSocketClose(ws: WebSocket): void {
    // Cleanup — WS closed by client
  }
}
```

### `src/runtime/agent-run-do.ts`
Per-agent-run DO. Tracks run state (status, logs, current step). Similar structure to TaskDO but without WS by default — runs communicate via fetch calls from Workflows.

### `src/runtime/workflows/heartbeat.ts`

```ts
import { WorkflowEntrypoint, type WorkflowStep, type WorkflowEvent } from "cloudflare:workers";

interface HeartbeatParams {
  agentId: string;
  companyId: string;
  runId: string;
}

export class HeartbeatWorkflow extends WorkflowEntrypoint<Env, HeartbeatParams> {
  async run(event: WorkflowEvent<HeartbeatParams>, step: WorkflowStep): Promise<void> {
    const { agentId, companyId, runId } = event.payload;
    
    // Step 1: Mark run as started
    await step.do("mark-running", async () => {
      // call internal API to update run status
    });
    
    // Step 2: Execute the heartbeat (LLM call etc) — delegate to sandbox bridge
    const result = await step.do("execute", { timeout: "5 minutes", retries: { limit: 2, delay: "5 seconds" } }, async () => {
      // call sandbox bridge or internal executor
      return { status: "ok" };
    });
    
    // Step 3: Record result
    await step.do("record-result", async () => {
      // call internal API to record result
    });
  }
}
```

### `src/adapter-executor/sandbox-bridge.ts`
Calls the existing sandbox bridge HTTP API (which is already running — look at packages/adapter-utils/src/sandbox-callback-bridge.ts and sandbox-managed-runtime.ts to understand the protocol). For now, implement as an HTTP call to a configurable `SANDBOX_BRIDGE_URL` env var.

```ts
export interface SandboxBridgeExecutorConfig {
  bridgeUrl: string;
  apiKey?: string;
}

export function createSandboxBridgeExecutor(config: SandboxBridgeExecutorConfig) {
  return {
    async run(input: CommandExecutorInput): Promise<RunProcessResult> {
      const resp = await fetch(`${config.bridgeUrl}/execute`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", ...(config.apiKey ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}` } : {}) },
        body: JSON.stringify(input),
      });
      if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`Sandbox bridge error: ${resp.status}`);
      return resp.json() as Promise<RunProcessResult>;
    },
    async cancel(runId: string): Promise<void> {
      await fetch(`${config.bridgeUrl}/cancel/${runId}`, { method: "POST" });
    },
  };
}
```

Use a local definition of `CommandExecutorInput` and `RunProcessResult` (copy the shapes from `packages/adapter-utils/src/server-utils.ts`) since importing Node modules in Workers will fail.

### `src/http/hono-adapter.ts`
Adapts the `Handler` type (from `server/src/http/types.ts`) to Hono. Since you can't import from `server/src/` in the Worker bundle, define a local copy of the interface types needed:

```ts
import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { Handler, RouteDefinition } from "../../server/src/http/types.js";
// ^ If this import path is too complex for bundling, define local copies:

export function mountRoutes(app: Hono, routes: RouteDefinition[], deps: { db: any; storage: any }): void {
  for (const route of routes) {
    const method = route.method.toLowerCase() as "get" | "post" | "put" | "patch" | "delete";
    app[method](route.path, async (c) => {
      const ctx: RequestCtx = {
        method: c.req.method,
        url: new URL(c.req.url),
        headers: new Headers(c.req.raw.headers),
        json: () => c.req.json(),
        text: () => c.req.text(),
        param: (name) => c.req.param(name),
        query: (name) => c.req.query(name),
        actor: null, // populated by auth middleware
        db: deps.db,
        storage: deps.storage,
      };
      return route.handler(ctx);
    });
  }
}
```

```ts
});
```

### `src/worker/mcp-sse.ts`
Worker that exposes the MCP server over SSE (Server-Sent Events):

```ts
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    if (request.method === "GET" && new URL(request.url).pathname === "/mcp") {
      const { readable, writable } = new TransformStream();
      const writer = writable.getWriter();
      // SSE handshake
      return new Response(readable, {
        headers: {
          "Content-Type": "text/event-stream",
          "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
          Connection: "keep-alive",
        },
      });
    }
    return new Response("Not Found", { status: 404 });
  },
};
```
