import { timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
import { Router } from "express";
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
import { and, count, eq, gt, inArray, isNull, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { heartbeatRuns, instanceUserRoles, invites } from "@paperclipai/db";
import type { DeploymentExposure, DeploymentMode } from "@paperclipai/shared";
import { readPersistedDevServerStatus, toDevServerHealthStatus } from "../dev-server-status.js";
import { logger } from "../middleware/logger.js";
import { instanceSettingsService } from "../services/instance-settings.js";
import { serverVersion } from "../version.js";
import { expressHandler } from "../http/express-adapter.js";
import type { Handler } from "../http/types.js";
import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";

function shouldExposeFullHealthDetails(
  actorType: "none" | "board" | "agent" | null | undefined,
  deploymentMode: DeploymentMode,
) {
  if (deploymentMode !== "authenticated") return true;
  return actorType === "board" || actorType === "agent";
}

function hasDevServerStatusToken(providedToken: string | undefined) {
  const expectedToken = process.env.PAPERCLIP_DEV_SERVER_STATUS_TOKEN?.trim();
  const token = providedToken?.trim();
  if (!expectedToken || !token) return false;

  const expected = Buffer.from(expectedToken);
  const provided = Buffer.from(token);
  if (expected.length !== provided.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(expected, provided);
}

/**
 * Builds the health-check {@link Handler} closed over the optional db and
 * deployment options. Using a factory lets us avoid threading `db` through
 * the adapter deps when it is genuinely optional for this endpoint.
 */
function buildHealthHandler(
  db: Db | undefined,
  opts: {
    deploymentMode: DeploymentMode;
    deploymentExposure: DeploymentExposure;
    authReady: boolean;
    companyDeletionEnabled: boolean;
  },
): Handler {
  return async (ctx) => {
    // ctx.actor is null when unauthenticated; map back to the legacy shape.
    const actorType = ctx.actor?.type ?? null;
    const exposeFullDetails = shouldExposeFullHealthDetails(actorType, opts.deploymentMode);
    const exposeDevServerDetails =
      exposeFullDetails ||
      hasDevServerStatusToken(ctx.headers.get("x-paperclip-dev-server-status-token") ?? undefined);

    if (!db) {
      return Response.json(
        exposeFullDetails
          ? { status: "ok", version: serverVersion }
          : { status: "ok", deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode },
      );
    }

    try {
      await db.execute(sql`SELECT 1`);
    } catch (error) {
      logger.warn({ err: error }, "Health check database probe failed");
      return Response.json(
        {
          status: "unhealthy",
          version: serverVersion,
          error: "database_unreachable",
        },
        { status: 503 },
      );
    }

    let bootstrapStatus: "ready" | "bootstrap_pending" = "ready";
    let bootstrapInviteActive = false;
    if (opts.deploymentMode === "authenticated") {
      const roleCount = await db
        .select({ count: count() })
        .from(instanceUserRoles)
        .where(sql`${instanceUserRoles.role} = 'instance_admin'`)
        .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));
      bootstrapStatus = roleCount > 0 ? "ready" : "bootstrap_pending";

      if (bootstrapStatus === "bootstrap_pending") {
        const now = new Date();
        const inviteCount = await db
          .select({ count: count() })
          .from(invites)
          .where(
            and(
              eq(invites.inviteType, "bootstrap_ceo"),
              isNull(invites.revokedAt),
              isNull(invites.acceptedAt),
              gt(invites.expiresAt, now),
            ),
          )
          .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));
        bootstrapInviteActive = inviteCount > 0;
      }
    }

    const persistedDevServerStatus = readPersistedDevServerStatus();
    let devServer: ReturnType<typeof toDevServerHealthStatus> | undefined;
    if (
      exposeDevServerDetails &&
      persistedDevServerStatus &&
      typeof (db as { select?: unknown }).select === "function"
    ) {
      const instanceSettings = instanceSettingsService(db);
      const experimentalSettings = await instanceSettings.getExperimental();
      const activeRunCount = await db
        .select({ count: count() })
        .from(heartbeatRuns)
        .where(inArray(heartbeatRuns.status, ["queued", "running"]))
        .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));

      devServer = toDevServerHealthStatus(persistedDevServerStatus, {
        autoRestartEnabled: experimentalSettings.autoRestartDevServerWhenIdle ?? false,
        activeRunCount,
      });
    }

    if (!exposeFullDetails) {
      return Response.json({
        status: "ok",
        deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode,
        bootstrapStatus,
        bootstrapInviteActive,
        ...(devServer ? { devServer } : {}),
      });
    }

    return Response.json({
      status: "ok",
      version: serverVersion,
      deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode,
      deploymentExposure: opts.deploymentExposure,
      authReady: opts.authReady,
      bootstrapStatus,
      bootstrapInviteActive,
      features: {
        companyDeletionEnabled: opts.companyDeletionEnabled,
      },
      ...(devServer ? { devServer } : {}),
    });
  };
}

/**
 * Returns an Express Router for the health endpoint.
 *
 * The public signature is intentionally identical to the previous version so
 * that the existing mount in app.ts (`api.use("/health", healthRoutes(...))`)
 * continues to work without any changes.
 */
export function healthRoutes(
  db?: Db,
  opts: {
    deploymentMode: DeploymentMode;
    deploymentExposure: DeploymentExposure;
    authReady: boolean;
    companyDeletionEnabled: boolean;
  } = {
    deploymentMode: "local_trusted",
    deploymentExposure: "private",
    authReady: true,
    companyDeletionEnabled: true,
  },
) {
  const handler = buildHealthHandler(db, opts);

  // expressHandler requires a StorageService in deps, but the health endpoint
  // never touches storage. We supply a sentinel that throws if accidentally
  // called, keeping the type contract honest without introducing a real dep.
  const storageSentinel = new Proxy({} as StorageService, {
    get(_target, prop) {
      throw new Error(`health handler unexpectedly accessed storage.${String(prop)}`);
    },
  });

  // db is optional for health but expressHandler's AdapterDeps types it as Db.
  // When db is undefined the handler returns early before touching ctx.db, so
  // we supply a sentinel here too rather than widen the adapter's types.
  const dbSentinel = new Proxy({} as Db, {
    get(_target, prop) {
      throw new Error(`health handler unexpectedly accessed db.${String(prop)}`);
    },
  });

  const router = Router();
  router.get(
    "/",
    expressHandler(handler, {
      db: db ?? dbSentinel,
      storage: storageSentinel,
    }),
  );
  return router;
}

```text
1	# Cloudflare Deployment Plan
2	
3	Status: Design contract for an additive Cloudflare deployment target
4	Date: 2026-04-30
5	Audience: Engineers implementing or reviewing the Cloudflare deployment path
6	Related: [DEPLOYMENT-MODES.md](./DEPLOYMENT-MODES.md), [DATABASE.md](./DATABASE.md), [SPEC-implementation.md](./SPEC-implementation.md)
7	
8	## 1. Goal
9	
10	Make Paperclip deployable to a user's Cloudflare account behind a single "Deploy to Cloudflare" button, with these properties:
11	
12	- **Pay-per-use**: idle cost approximates the Workers Paid base ($5/mo) plus storage.
13	- **Scales horizontally**: per-task isolation via Durable Objects, no shared in-process state.
14	- **Additive, not a fork**: lives as a new package (`packages/deploy-cloudflare/`) plus a small set of upstream-mergeable abstraction seams. Operators continue to track upstream Paperclip releases.
15	- **Same product**: identical UI, identical REST contract, identical agent-facing API. The deployment target is configurable; the product surface is not.
16	
17	## 2. Non-Goals
18	
19	- Replacing the Node/embedded-Postgres deployment path. That remains the primary local/self-hosted mode.
20	- Eliminating Containers/E2B for plugin execution. Cloudflare cannot spawn arbitrary child processes; sandboxed plugin work continues to run in Containers, E2B, or remote SSH (the existing sandbox bridge from [#4801](https://github.com/.../pull/4801)).
21	- Multi-region / multi-tenant SaaS. Each Cloudflare deployment is one Paperclip instance owned by one operator.
22	
23	## 3. Architectural Principle: Deployment Platform as an Orthogonal Axis
24	
25	Paperclip already has two orthogonal config axes (see [DEPLOYMENT-MODES.md](./DEPLOYMENT-MODES.md)):
26	
27	- **Auth mode**: `local_trusted | authenticated`
28	- **Reachability**: `loopback | lan | tailnet | custom`
29	
30	We add a third:
31	
32	- **Deployment platform**: `node | cloudflare`
33	
34	This axis decides which implementations of platform interfaces (DB driver, storage provider, scheduler, adapter executor, HTTP adapter) get wired in at boot. Auth mode and reachability stay unchanged. A Cloudflare deployment is `platform=cloudflare, mode=authenticated, exposure=public` — the auth/exposure semantics are unchanged from the existing `authenticated/public` mode, which is already the canonical internet-facing configuration.
35	
36	**Why this matters for upstream-mergeability**: every change required for Cloudflare also benefits the existing Node deployment (testability, DI, fewer global singletons). The Cloudflare package only contains *Cloudflare-specific implementations* of those interfaces — never branching logic in shared code.
37	
38	## 4. Resource Mapping
39	
40	| Concern | Cloudflare resource | Notes |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| UI ([ui/](../ui/)) | **Pages** | Static SPA build, no SSR. Free. |
43	| API + auth + MCP-over-SSE | **Workers** | One main Worker; route handlers from [server/src/routes/](../server/src/routes/) re-mounted via Hono. |
44	| Per-task / per-agent state, websockets, watchdogs | **Durable Objects** | One DO class per concern (TaskDO, AgentRunDO, ScheduledJobDO). Hibernation API for sockets. |
45	| Multi-step agent runs (heartbeat, retries, tool calls) | **Workflows** | Replaces in-process orchestration in [services/heartbeat.ts](../server/src/services/heartbeat.ts). Checkpointed, retry-safe. |
46	| Relational data | **Phase 1: Hyperdrive → Neon Postgres** / **Phase 2: D1** | See §6. Phase 1 keeps the existing schema unchanged. |
47	| Artifacts, skill bundles, attachments, DB backups | **R2** | New `R2Provider` implementation of `StorageProvider` ([server/src/storage/types.ts:31-37](../server/src/storage/types.ts#L31-L37)). |
48	| Sessions, hot config, instance settings cache | **KV** | BetterAuth sessions stay in DB (already portable); KV used for ephemeral hot reads only. |
49	| Background fanout (cost rollups, activity log flush, plugin job dispatch) | **Queues** | Replaces in-process timers in [server/src/index.ts:672-784](../server/src/index.ts#L672-L784). |
50	| Plugin / adapter process execution | **Containers** OR existing E2B/SSH sandbox bridge | Workers cannot spawn processes. Default: route to existing sandbox bridge. Containers is opt-in for users who want everything on Cloudflare. |
51	| Cron-style routines | **Cron Triggers** → enqueue into Queues / fire Workflows | Replaces in-process cron scheduler in [services/cron.ts](../server/src/services/cron.ts). |
52	| LLM API egress | Worker `fetch()` | No changes; LLM calls were already HTTP. |
53	
54	## 5. Existing Seams (Confirmed Clean)
55	
56	These already exist and only need new implementations — **no upstream changes required**:
57	
58	| Seam | File | What we add |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| `StorageProvider` | [server/src/storage/types.ts:31-37](../server/src/storage/types.ts#L31-L37) | `R2Provider` |
61	| `createApp(db, opts)` | [server/src/app.ts:108](../server/src/app.ts#L108) | Workers entrypoint that mounts the same route modules — see §6.3 for the Express/Hono adapter strategy |
62	| BetterAuth (DB-resident sessions) | [server/src/auth/better-auth.ts](../server/src/auth/better-auth.ts) | Works as-is on Hyperdrive+Neon |
63	| MCP server stdio transport | [packages/mcp-server/src/](../packages/mcp-server/src/) | Optional: wrap with SSE transport for hosted MCP. Stdio MCP continues to work locally. |
64	| Drizzle schema | [packages/db/src/schema/](../packages/db/src/schema/) | Used unchanged in Phase 1 (Hyperdrive+Neon) |
65	
66	## 6. New Seams Required (Upstream-Mergeable)
67	
68	These changes land in the main packages, with default Node implementations preserved. Each is independently useful for testability and is structured to be reviewable/mergeable upstream as standalone PRs.
69	
70	### 6.1 DB Driver Factory
71	
72	**Today**: [packages/db/src/client.ts:48-50](../packages/db/src/client.ts#L48-L50) hardcodes `postgres-js`.
73	
74	**Change**:
75	
76	```ts
77	// packages/db/src/client.ts
78	export type Db = ReturnType<typeof drizzlePg>; // unchanged shape
79	export function createPostgresDb(url: string): Db { /* current body */ }
80	// Re-export createDb for backwards compat:
81	export const createDb = createPostgresDb;
82	```
83	
84	The Cloudflare package adds (without touching `packages/db`):
85	
86	```ts
87	// packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/db/d1.ts  (Phase 2)
88	import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/d1";
89	export function createD1Db(binding: D1Database): Db { /* ... */ }
90	
91	// packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/db/hyperdrive.ts  (Phase 1)
92	import postgres from "postgres";
93	import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js";
94	export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: Hyperdrive): Db {
95	  return drizzle(postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString), { schema });
96	}
97	```
98	
99	**Migrations**: [packages/db/src/client.ts:9](../packages/db/src/client.ts#L9) reads migrations from disk. In Workers, migrations run at deploy time via `wrangler d1 migrations apply` (Phase 2) or via Neon/Hyperdrive direct connection during the post-deploy setup step (Phase 1). The disk-reading migration runner stays as-is for Node.
100	
101	### 6.2 Scheduler Interface
102	
103	**Today**: in-process `setInterval` loops in [server/src/index.ts:672-784](../server/src/index.ts#L672-L784) and [server/src/services/heartbeat.ts](../server/src/services/heartbeat.ts).
104	
105	**Change**: extract to an interface in `server/src/scheduler/types.ts`:
106	
107	```ts
108	export interface Scheduler {
109	  every(name: string, intervalMs: number, fn: () => Promise<void>): Disposable;
110	  at(name: string, when: Date, fn: () => Promise<void>): Disposable;
111	  cancel(name: string): void;
112	}
113	```
114	
115	Default Node implementation wraps `setInterval`/`setTimeout` (current behavior). Cloudflare implementation lives in the CF package and dispatches to a **`SchedulerDO`** that owns alarms — one DO per scheduled job, hibernates between fires.
116	
117	Heartbeat, watchdog, budget threshold, DB backup, plugin job sweep all become consumers of this interface. Each becomes individually testable in unit tests with a fake scheduler.
118	
119	### 6.3 HTTP Runtime Adapter
120	
121	**Today**: [server/src/app.ts:108](../server/src/app.ts#L108) returns an Express app. Routes live in [server/src/routes/](../server/src/routes/) as Express routers.
122	
123	**Constraint**: Workers cannot run Express. Hono runs on both Node and Workers.
124	
125	**Strategy** (lowest-risk, highest-leverage): introduce a transport-agnostic handler shape and adapters for Express (today) and Hono (Workers). Per-route migration is incremental.
126	
127	```ts
128	// server/src/http/handler.ts
129	export type Handler = (ctx: RequestCtx) => Promise<Response>;
130	export interface RequestCtx {
131	  method: string;
132	  url: URL;
133	  headers: Headers;
134	  json<T>(): Promise<T>;
135	  text(): Promise<string>;
136	  param(name: string): string | undefined;
137	  query(name: string): string | undefined;
138	  actor: ActorContext;        // already populated by middleware
139	  db: Db;
140	  storage: StorageService;
141	}
142	
143	// server/src/http/express-adapter.ts → wraps Handler as Express RequestHandler
144	// packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/http/hono-adapter.ts → mounts Handler under Hono
145	```
146	
147	**Migration**: routes are migrated one-at-a-time. Until a route is migrated, the Workers entrypoint can fall back to invoking the Express handler via a Web-Streams-based shim (slow path, but works). Health, auth, and the agent-facing API endpoints migrate first because they're the hot path.
148	
149	This is the largest change and the single biggest upstream PR. It is independently valuable: it makes route handlers unit-testable without spinning up Express, and it is the precondition for any non-Express deployment (Bun, Deno, edge runtimes, future workers).
150	
151	### 6.4 Adapter Executor Interface
152	
153	**Today**: [server/src/adapters/utils.ts:77-93](../server/src/adapters/utils.ts#L77-L93) wraps `child_process.spawn` directly via `runChildProcess`.
154	
155	**Change**: extract to an interface:
156	
157	```ts
158	// packages/adapter-utils/src/executor.ts
159	export interface CommandExecutor {
160	  run(input: {
161	    runId: string;
162	    command: string;
163	    args: string[];
164	    cwd: string;
165	    env: Record<string, string>;
166	    timeoutSec: number;
167	    graceSec: number;
168	    onLog: (stream: "stdout" | "stderr", chunk: string) => Promise<void>;
169	  }): Promise<RunProcessResult>;
170	  cancel(runId: string): Promise<void>;
171	}
172	```
173	
174	Default implementation = current `child_process.spawn` path. Cloudflare implementations:
175	
176	- `SandboxBridgeExecutor` — calls the existing E2B/SSH sandbox bridge (preferred default for `platform=cloudflare`).
177	- `ContainerExecutor` — invokes a Cloudflare Container service binding for users who want everything on Cloudflare.
178	
179	The choice is config: `cloudflare.adapter_executor = sandbox_bridge | container`.
180	
181	### 6.5 Object Storage Provider Registration
182	
183	**Today**: providers register via [server/src/storage/provider-registry.ts](../server/src/storage/provider-registry.ts) for `local_disk` and `s3`.
184	
185	**Change**: add an extension point so the CF package can register `r2` without touching the registry file (keeps the upstream registry stable):
186	
187	```ts
188	// server/src/storage/provider-registry.ts
189	const externalProviders = new Map<StorageProviderId, StorageProviderFactory>();
190	export function registerStorageProvider(id: StorageProviderId, factory: StorageProviderFactory) {
191	  externalProviders.set(id, factory);
192	}
193	```
194	
195	The `StorageProviderId` union in `@paperclipai/shared` adds `"r2"`. CF package registers `R2Provider` at boot.
196	
197	### 6.6 Filesystem Quarantine
198	
199	**Today**: server writes to `~/.paperclip/instances/default/` for skill bundles, artifacts, DB backups.
200	
201	**Change**: every disk write currently in the request path is already (or should be) routed through `StorageService` ([server/src/storage/types.ts](../server/src/storage/types.ts)). Audit and convert any direct `fs.writeFile`/`fs.readFile` in the request path to go through `StorageService`. This is a hygiene fix valuable on Node too. After this change, Workers compatibility is automatic for the request path.
202	
203	DB backups and migration journal reads remain disk-based but only run in admin/boot paths that don't execute on Workers (boot is `wrangler deploy`-time; backups become R2 dumps via a Worker cron + Workflow).
204	
205	## 7. Package Layout
206	
207	```
208	paperclip/
209	├── packages/
210	│   ├── db/                                  # +createPostgresDb (renamed); schema unchanged
211	│   ├── shared/                              # +"r2" added to StorageProviderId union
212	│   ├── adapter-utils/                       # +CommandExecutor interface
213	│   └── deploy-cloudflare/                   # NEW — all CF-specific code
214	│       ├── package.json
215	│       ├── wrangler.toml                    # resource bindings (D1/R2/KV/DOs/Queues/Workflows)
216	│       ├── src/
217	│       │   ├── worker/
218	│       │   │   ├── api.ts                   # Hono app: mounts route handlers
219	│       │   │   ├── mcp-sse.ts               # MCP-over-SSE Worker
220	│       │   │   └── setup.ts                 # /setup first-run flow (writes secrets)
221	│       │   ├── db/
222	│       │   │   ├── hyperdrive.ts            # Phase 1 driver
223	│       │   │   └── d1.ts                    # Phase 2 driver
224	│       │   ├── storage/
225	│       │   │   └── r2-provider.ts           # implements StorageProvider
226	│       │   ├── scheduler/
227	│       │   │   ├── scheduler-do.ts          # Durable Object owning alarms
228	│       │   │   └── cf-scheduler.ts          # Scheduler impl that talks to SchedulerDO
229	│       │   ├── runtime/
230	│       │   │   ├── task-do.ts               # per-task DO (state + WS hibernation)
231	│       │   │   ├── agent-run-do.ts          # per-agent-run DO
232	│       │   │   └── workflows/
233	│       │   │       ├── heartbeat.ts         # Cloudflare Workflow
234	│       │   │       └── plugin-dispatch.ts
235	│       │   ├── adapter-executor/
236	│       │   │   ├── sandbox-bridge.ts        # routes to existing E2B/SSH bridge
237	│       │   │   └── container.ts             # Cloudflare Container binding
238	│       │   ├── http/
239	│       │   │   └── hono-adapter.ts          # wraps server Handler as Hono routes
240	│       │   └── boot.ts                      # wires CF impls into the shared service container
241	│       └── deploy/
242	│           ├── deploy-button.md             # README snippet with the URL
243	│           └── post-deploy-setup.md         # operator instructions
244	├── ui/                                      # unchanged; deploys to Pages
245	└── server/                                  # +new seams (DB factory, Scheduler, Handler shape, CommandExecutor)
246	```
247	
248	## 8. Two-Phase Rollout
249	
250	### Phase 1 — Hyperdrive + Neon Postgres ("works in 2 weeks of focused work")
251	
252	Goal: get a working Cloudflare deployment without touching the schema.
253	
254	- DB: Hyperdrive in front of Neon Postgres. Drizzle schema unchanged.
255	- Storage: R2.
256	- Compute: Workers + DOs + Workflows.
257	- Plugin execution: existing sandbox bridge (no Containers).
258	- UI: Pages.
259	
260	This is the MVP. It validates the entire architecture (HTTP adapter, scheduler, storage, DOs) without taking on the schema port. Idle cost: $5/mo Workers Paid + Neon free tier + R2 (free tier covers small instances).
261	
262	### Phase 2 — D1 Migration (optional, for pure-Cloudflare)
263	
264	Goal: eliminate the external Postgres dependency.
265	
266	- Schema port: `jsonb` → `text` JSON columns; remove any pg-only types/operators (audit needed). Drizzle has a D1 dialect.
267	- New migration set targeting D1; data migration tool that reads from Postgres and writes to D1.
268	- Idle cost drops further (no Neon).
269	
270	Phase 2 is opt-in. Phase 1 deployments keep working. The CF package config selects between `db: hyperdrive | d1`.
271	
272	## 9. One-Click Install Flow
273	
274	### 9.1 The Button
275	
276	`README.md` gets a button that links to:
277	
278	```
279	https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/<org>/paperclip
280	```
281	
282	`wrangler.toml` at `packages/deploy-cloudflare/wrangler.toml` declares all bindings: D1 (or Hyperdrive config placeholder), R2 buckets, KV namespaces, DO classes + migrations, Queues, Workflows, Cron Triggers, Pages project.
283	
284	Cloudflare provisions every resource declared in `wrangler.toml` in one shot.
285	
286	### 9.2 First-Run Setup
287	
288	Cloudflare cannot collect secrets via the deploy flow. After provisioning, the deployed Worker serves `/setup` on first request when no `SETUP_COMPLETED` flag is present in KV. The setup page collects:
289	
290	- LLM provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.)
291	- (Phase 1 only) Neon connection string — or auto-provision via Neon API if user pastes a Neon API token
292	- Operator email / initial board user credentials
293	- Optional: sandbox bridge credentials (E2B API key, or SSH endpoint)
294	
295	The setup endpoint writes secrets via the Cloudflare API using a scoped API token the user pastes. Token requirements (minimum scopes) are documented in `deploy/post-deploy-setup.md`. Once written, they propagate to all Workers in the project on the next request — no redeploy.
296	
297	To avoid per-Worker secret duplication, the canonical store is **encrypted config in D1/Postgres** (`instance_settings` table, already exists per [services/instance-settings.ts](../server/src/services/instance-settings.ts) pattern). Worker secrets hold only the master encryption key. All Workers read decrypted config from the DB. Updating a config value is one DB write, no CF API calls.
298	
299	### 9.3 Post-Setup State
300	
301	After `/setup` completes, the operator is redirected into the standard authenticated UI. The instance behaves identically to a self-hosted Paperclip in `authenticated/public` mode. All upstream-documented operator workflows ([CLI.md](./CLI.md), [DEVELOPING.md](./DEVELOPING.md), [DEPLOYMENT-MODES.md](./DEPLOYMENT-MODES.md)) apply.
302	
303	## 10. Pricing Model
304	
305	Idle (no traffic, no scheduled jobs firing):
306	
307	| Item | Cost |
308	|---|---|
309	| Workers Paid plan | $5/mo flat |
310	| Pages | $0 |
311	| D1 storage (Phase 2) | ~$0 for small instance |
312	| R2 storage | $0.015/GB-mo |
313	| KV storage | $0 within free tier |
314	| Neon Postgres (Phase 1, free tier) | $0 |
315	| **Idle total** | **~$5–6/mo** |
316	
317	Active usage adds: Worker requests ($0.30/M after included 10M), Worker CPU time, DO duration (per-ms while awake), DO requests, Workflow steps, R2 operations, D1 reads/writes. No request, no cost. WS hibernation API ensures DOs aren't billed for idle sockets.
318	
319	What kills the pay-per-use story if misused:
320	
321	- DOs holding non-hibernated WebSockets — fix: always use `WebSocketHibernation` API.
322	- Workflows with infinite loops or no checkpointing — fix: bound steps and use `step.sleep` for waits.
323	- Cron triggers firing too often — fix: use Queues + lazy DO wakeup instead of high-frequency cron.
324	
325	## 11. Observability
326	
327	- **Logs**: Workers Logs (via Logpush to R2 for retention).
328	- **Metrics**: Workers Analytics + custom counters via Analytics Engine.
329	- **Tracing**: existing telemetry shape in [packages/shared/src/telemetry/](../packages/shared/src/telemetry/) maps onto Workers Tail. No new abstraction needed.
330	- **Alerting**: Cloudflare email alerts on error rate / DO storage thresholds. Optional: forward to user's preferred channel via a Worker.
331	
332	## 12. Security
333	
334	- Auth mode is locked to `authenticated/public` for `platform=cloudflare`. `local_trusted` is rejected at boot.
335	- Secrets at rest: master key in Worker secrets, all other secrets in DB encrypted with that key.
336	- Inter-Worker auth: service bindings (capability-based, no shared secret). For external service-to-Worker, mTLS via Cloudflare Access in front of the Worker is recommended for non-public endpoints (agent-facing API can be public; admin endpoints behind Access).
337	- CSRF/CORS: existing middleware in [server/src/middleware/](../server/src/middleware/) ports unchanged via the HTTP adapter.
338	
339	## 13. Out of Scope (Explicit)
340	
341	- **Plugin marketplace on Cloudflare**: not yet. Plugin distribution remains as in [SPEC-implementation.md §5.2](./SPEC-implementation.md#52-out-of-scope-v1).
342	- **Multi-region active-active**: Cloudflare auto-routes Workers; D1/Postgres remains single-region. No cross-region consistency story.
343	- **Bring-your-own-VPC**: not supported. Hyperdrive can target a private Postgres via Tunnel, but is not in scope for the MVP.
344	- **Replacing Containers/E2B for plugin execution with pure Workers**: out of scope. Workers cannot spawn processes; plugins that depend on subprocesses always require a sandbox.
345	
346	## 14. Open Questions
347	
348	1. **Express → Hono migration scope**: do we migrate all routes in one PR, or one route module at a time with a transitional Express-via-shim path on Workers? Recommend: incremental, hot-path first.
349	2. **D1 jsonb port**: which queries currently rely on Postgres JSONB operators (`->`, `->>`, `@>`)? Audit needed before committing to Phase 2.
350	3. **Plugin worker manager** ([services/plugin-worker-manager.ts](../server/src/services/plugin-worker-manager.ts)) abstracts plugin lifecycle. How much of its current shape maps to a Workflow + Container model? Needs its own design pass before Phase 1 declares done.
351	4. **MCP transport on Cloudflare**: confirm SSE-over-Workers is acceptable to the MCP clients we care about, or whether we need WebSocket transport.
352	5. **DO-per-task cardinality**: at 10K+ active tasks, do we want one DO per task, or one DO per company sharded? Affects storage layout and cost.
353	
354	## 15. Implementation Order
355	
356	The work decomposes into independently-mergeable PRs. Each upstream PR is reviewed and merged on its own merit (improves testability or modularity for the Node deployment too); the CF package PR lands last and only contains additive code.
357	
358	| # | PR | Target | Scope |
359	|---|---|---|---|
360	| 1 | DB factory split | upstream | Rename `createDb` → `createPostgresDb` with backwards-compat alias; export `Db` type. |
361	| 2 | StorageProvider extension point | upstream | Add `registerStorageProvider`; add `"r2"` to `StorageProviderId`. |
362	| 3 | Filesystem quarantine | upstream | Audit request path for direct `fs` writes, route through `StorageService`. |
363	| 4 | Scheduler interface | upstream | Extract `Scheduler` interface; default Node impl wraps current `setInterval` calls. |
364	| 5 | CommandExecutor interface | upstream | Extract from [adapters/utils.ts](../server/src/adapters/utils.ts); default impl unchanged. |
365	| 6 | HTTP Handler shape | upstream | Introduce transport-agnostic `Handler` + Express adapter; migrate health/auth routes first. |
366	| 7 | Continue HTTP migration | upstream | Migrate remaining routes one module at a time. |
367	| 8 | `packages/deploy-cloudflare` skeleton | additive | Package layout, `wrangler.toml`, Hono adapter, R2 provider, Hyperdrive driver, `/setup` flow. |
368	| 9 | Durable Objects (Task, AgentRun, Scheduler) | additive | DO classes implementing the Scheduler interface and per-task state. |
369	| 10 | Workflows for heartbeat/budget | additive | Replace in-process scheduling with Workflows + Cron Triggers. |
370	| 11 | Adapter executors | additive | `SandboxBridgeExecutor` (default) and `ContainerExecutor`. |
371	| 12 | Deploy button + setup wizard polish | additive | README button, post-deploy docs, end-to-end install rehearsal. |
372	| 13 | (Optional) D1 migration | additive | Schema port, data migration tool, dual-driver runtime. |
373	
374	Each upstream PR (#1–#7) is independently reviewable, has tests, and improves the Node deployment. The Cloudflare package never blocks upstream review.
375

265	export function createCommandManagedSandboxCallbackBridgeQueueClient(input: {
266	  runner: CommandManagedRuntimeRunner;
267	  remoteCwd: string;
268	  timeoutMs?: number | null;
269	}): SandboxCallbackBridgeQueueClient {
270	  const timeoutMs = normalizeTimeoutMs(input.timeoutMs, DEFAULT_BRIDGE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS);
271	  const runChecked = async (action: string, script: string) =>
272	    requireSuccessfulResult(action, await runShell(input.runner, input.remoteCwd, script, timeoutMs));
273	
274	  return {
275	    makeDir: async (remotePath) => {
276	      await runChecked(`mkdir ${remotePath}`, `mkdir -p ${shellQuote(remotePath)}`);
277	    },
278	    listJsonFiles: async (remotePath) => {
279	      const result = await runShell(
280	        input.runner,
281	        input.remoteCwd,
282	        [
283	          `if [ -d ${shellQuote(remotePath)} ]; then`,
284	          `  for file in ${shellQuote(remotePath)}/*.json; do`,
285	          `    [ -f "$file" ] || continue`,
286	          "    basename \"$file\"",
287	          "  done",
288	          "fi",
289	        ].join("\n"),
290	        timeoutMs,
291	      );
292	      requireSuccessfulResult(`list ${remotePath}`, result);
293	      return result.stdout
294	        .split(/\r?\n/)
295	        .map((line) => line.trim())
296	        .filter((line) => line.length > 0)
297	        .sort((left, right) => left.localeCompare(right));
298	    },
299	    readTextFile: async (remotePath) => {
300	      const result = await runChecked(`read ${remotePath}`, `base64 < ${shellQuote(remotePath)}`);
301	      return Buffer.from(result.stdout.replace(/\s+/g, ""), "base64").toString("utf8");
302	    },
303	    writeTextFile: async (remotePath, body) => {
304	      const remoteDir = path.posix.dirname(remotePath);
305	      const tempPath = `${remotePath}.paperclip-upload.b64`;
306	      await runChecked(
307	        `prepare upload ${remotePath}`,
308	        `mkdir -p ${shellQuote(remoteDir)} && rm -f ${shellQuote(tempPath)} && : > ${shellQuote(tempPath)}`,
309	      );
310	      const base64Body = toBuffer(Buffer.from(body, "utf8")).toString("base64");
311	      for (const chunk of base64Chunks(base64Body)) {
312	        await runChecked(
313	          `append upload chunk ${remotePath}`,
314	          `printf '%s' ${shellQuote(chunk)} >> ${shellQuote(tempPath)}`,
315	        );
316	      }
317	      await runChecked(
318	        `finalize upload ${remotePath}`,
319	        `base64 -d < ${shellQuote(tempPath)} > ${shellQuote(remotePath)} && rm -f ${shellQuote(tempPath)}`,
320	      );
321	    },
322	    rename: async (fromPath, toPath) => {
323	      await runChecked(
324	        `rename ${fromPath}`,
325	        `mkdir -p ${shellQuote(path.posix.dirname(toPath))} && mv ${shellQuote(fromPath)} ${shellQuote(toPath)}`,
326	      );
327	    },
328	    remove: async (remotePath) => {
329	      await runChecked(`remove ${remotePath}`, `rm -rf ${shellQuote(remotePath)}`);
330	    },
331	  };
332	}

344	export async function startSandboxCallbackBridgeWorker(input: {
345	  client: SandboxCallbackBridgeQueueClient;
346	  queueDir: string;
347	  pollIntervalMs?: number | null;
348	  authorizeRequest?: (request: SandboxCallbackBridgeRequest) => string | null | Promise<string | null>;
349	  handleRequest: (request: SandboxCallbackBridgeRequest) => Promise<{
350	    status: number;
351	    headers?: Record<string, string>;
352	    body?: string;
353	  }>;
354	  maxBodyBytes?: number | null;
355	}): Promise<SandboxCallbackBridgeWorkerHandle> {
356	  const pollIntervalMs = normalizeTimeoutMs(input.pollIntervalMs, DEFAULT_BRIDGE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS);
357	  const maxBodyBytes = normalizeTimeoutMs(input.maxBodyBytes, DEFAULT_BRIDGE_MAX_BODY_BYTES);
358	  const directories = sandboxCallbackBridgeDirectories(input.queueDir);
359	  await input.client.makeDir(directories.rootDir);
360	  await input.client.makeDir(directories.requestsDir);
361	  await input.client.makeDir(directories.responsesDir);
362	  await input.client.makeDir(directories.logsDir);
363	
364	  let stopping = false;
365	  let inFlight = 0;
366	  let settled = false;
367	  let stopDeadline = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
368	  let settleResolve: (() => void) | null = null;
369	  const settledPromise = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
370	    settleResolve = resolve;
371	  });
372	  const authorizeRequest = input.authorizeRequest ??
373	    ((request: SandboxCallbackBridgeRequest) => authorizeSandboxCallbackBridgeRequestWithRoutes(request));
374	
375	  const processRequestFile = async (fileName: string) => {
376	    const requestPath = path.posix.join(directories.requestsDir, fileName);
377	    const responsePath = path.posix.join(directories.responsesDir, fileName);
378	    const raw = await input.client.readTextFile(requestPath);
379	    let request: SandboxCallbackBridgeRequest;
380	    try {
381	      request = JSON.parse(raw) as SandboxCallbackBridgeRequest;
382	    } catch {
383	      const requestId = fileName.replace(/\.json$/i, "") || randomUUID();
384	      await writeBridgeResponse(input.client, responsePath, {
385	        id: requestId,
386	        status: 400,
387	        headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
388	        body: JSON.stringify({ error: "Invalid bridge request payload." }),
389	        completedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
390	      });
391	      await input.client.remove(requestPath);
392	      return;
393	    }
394	
395	    const denialReason = await authorizeRequest(request);
396	    if (denialReason) {
397	      await writeBridgeResponse(input.client, responsePath, {
398	        id: request.id,
399	        status: 403,
400	        headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
401	        body: JSON.stringify({ error: denialReason }),
402	        completedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
403	      });
404	      await input.client.remove(requestPath);
405	      return;
406	    }
407	
408	    try {
409	      const result = await input.handleRequest(request);
410	      const responseBody = result.body ?? "";
411	      if (Buffer.byteLength(responseBody, "utf8") > maxBodyBytes) {
412	        throw new Error(`Bridge response body exceeded the configured size limit of ${maxBodyBytes} bytes.`);
413	      }
414	      await writeBridgeResponse(input.client, responsePath, {
415	        id: request.id,
416	        status: result.status,
417	        headers: result.headers ?? {},
418	        body: responseBody,
419	        completedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
420	      });
421	    } catch (error) {
422	      console.warn(
423	        `[paperclip] sandbox callback bridge handler failed for ${request.id}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
424	      );
425	      await writeBridgeResponse(input.client, responsePath, {
426	        id: request.id,
427	        status: 502,
428	        headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
429	        body: JSON.stringify({
430	          error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
431	        }),
432	        completedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
433	      });
434	    } finally {
435	      await input.client.remove(requestPath);
436	    }
437	  };
438	
439	  const failPendingRequests = async (message: string) => {
440	    const fileNames = await input.client.listJsonFiles(directories.requestsDir).catch(() => []);
441	    for (const fileName of fileNames) {
442	      const requestPath = path.posix.join(directories.requestsDir, fileName);
443	      const responsePath = path.posix.join(directories.responsesDir, fileName);
444	      const requestId = fileName.replace(/\.json$/i, "") || randomUUID();
445	      try {
446	        const raw = await input.client.readTextFile(requestPath);
447	        const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<SandboxCallbackBridgeRequest>;
448	        await writeBridgeResponse(input.client, responsePath, {
449	          id: typeof parsed.id === "string" && parsed.id.length > 0 ? parsed.id : requestId,
450	          status: 503,
451	          headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
452	          body: JSON.stringify({ error: message }),
453	          completedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
454	        });
455	      } catch (error) {
456	        console.warn(
457	          `[paperclip] sandbox callback bridge failed to abort pending request ${requestId}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
458	        );
459	      } finally {
460	        await input.client.remove(requestPath).catch(() => undefined);
461	      }
462	    }
463	  };
464	
465	  const loop = (async () => {
466	    try {
467	      while (true) {
468	        const fileNames = await input.client.listJsonFiles(directories.requestsDir);
469	        if (fileNames.length === 0) {
470	          if (stopping) {
471	            break;
472	          }
473	          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, pollIntervalMs));
474	          continue;
475	        }
476	        for (const fileName of fileNames) {
477	          if (stopping && Date.now() >= stopDeadline) break;
478	          inFlight += 1;
479	          try {
480	            await processRequestFile(fileName);
481	          } finally {
482	            inFlight -= 1;
483	          }
484	        }
485	        if (stopping && Date.now() >= stopDeadline) {
486	          break;
487	        }
488	      }
489	    } finally {
490	      settled = true;
491	      if (settleResolve) {
492	        settleResolve();
493	      }
494	    }
495	  })();
496	
497	  void loop;
498	
499	  return {
500	    stop: async (options = {}) => {
501	      stopping = true;
502	      const drainMs = normalizeTimeoutMs(options.drainTimeoutMs, DEFAULT_BRIDGE_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS);
503	      stopDeadline = Date.now() + drainMs;
504	      if (!settled) {
505	        await Promise.race([
506	          settledPromise,
507	          new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, drainMs)),
508	        ]);
509	      }
510	      await failPendingRequests("Bridge worker stopped before request could be handled.");
511	    },
512	  };
513	}

## Summary

### Scope

The audit covered all `node:fs` / `node:fs/promises` usage in request-path files under `server/src/routes/`, `server/src/services/`, and `server/src/middleware/`. Tests (`__tests__/`) and boot-only infrastructure were noted but no changes made there.

All hits fall into Pattern C (local-disk-only logic incompatible with Workers) — none were simple Pattern A/B substitutions that could be mechanically swapped for `StorageService` calls without a broader architectural redesign. Every affected site received a `// TODO(cloudflare):` comment explaining the problem and the required migration path.

### Key observations for prioritization

The highest-complexity migrations are:
1. **`company-skills.ts` + `agent-instructions.ts`** — these are deep business-logic services that need R2 object storage + D1 file-inventory tables to replace the directory tree model
2. **`run-log-store.ts` + `workspace-operation-log-store.ts`** — these are clean interface-abstracted stores; the Workers implementation is straightforward once R2 multipart upload is available

You are implementing PR #3 (Filesystem Quarantine) from a Cloudflare deployment plan for the Paperclip monorepo at `/Users/migmac/Documents/GitHub/_ABM/paperclip`.

## Goal

Audit and fix all direct `node:fs` / `fs/promises` usage in the **request path** of `server/src/` so that every read/write of business data goes through `StorageService` instead. This is required for Workers compatibility (Workers have no persistent filesystem).

**Scope**: Only the request path (routes, services, middleware). NOT:
- DB migration runner (boot-time only, fine to keep disk reads there)
- DB backup code (admin-only path, not in Workers)
- Dev-only utilities

## Step 1: Audit

Run a search to find all direct `fs`, `node:fs`, `fs/promises` usages in `server/src/`:
```bash
grep -rn "from 'node:fs" server/src/ 
grep -rn "from \"node:fs" server/src/
grep -rn "from 'fs'" server/src/
grep -rn "node:fs/promises" server/src/
grep -rn "readFile\|writeFile\|mkdir\|readdir\|unlink\|stat\b" server/src/routes/ server/src/services/ server/src/middleware/
```

For each hit, determine:
1. Is it in a request-path function (called during HTTP requests or heartbeat ticks)?
2. What is it doing? Reading a skill bundle? Writing an artifact? Something else?
3. Can it be replaced with a StorageService call?

## Step 2: Fix request-path fs usage

For each request-path `fs` usage you find:

### Pattern A: Writing a file (artifact, skill bundle output)
Replace `fs.writeFile(path, buffer)` with:
```ts
await storageService.putFile({
  companyId,
  namespace: "artifacts", // or appropriate namespace
  originalFilename: filename,
  contentType: "application/octet-stream",
  body: Buffer.from(content),
});
```

### Pattern B: Reading a file that was written via StorageService
Replace `fs.readFile(path)` with:
```ts
const result = await storageService.getObject(companyId, objectKey);
// result.stream is a Node Readable
```

### Pattern C: Reading static bundled files (skill definitions, templates)
These should be converted to either:
- Inline the content as a TypeScript constant (if small)
- Bundle as a Worker asset (if large)
- Read from R2 at deploy-time

For each Pattern C hit, note the file and add a TODO comment: `// TODO(cloudflare): convert to bundled asset or R2 object`.

## StorageService type reminder
The interface is in `server/src/storage/types.ts`:
- `putFile(input: PutFileInput): Promise<PutFileResult>` 
- `getObject(companyId, objectKey): Promise<GetObjectResult>`
- `headObject(companyId, objectKey): Promise<HeadObjectResult>`
- `deleteObject(companyId, objectKey): Promise<void>`

`StorageService` is injected via `createApp(db, opts)` where `opts.storageService` is the service. In route handlers, it's available as a dependency.

## How StorageService flows to route handlers

Read `server/src/app.ts` (lines 108 onwards) to understand how `storageService` is passed to routes. Look at one or two existing routes that use `storageService` (e.g. `server/src/routes/assets.ts`) to see the established pattern for accessing it.

The issue is that `Object.entries(req.headers)` yields `[string, string | string[] | undefined][]`, so after the `Array.isArray` branch the `else` has `string | undefined` — the `undefined` guard only prevents `undefined` entries at the top level but TypeScript doesn't fully narrow in the `else`. Let me fix this with an explicit string cast:

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-04-30 14:51:56Z)**_

39	export function buildInvocationEnvForLogs(
40	  env: Record<string, string>,
41	  options: BuildInvocationEnvForLogsOptions = {},
42	): Record<string, string> {
43	  const maybeBuildInvocationEnvForLogs = (
44	    serverUtils as typeof serverUtils & {
45	      buildInvocationEnvForLogs?: (
46	        env: Record<string, string>,
47	        options?: BuildInvocationEnvForLogsOptions,
48	      ) => Record<string, string>;
49	    }
50	  ).buildInvocationEnvForLogs;
51	
52	  if (typeof maybeBuildInvocationEnvForLogs === "function") {
53	    return maybeBuildInvocationEnvForLogs(env, options);
54	  }
55	
56	  const merged: Record<string, string> = { ...env };
57	  const runtimeEnv = options.runtimeEnv ?? {};
58	
59	  for (const key of options.includeRuntimeKeys ?? []) {
60	    if (key in merged) continue;
61	    const value = runtimeEnv[key];
62	    if (typeof value !== "string" || value.length === 0) continue;
63	    merged[key] = value;
64	  }
65	
66	  const resolvedCommand = options.resolvedCommand?.trim();
67	  if (resolvedCommand) {
68	    merged[options.resolvedCommandEnvKey ?? "PAPERCLIP_RESOLVED_COMMAND"] = resolvedCommand;
69	  }
70	
71	  return redactEnvForLogs(merged);
72	}

228	  router.get("/_plugins/:pluginId/ui/*filePath", async (req, res) => {
229	    const { pluginId } = req.params;
230	
231	    // Extract the relative file path from the named wildcard.
232	    // In Express 5 with path-to-regexp v8, named wildcards may return
233	    // an array of path segments or a single string.
234	    const rawParam = req.params.filePath;
235	    const rawFilePath = Array.isArray(rawParam)
236	      ? rawParam.join("/")
237	      : rawParam as string | undefined;
238	
239	    if (!rawFilePath || rawFilePath.length === 0) {
240	      res.status(400).json({ error: "File path is required" });
241	      return;
242	    }
243	
244	    // Step 1: Look up the plugin
245	    let plugin = null;
246	    try {
247	      plugin = await registry.getById(pluginId);
248	    } catch (error) {
249	      const maybeCode =
250	        typeof error === "object" && error !== null && "code" in error
251	          ? (error as { code?: unknown }).code
252	          : undefined;
253	      if (maybeCode !== "22P02") {
254	        throw error;
255	      }
256	    }
257	    if (!plugin) {
258	      plugin = await registry.getByKey(pluginId);
259	    }
260	
261	    if (!plugin) {
262	      res.status(404).json({ error: "Plugin not found" });
263	      return;
264	    }
265	
266	    // Step 2: Verify the plugin is ready and has UI declared
267	    if (plugin.status !== "ready") {
268	      res.status(403).json({
269	        error: `Plugin UI is not available (status: ${plugin.status})`,
270	      });
271	      return;
272	    }
273	
274	    const manifest = plugin.manifestJson;
275	    if (!manifest?.entrypoints?.ui) {
276	      res.status(404).json({ error: "Plugin does not declare a UI bundle" });
277	      return;
278	    }
279	
280	    // Step 2b: Check for devUiUrl in plugin config — proxy to local dev server
281	    // when a plugin author has configured a dev server URL for hot-reload.
282	    // See PLUGIN_SPEC.md §27.2 — Local Development Workflow
283	    try {
284	      const configRow = await registry.getConfig(plugin.id);
285	      const devUiUrl =
286	        configRow &&
287	        typeof configRow === "object" &&
288	        "configJson" in configRow &&
289	        (configRow as { configJson: Record<string, unknown> }).configJson?.devUiUrl;
290	
291	      if (typeof devUiUrl === "string" && devUiUrl.length > 0) {
292	        // Dev proxy is only available in development mode
293	        if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production") {
294	          log.warn(
295	            { pluginId: plugin.id },
296	            "plugin-ui-static: devUiUrl ignored in production",
297	          );
298	          // Fall through to static file serving below
299	        } else {
300	          // Guard against rawFilePath overriding the base URL via protocol
301	          // scheme (e.g. "https://evil.com/x") or protocol-relative paths
302	          // (e.g. "//evil.com/x") which cause `new URL(path, base)` to
303	          // ignore the base entirely.
304	          // Normalize percent-encoding so encoded slashes (%2F) can't bypass
305	          // the protocol/path checks below.
306	          let decodedPath: string;
307	          try {
308	            decodedPath = decodeURIComponent(rawFilePath);
309	          } catch {
310	            res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid file path" });
311	            return;
312	          }
313	          if (
314	            decodedPath.includes("://") ||
315	            decodedPath.startsWith("//") ||
316	            decodedPath.startsWith("\\\\")
317	          ) {
318	            res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid file path" });
319	            return;
320	          }
321	
322	          // Proxy the request to the dev server
323	          const targetUrl = new URL(rawFilePath, devUiUrl.endsWith("/") ? devUiUrl : devUiUrl + "/");
324	
325	          // SSRF protection: only allow http/https and localhost targets for dev proxy
326	          if (targetUrl.protocol !== "http:" && targetUrl.protocol !== "https:") {
327	            res.status(400).json({ error: "devUiUrl must use http or https protocol" });
328	            return;
329	          }
330	
331	          // Dev proxy is restricted to loopback addresses only.
332	          // Validate the *constructed* targetUrl hostname (not the base) to
333	          // catch any path-based override that slipped past the checks above.
334	          const devHost = targetUrl.hostname;
335	          const isLoopback =
336	            devHost === "localhost" ||
337	            devHost === "127.0.0.1" ||
338	            devHost === "::1" ||
339	            devHost === "[::1]";
340	          if (!isLoopback) {
341	            log.warn(
342	              { pluginId: plugin.id, devUiUrl, host: devHost },
343	              "plugin-ui-static: devUiUrl must target localhost, rejecting proxy",
344	            );
345	            res.status(400).json({ error: "devUiUrl must target localhost" });
346	            return;
347	          }
348	
349	          log.debug(
350	            { pluginId: plugin.id, devUiUrl, targetUrl: targetUrl.href },
351	            "plugin-ui-static: proxying to devUiUrl",
352	          );
353	
354	          try {
355	            const controller = new AbortController();
356	            const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10_000);
357	            try {
358	              const upstream = await fetch(targetUrl.href, { signal: controller.signal });
359	              if (!upstream.ok) {
360	                res.status(upstream.status).json({
361	                  error: `Dev server returned ${upstream.status}`,
362	                });
363	                return;
364	              }
365	
366	              const contentType = upstream.headers.get("content-type");
367	              if (contentType) res.set("Content-Type", contentType);
368	              res.set("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate");
369	
370	              const body = await upstream.arrayBuffer();
371	              res.send(Buffer.from(body));
372	              return;
373	            } finally {
374	              clearTimeout(timeout);
375	            }
376	          } catch (proxyErr) {
377	            log.warn(
378	              {
379	                pluginId: plugin.id,
380	                devUiUrl,
381	                err: proxyErr instanceof Error ? proxyErr.message : String(proxyErr),
382	              },
383	              "plugin-ui-static: failed to proxy to devUiUrl, falling back to static",
384	            );
385	            // Fall through to static serving below
386	          }
387	        }
388	      }
389	    } catch {
390	      // Config lookup failure is non-fatal — fall through to static serving
391	    }
392	
393	    // Step 3: Resolve the plugin's UI directory
394	    const uiDir = resolvePluginUiDir(
395	      options.localPluginDir,
396	      plugin.packageName,
397	      manifest.entrypoints.ui,
398	      plugin.packagePath,
399	    );
400	
401	    if (!uiDir) {
402	      log.warn(
403	        { pluginId: plugin.id, pluginKey: plugin.pluginKey, packageName: plugin.packageName },
404	        "plugin-ui-static: UI directory not found on disk",
405	      );
406	      res.status(404).json({ error: "Plugin UI directory not found" });
407	      return;
408	    }
409	
410	    // Step 4: Resolve the requested file path and prevent traversal (including symlinks)
411	    const resolvedFilePath = path.resolve(uiDir, rawFilePath);
412	
413	    // Step 5: Check that the file exists and is a regular file
414	    let fileStat: fs.Stats;
415	    try {
416	      fileStat = fs.statSync(resolvedFilePath);
417	    } catch {
418	      res.status(404).json({ error: "File not found" });
419	      return;
420	    }
421	
422	    // Security: resolve symlinks via realpathSync and verify containment.
423	    // This prevents symlink-based traversal that string-based startsWith misses.
424	    let realFilePath: string;
425	    let realUiDir: string;
426	    try {
427	      realFilePath = fs.realpathSync(resolvedFilePath);
428	      realUiDir = fs.realpathSync(uiDir);
429	    } catch {
430	      res.status(404).json({ error: "File not found" });
431	      return;
432	    }
433	
434	    const relative = path.relative(realUiDir, realFilePath);
435	    if (relative.startsWith("..") || path.isAbsolute(relative)) {
436	      res.status(403).json({ error: "Access denied" });
437	      return;
438	    }
439	
440	    if (!fileStat.isFile()) {
441	      res.status(404).json({ error: "File not found" });
442	      return;
443	    }
444	
445	    // Step 6: Determine cache strategy based on filename
446	    const basename = path.basename(resolvedFilePath);
447	    const isContentHashed = CONTENT_HASH_PATTERN.test(basename);
448	
449	    // Step 7: Set cache headers
450	    if (isContentHashed) {
451	      res.set("Cache-Control", CACHE_CONTROL_IMMUTABLE);
452	    } else {
453	      res.set("Cache-Control", CACHE_CONTROL_REVALIDATE);
454	
455	      // Compute and set ETag for conditional request support
456	      const etag = computeETag(fileStat.size, fileStat.mtimeMs);
457	      res.set("ETag", etag);
458	
459	      // Check If-None-Match for 304 Not Modified
460	      const ifNoneMatch = req.headers["if-none-match"];
461	      if (ifNoneMatch === etag) {
462	        res.status(304).end();
463	        return;
464	      }
465	    }
466	
467	    // Step 8: Set Content-Type
468	    const ext = path.extname(resolvedFilePath).toLowerCase();
469	    const contentType = MIME_TYPES[ext];
470	    if (contentType) {
471	      res.set("Content-Type", contentType);
472	    }
473	
474	    // Step 9: Set CORS headers (plugin UI may be loaded from different origin in dev)
475	    res.set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*");
476	
477	    // Step 10: Send the file
478	    // The plugin source can live in Git worktrees (e.g. ".worktrees/...").
479	    // `send` defaults to dotfiles:"ignore", which treats dot-directories as
480	    // not found. We already enforce traversal safety above, so allow dot paths.
481	    res.sendFile(resolvedFilePath, { dotfiles: "allow" }, (err) => {
482	      if (err) {
483	        log.error(
484	          { err, pluginId: plugin.id, filePath: resolvedFilePath },
485	          "plugin-ui-static: error sending file",
486	        );
487	        // Only send error if headers haven't been sent yet
488	        if (!res.headersSent) {
489	          res.status(500).json({ error: "Failed to serve file" });
490	        }
491	      }
492	    });
493	  });
494	
495	  return router;
496	}

# =============================================================================
# Paperclip — Cloudflare Workers deployment configuration
#
# After running `wrangler deploy` for the first time, fill in the placeholder
# IDs that Cloudflare generates (search for "FILL_IN_AFTER_DEPLOY").
#
# Quick start:
#   1. wrangler deploy
#   2. wrangler hyperdrive create paperclip-hyperdrive --connection-string="<neon-url>"
#      Then paste the returned ID into [hyperdrive] binding below.
#   3. Open https://<your-worker>.workers.dev/setup to complete first-run setup.
# =============================================================================

name = "paperclip-api"
compatibility_date = "2024-09-23"
compatibility_flags = ["nodejs_compat"]
main = "src/worker/api.ts"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pages — serves the React UI build from ui/dist
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[pages_build_output_dir]
path = "../../ui/dist"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables (non-secret; override secrets via `wrangler secret put`)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[vars]
DEPLOYMENT_PLATFORM = "cloudflare"
DEPLOYMENT_MODE = "authenticated"
DEPLOYMENT_EXPOSURE = "public"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# R2 object storage — artifacts, skill bundles, attachments, DB backups
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[r2_buckets]]
binding = "PAPERCLIP_STORAGE"
bucket_name = "paperclip-storage"
# preview_bucket_name = "paperclip-storage-preview"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KV — sessions cache, hot config, first-run setup flag
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[kv_namespaces]]
binding = "PAPERCLIP_KV"
id = "FILL_IN_AFTER_DEPLOY"
# preview_id = "FILL_IN_AFTER_DEPLOY_PREVIEW"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hyperdrive — Phase 1: wraps Neon/Postgres for low-latency DB access
# After deploying: wrangler hyperdrive create paperclip-hyperdrive --connection-string="<neon-url>"
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[hyperdrive]]
binding = "HYPERDRIVE"
id = "FILL_IN_AFTER_DEPLOY"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Queues — background fanout (cost rollups, activity log flush, plugin jobs)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[queues.producers]]
binding = "PAPERCLIP_QUEUE"
queue = "paperclip-jobs"

[[queues.consumers]]
queue = "paperclip-jobs"
max_batch_size = 10
max_batch_timeout = 5
max_retries = 3
dead_letter_queue = "paperclip-jobs-dlq"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Durable Objects — per-task state, per-agent-run state, scheduler alarms
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[durable_objects.bindings]]
name = "TASK_DO"
class_name = "TaskDO"

[[durable_objects.bindings]]
name = "AGENT_RUN_DO"
class_name = "AgentRunDO"

[[durable_objects.bindings]]
name = "SCHEDULER_DO"
class_name = "SchedulerDO"

# DO migrations — bump new_classes when adding a new DO class
[[migrations]]
tag = "v1"
new_classes = ["TaskDO", "AgentRunDO", "SchedulerDO"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Workflows — checkpointed multi-step agent execution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[workflows]]
binding = "HEARTBEAT_WORKFLOW"
name = "heartbeat-workflow"
class_name = "HeartbeatWorkflow"
script_name = "paperclip-api"

[[workflows]]
binding = "PLUGIN_DISPATCH_WORKFLOW"
name = "plugin-dispatch-workflow"
class_name = "PluginDispatchWorkflow"
script_name = "paperclip-api"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cron triggers — fire heartbeat sweep, budget checks, DB backup
# Adjust intervals to taste; avoid high-frequency triggers (see CLOUDFLARE.md §10)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[triggers]
crons = [
  "*/5 * * * *",   # heartbeat sweep every 5 minutes
  "0 * * * *",     # budget threshold check every hour
  "0 3 * * *",     # DB backup daily at 03:00 UTC
]

6	export interface AdapterDeps {
7	  db: Db;
8	  storage: StorageService;
9	}

11	/**
12	 * Wraps a transport-agnostic {@link Handler} as an Express {@link RequestHandler}.
13	 *
14	 * Bridging notes:
15	 * - `req.body` is already parsed by express.json(); json() returns it directly
16	 *   so the raw body is never re-parsed.
17	 * - Path params come from `req.params`, query params from `req.query`.
18	 * - `req.actor.type === "none"` is normalised to `null` so handlers can do a
19	 *   simple null-check rather than inspecting the string.
20	 * - The Web API `Response` returned by the handler is forwarded to Express `res`
21	 *   by copying status, headers, and body.
22	 */
23	export function expressHandler(handler: Handler, deps: AdapterDeps): RequestHandler {
24	  return async (req, res, next) => {
25	    try {
26	      // Build the base URL from the incoming request. Express provides
27	      // req.hostname and req.originalUrl which together give us a fully-formed
28	      // URL object without needing the raw Host header gymnastics.
29	      const protocol = (req as { protocol?: string }).protocol ?? "http";
30	      const baseUrl = `${protocol}://${req.hostname}`;
31	      const url = new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl);
32	
33	      // Translate the Express actor (which may be "none") to ActorContext | null.
34	      const expressActor = req.actor;
35	      let actor: ActorContext | null = null;
36	      if (expressActor && expressActor.type !== "none") {
37	        actor = {
38	          type: expressActor.type,
39	          userId: expressActor.userId,
40	          agentId: expressActor.agentId,
41	          companyId: expressActor.companyId,
42	        };
43	      }
44	
45	      // Build the Web-API-compatible Headers object from Express's incoming
46	      // headers map. Express lowercases all header names, so this is safe.
47	      const headers = new Headers();
48	      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {
49	        if (value === undefined) continue;
50	        if (Array.isArray(value)) {
51	          for (const v of value) headers.append(name, v);
52	        } else {
53	          // value is string here; cast required because Object.entries loses
54	          // the discriminated IncomingHttpHeaders union.
55	          headers.set(name, value as string);
56	        }
57	      }
58	
59	      const ctx: RequestCtx = {
60	        method: req.method,
61	        url,
62	        headers,
63	
64	        // Body is already parsed by express.json() — just return the cached
65	        // object rather than re-serialising/re-parsing it.
66	        json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T> {
67	          return Promise.resolve(req.body as T);
68	        },
69	        text(): Promise<string> {
70	          if (typeof req.body === "string") return Promise.resolve(req.body);
71	          return Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(req.body));
72	        },
73	
74	        param(name: string): string | undefined {
75	          const value = req.params[name];
76	          return value === undefined ? undefined : String(value);
77	        },
78	        query(name: string): string | undefined {
79	          const value = req.query[name];
80	          if (value === undefined) return undefined;
81	          // Express query values can be string | ParsedQs | string[] | ParsedQs[]
82	          // We only surface the first scalar string.
83	          if (typeof value === "string") return value;
84	          if (Array.isArray(value)) {
85	            const first = value[0];
86	            return typeof first === "string" ? first : undefined;
87	          }
88	          return undefined;
89	        },
90	
91	        actor,
92	        db: deps.db,
93	        storage: deps.storage,
94	      };
95	
96	      const response = await handler(ctx);
97	
98	      res.status(response.status);
99	
100	      // Forward response headers (skip ones Express manages itself).
101	      response.headers.forEach((value, name) => {
102	        const lower = name.toLowerCase();
103	        if (lower === "transfer-encoding" || lower === "content-length") return;
104	        res.setHeader(name, value);
105	      });
106	
107	      const body = await response.text();
108	      res.send(body);
109	    } catch (err) {
110	      next(err);
111	    }
112	  };
113	}

```typescript
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js";
import postgres from "postgres";
import * as schema from "@paperclipai/db/src/schema/index.js";
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";

/**
 * Minimal interface that matches the Cloudflare Hyperdrive binding shape.
 * The full type is `Hyperdrive` from `@cloudflare/workers-types`, but we
 * declare a local structural equivalent so this file compiles without
 * requiring the workers-types package at import time.
 */
export interface HyperdriveBinding {
  /** The connection string Cloudflare injects — points to the Hyperdrive proxy. */
  connectionString: string;
}

/**
 * Creates a Drizzle `Db` instance backed by Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
 *
 * Hyperdrive terminates the Postgres connection pool near the Worker and
 * forwards queries to the upstream Neon/Postgres database over a long-lived
 * TCP connection. The `postgres-js` driver is compatible with the Workers
 * `nodejs_compat` flag, which provides a polyfilled TCP socket layer.
 *
 * Pool size is capped at 5 — each Worker invocation is short-lived so a
 * large pool wastes Hyperdrive connection slots.
 *
 * @param hyperdrive - The Hyperdrive binding from the Worker `Env`.
 */
export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: HyperdriveBinding): Db {
  // max: 5 keeps connection usage low across concurrent invocations.
  // prepare: false disables prepared-statement caching because Hyperdrive
  // routes across multiple upstream connections and cannot share PS state.
  const sql = postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString, {
    max: 5,
    prepare: false,
  });
  // drizzle-orm's postgres-js adapter returns a type that is structurally
  // identical to the `Db` exported from @paperclipai/db. The cast via
  // `unknown` is necessary only because the generic parameters differ at
  // the type level; the runtime shapes are identical.
  return drizzle(sql, { schema }) as unknown as Db;
}

import type { StorageProvider as StorageProviderId } from "@paperclipai/shared";

/**
 * Local copies of the StorageProvider interface types from
 * `server/src/storage/types.ts`. We duplicate only the shapes needed here
 * because importing Node-typed server modules into a Worker bundle would pull
 * in `node:stream` and other Node-only dependencies.
 *
 * Keep these in sync with `server/src/storage/types.ts`.
 */
export interface PutObjectInput {
  objectKey: string;
  body: Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer;
  contentType: string;
  contentLength: number;
}

export interface GetObjectInput {
  objectKey: string;
}

export interface GetObjectResult {
  /** ReadableStream — Workers environment returns Web Streams, not Node Readable. */
  stream: ReadableStream;
  contentType?: string;
  contentLength?: number;
  etag?: string;
  lastModified?: Date;
}

export interface HeadObjectResult {
  exists: boolean;
  contentType?: string;
  contentLength?: number;
  etag?: string;
  lastModified?: Date;
}

export interface StorageProvider {
  id: StorageProviderId;
  putObject(input: PutObjectInput): Promise<void>;
  getObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<GetObjectResult>;
  headObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<HeadObjectResult>;
  deleteObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<void>;
}

export interface R2ProviderConfig {
  /** Logical bucket name — recorded on stored objects for observability. */
  bucket: string;
  /**
   * Optional key prefix applied to every object key before passing to R2.
   * Useful when sharing a single R2 bucket across multiple environments.
   * Example: `"prod/"` → all keys become `"prod/<objectKey>"`.
   */
  prefix: string;
}

/**
 * `StorageProvider` implementation backed by Cloudflare R2.
 *
 * R2 is S3-compatible at the conceptual level but exposes a native binding
 * API (`R2Bucket`) in Workers rather than the AWS SDK. This provider wraps
 * that binding to satisfy the `StorageProvider` contract used throughout the
 * server package.
 *
 * The `stream` field in `GetObjectResult` is a `ReadableStream` (Web Streams
 * API) rather than a Node `Readable`. Callers in the Workers environment
 * should consume it directly. If a Node `Readable` is needed (e.g. in a
 * test shim), wrap it: `Readable.fromWeb(result.stream)`.
 */
export class R2Provider implements StorageProvider {
  readonly id: StorageProviderId = "r2";

  private readonly bucket: R2Bucket;
  private readonly prefix: string;

  constructor(bucket: R2Bucket, config: R2ProviderConfig) {
    this.bucket = bucket;
    this.prefix = config.prefix;
  }

  private key(objectKey: string): string {
    return this.prefix ? `${this.prefix}${objectKey}` : objectKey;
  }

  async putObject(input: PutObjectInput): Promise<void> {
    await this.bucket.put(this.key(input.objectKey), input.body, {
      httpMetadata: { contentType: input.contentType },
    });
  }

  async getObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<GetObjectResult> {
    const obj = await this.bucket.get(this.key(input.objectKey));
    if (!obj) {
      throw new Error(`R2: object not found: ${input.objectKey}`);
    }
    return {
      // R2ObjectBody.body is a ReadableStream<Uint8Array> — cast to the
      // opaque ReadableStream type our interface declares.
      stream: obj.body as unknown as ReadableStream,
      contentType: obj.httpMetadata?.contentType,
      contentLength: obj.size,
      etag: obj.etag,
      lastModified: obj.uploaded,
    };
  }

  async headObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<HeadObjectResult> {
    const obj = await this.bucket.head(this.key(input.objectKey));
    if (!obj) {
      return { exists: false };
    }
    return {
      exists: true,
      contentType: obj.httpMetadata?.contentType,
      contentLength: obj.size,
      etag: obj.etag,
      lastModified: obj.uploaded,
    };
  }

  async deleteObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<void> {
    await this.bucket.delete(this.key(input.objectKey));
  }
}

## What was created and edited

### Files created

**`server/src/http/types.ts`** (new, 35 lines)

Defines the three core transport-agnostic types:

- `ActorContext` (line 5) — the normalized subset of the Express actor shape, only for authenticated actors (`"board" | "agent"`). The `"none"` case from `express.d.ts` is represented as `null` on `RequestCtx.actor` instead.
- `RequestCtx` (line 13) — the minimal normalized request interface. `json<T>()`, `text()`, `param()`, `query()` are all methods so callers never touch transport primitives directly. `db` and `storage` are always present here; the optional-db case in health is handled in the route layer.
- `Handler` (line 28) — `(ctx: RequestCtx) => Promise<Response>`. Uses the Web API `Response` type so handlers are portable to Hono/Workers.
- `RouteDefinition` (line 30) — carry type for future route registration tables.

**`server/src/http/express-adapter.ts`** (new, 113 lines)

`expressHandler(handler, deps)` at line 23 does five bridging jobs:

1. URL construction (line 29-31): builds `new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl)` from `req.hostname` + `req.protocol`.
2. Actor normalization (line 34-43): maps `req.actor.type === "none"` → `null`; copies only the four fields defined in `ActorContext`.
3. Header bridging (line 47-57): iterates `req.headers` (already lowercased by Node's HTTP parser) into a Web `Headers` object; handles `string[]` multi-value headers via `append`.
4. Body bridging (line 66-72): `json()` returns `req.body` directly (already parsed by `express.json()`); `text()` JSON-serialises if body is not already a string. No re-parsing.
5. Response forwarding (line 98-108): copies `response.status`, iterates `response.headers` (skipping `transfer-encoding` and `content-length` which Express manages), then sends via `res.send()`. Errors fall through to `next(err)`.

**`server/src/http/index.ts`** (new, 2 lines)

Barrel re-export of all four types and `expressHandler`.
