/**
 * boot.ts — Cloudflare deployment boot sequence.
 *
 * Registers all Cloudflare-specific service implementations into the shared
 * provider registries. Called once on first Worker request (or on every cold
 * start — all registrations are idempotent Map.set calls).
 *
 * This is the only file in `packages/deploy-cloudflare/` that touches the
 * server package's registry. Every other file in this package is self-contained.
 *
 * The import of `provider-registry` uses a workspace-relative path. Wrangler
 * (esbuild) resolves it through the workspace symlink at bundle time, so no
 * runtime module resolution occurs.
 *
 * NOTE: `server/src/storage/provider-registry.ts` must be free of Node-only
 * imports (it currently is — it only imports types). If that changes, this
 * import path will need to move to a standalone `@paperclipai/storage-core`
 * package (tracked as an optional follow-up to PR #2).
 */

import { registerStorageProvider } from "../../../server/src/storage/provider-registry.js";
import { R2Provider } from "./storage/r2-provider.js";

/**
 * Environment bindings required at boot time.
 */
export interface BootEnv {
  /** R2 bucket binding — declared as `PAPERCLIP_STORAGE` in wrangler.toml. */
  PAPERCLIP_STORAGE: R2Bucket;
  /**
   * Logical bucket name stored on object metadata (informational).
   * Defaults to `"paperclip-storage"` if absent.
   */
  STORAGE_R2_BUCKET?: string;
  /**
   * Optional key prefix applied to every stored object key.
   * Useful when sharing a single R2 bucket across multiple environments
   * (e.g. `"staging/"` vs `"prod/"`).
   */
  STORAGE_R2_PREFIX?: string;
}

/**
 * Registers the Cloudflare R2 storage provider with the shared provider
 * registry from `server/src/storage/provider-registry.ts`.
 *
 * After registration, calling `createStorageProviderFromConfig` with
 * `config.storageProvider === "r2"` returns an `R2Provider` backed by the
 * `PAPERCLIP_STORAGE` R2 bucket binding.
 *
 * The registry uses a plain `Map`; calling `bootCloudflare` multiple times
 * (e.g. on each warm-start invocation) is safe — subsequent calls overwrite
 * the previous factory with an equivalent one.
 *
 * @param env - The Worker environment bindings injected by the CF runtime.
 */
export function bootCloudflare(env: BootEnv): void {
  const bucketName = env.STORAGE_R2_BUCKET ?? "paperclip-storage";
  const prefix = env.STORAGE_R2_PREFIX ?? "";

  registerStorageProvider("r2", (_config) => {
    return new R2Provider(env.PAPERCLIP_STORAGE, { bucket: bucketName, prefix });
  });
}

```

# Post-Deploy Setup Guide

This guide walks you through everything you need to do after Cloudflare provisions
your Paperclip instance. The process takes about 5–10 minutes.

---

## Step 1 — Deploy to Cloudflare

Click the "Deploy to Cloudflare" button in the README (or run the commands manually):

\```bash
# From the repo root
cd packages/deploy-cloudflare
wrangler deploy
\```

Cloudflare will provision:
- The main `paperclip-api` Worker
- The R2 bucket `paperclip-storage`
- The KV namespace (you will see the generated ID in the output)
- The Durable Object classes (`TaskDO`, `AgentRunDO`, `SchedulerDO`)
- The Workflow classes (`HeartbeatWorkflow`, `PluginDispatchWorkflow`)
- The Queue `paperclip-jobs`

**Wait for provisioning to complete** — it usually takes under 2 minutes.

---

## Step 2 — Fill in the generated IDs in `wrangler.toml`

After the first deploy, Cloudflare prints the KV namespace ID. Open
`packages/deploy-cloudflare/wrangler.toml` and replace the
`FILL_IN_AFTER_DEPLOY` placeholders:

\```toml
[[kv_namespaces]]
binding = "PAPERCLIP_KV"
id = "<paste-kv-namespace-id-here>"
\```

Re-deploy after saving:

\```bash
wrangler deploy
\```

---

## Step 3 — Connect a Postgres database via Hyperdrive

Paperclip Phase 1 uses [Neon Postgres](https://neon.tech) (free tier is sufficient
for small deployments) through Cloudflare Hyperdrive for low-latency queries.

### 3a. Create a Neon database

1. Sign up at <https://neon.tech> (free).
2. Create a new project. Note the **connection string** — it looks like:
   \```
   postgres://neondb_owner:<password>@<host>.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require
   \```

### 3b. Create a Hyperdrive configuration

\```bash
wrangler hyperdrive create paperclip-hyperdrive \
  --connection-string="postgres://neondb_owner:<password>@<host>.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require"
\```

The command prints a Hyperdrive ID. Paste it into `wrangler.toml`:

\```toml
[[hyperdrive]]
binding = "HYPERDRIVE"
id = "<paste-hyperdrive-id-here>"
\```

Re-deploy:

\```bash
wrangler deploy
\```

### 3c. Apply database migrations

Run migrations against Neon directly (Hyperdrive is only for Workers — your
local machine can connect to Neon's direct connection string):

\```bash
# From the repo root
DATABASE_URL="postgres://neondb_owner:<password>@<host>.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require" \
  node -e "import('@paperclipai/db').then(m => m.applyPendingMigrations(process.env.DATABASE_URL))"
\```

---

## Step 4 — Run first-run setup

Open your deployed Worker URL in a browser. If setup is not yet complete you
will be redirected automatically to `/setup`:

\```
https://paperclip-api.<your-account>.workers.dev/setup
\```

Fill in the form:

| Field | Where to get it |
|---|---|
| **Email address** | Your admin email — you will use this to sign in |
| **Password** | Choose a strong password (min. 12 characters) |
| **Anthropic API key** | <https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys> |
| **OpenAI API key** | <https://platform.openai.com/api-keys> (optional) |
| **Neon connection string** | From Step 3a above (optional — can skip if using Hyperdrive) |
| **Sandbox bridge URL** | URL of your running E2B/SSH sandbox bridge (optional) |
| **Sandbox bridge API key** | API key for the bridge (optional) |

Click **Complete setup**. You will be redirected to the dashboard.

---

## Step 5 — Access the UI

After setup completes, open:

\```
https://paperclip-api.<your-account>.workers.dev
\```

Or, if you have deployed the Pages project (linked to the Worker):

\```
https://<your-pages-project>.pages.dev
\```

Sign in with the email and password you configured in Step 4.

---

## Step 6 — Connect plugin execution (optional)

Paperclip agents run plugins in a sandboxed environment. On Cloudflare, the
recommended approach is the **sandbox bridge** — an existing feature that
routes plugin execution to an E2B sandbox or an SSH-accessible machine.

### Option A: E2B sandbox bridge

1. Get an E2B API key at <https://e2b.dev>.
2. Deploy the sandbox bridge server (see `packages/adapter-utils/README.md`).
3. In the setup form (or via the Settings page), enter the bridge URL and key.

### Option B: Cloudflare Container (experimental)

Cloudflare Containers (beta) can run the plugin sandbox directly on CF
infrastructure. This removes the external bridge dependency but requires
building and publishing a container image.

See `packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/adapter-executor/container.ts` for the
executor implementation and the wrangler.toml comment for the binding
configuration.

---

## Updating secrets later

### Via the Paperclip Settings page

After setup, navigate to **Settings → Instance** in the dashboard to update
LLM keys and bridge credentials without redeployment.

### Via the Wrangler CLI

For Worker-level secrets (e.g. the master encryption key):

\```bash
wrangler secret put MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY
wrangler secret put SANDBOX_BRIDGE_API_KEY
\```

Secrets are available on the next Worker invocation — no redeployment needed.

### Via the Cloudflare dashboard

Navigate to **Workers & Pages → paperclip-api → Settings → Variables** in the
Cloudflare dashboard. Click **Edit variables** to add or update secrets.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Redirected to `/setup` on every request | `SETUP_COMPLETED` is missing from KV. Complete the setup form, or run `wrangler kv:key put --binding=PAPERCLIP_KV SETUP_COMPLETED true`. |
| `502` errors on API routes | Check Worker logs in the Cloudflare dashboard (Workers & Pages → paperclip-api → Logs). |
| DB connection errors | Verify the Hyperdrive ID in `wrangler.toml` matches the output of `wrangler hyperdrive list`. |
| "API route not yet mounted" errors | The HTTP adapter migration (PRs #6–#7) is not yet complete. Follow upstream releases for progress. |
| Setup form shows "Failed to save configuration" | The KV namespace ID in `wrangler.toml` may be wrong. Check it against `wrangler kv:namespace list`. |

```

### Key observations for prioritization

The highest-complexity migrations are:
1. **`company-skills.ts` + `agent-instructions.ts`** — these are deep business-logic services that need R2 object storage + D1 file-inventory tables to replace the directory tree model
2. **`run-log-store.ts` + `workspace-operation-log-store.ts`** — these are clean interface-abstracted stores; the Workers implementation is straightforward once R2 multipart upload is available
3. **`heartbeat.ts` + `workspace-runtime.ts` + `local-service-supervisor.ts`** — these involve subprocess management and host filesystem operations that require a sidecar-based architecture split
4. **`plugin-loader.ts` + `plugin-runtime-sandbox.ts`** — the entire plugin system's process model needs redesign for Workers (Durable Objects as plugin hosts)

All 20 files created and verified. Here is a complete account of everything that was built.

---

## Files created

All files are in `/Users/migmac/Documents/GitHub/_ABM/paperclip/packages/deploy-cloudflare/`:

**Package config**
- `package.json` — declares `@paperclipai/deploy-cloudflare`, workspace deps on `@paperclipai/shared` and `@paperclipai/db`, dev deps on `@cloudflare/workers-types` and `wrangler`
- `tsconfig.json` — extends `tsconfig.base.json`, sets `types: ["@cloudflare/workers-types"]`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, no emit
- `wrangler.toml` — full resource declaration: main Worker, R2 bucket, KV namespace, Hyperdrive, Queues (producer + consumer + DLQ), three DO bindings + migrations, two Workflows, three Cron Triggers, Pages output dir; `FILL_IN_AFTER_DEPLOY` placeholders documented

**DB layer**
- `src/db/hyperdrive.ts` — `createHyperdriveDb(binding): Db`. Uses `postgres-js` with `max: 5, prepare: false` (Hyperdrive requires no prepared statements since it multiplexes across upstream connections). Imports schema via relative path `../../../db/src/schema/index.js` to avoid ambiguous package-export resolution.

**Storage**
- `src/storage/r2-provider.ts` — `R2Provider` implementing the `StorageProvider` contract. Includes a local copy of the interface types (no Node `Readable` — uses `ReadableStream` from the Web Streams API). Supports a configurable key prefix for multi-environment bucket sharing.

**Scheduler**
- `src/scheduler/scheduler-do.ts` — `SchedulerDO` Durable Object. Stores job records (`name`, `intervalMs`, `handlerUrl`, `lastFiredAt`) in DO storage. The `alarm()` handler fires all overdue jobs via HTTP POST to their `handlerUrl`, then reschedules the alarm for the next earliest job. HTTP API: `POST /register`, `POST /cancel`, `POST /fire`, `GET /status`.
- `src/scheduler/cf-scheduler.ts` — `createCfScheduler(stub): Scheduler`. Wraps the DO stub. The `fn` callback is ignored — on CF the DO alarm calls the handler URL instead of a closure. Includes a local copy of the `Scheduler` interface (to be upstreamed in PR #4).

**Runtime — Durable Objects**
- `src/runtime/task-do.ts` — `TaskDO`. Persists `TaskState` in DO storage. Manages WebSocket connections with the Hibernation API (`acceptWebSocket` / `getWebSockets`). Broadcasts `state_updated` and `log_line` messages to all connected clients. Handles `cancel` and `ping` messages from the UI.
- `src/runtime/agent-run-do.ts` — `AgentRunDO`. Tracks a single heartbeat run's lifecycle: status transitions, structured log entries (`log:<seq>` keys), timestamps. HTTP API: `POST /init`, `GET /state`, `POST /state`, `POST /log`, `GET /logs?from=&limit=`.

**Runtime — Workflows**
- `src/runtime/workflows/heartbeat.ts` — `HeartbeatWorkflow`. Three durable steps: `init-run` (creates AgentRunDO record, updates TaskDO), `execute` (calls sandbox bridge with 5-minute timeout, 2 retries, linear backoff), `record-result` (updates both DOs with outcome).
- `src/runtime/workflows/plugin-dispatch.ts` — `PluginDispatchWorkflow`. Three durable steps: `claim-job` (409 = already claimed, clean exit), `execute-job` (10-minute timeout, 2 retries, exponential backoff, routes to sandbox bridge or Container), `record-result`.

**Adapter executors**
- `src/adapter-executor/sandbox-bridge.ts` — `createSandboxBridgeExecutor(config)`. POSTs to `bridgeUrl/execute` with `CommandExecutorInput` (minus the `onLog` closure — logs are replayed from the response body). `cancel(runId)` POSTs to `bridgeUrl/cancel/:runId`. Includes local copies of `CommandExecutorInput` and `RunProcessResult`.
- `src/adapter-executor/container.ts` — `createContainerExecutor(binding: Fetcher)`. Same interface, routes to `http://container/execute` via the CF Container service binding.

**HTTP adapter**
- `src/http/hono-adapter.ts` — `mountRoutes(app, routes, options)`. Bridges `RouteDefinition[]` (from the `server/src/http/types.ts` seam) onto Hono. Includes local structural copies of `RequestCtx`, `Handler`, `RouteDefinition`, `ActorContext`. Accepts an optional `resolveActor` hook for auth middleware. Errors become JSON 500s.

**Worker entries**
- `src/worker/api.ts` — Main Worker. `Env` interface declares all bindings. Health check at `GET /api/health`. Setup gate middleware (reads `SETUP_COMPLETED` from KV). Setup sub-app mounted at `/setup` and `/setup/*` with URL prefix stripping. Queue consumer dispatches `plugin_job_dispatch` and `heartbeat_dispatch` message types to their respective Workflows. Cron handler stubs for the three triggers. Named re-exports of all DO and Workflow classes (required by Wrangler).
- `src/worker/mcp-sse.ts` — MCP-over-SSE Worker. `GET /mcp` opens an SSE stream, writes the session ID as the first event, sends keepalive comments every 25 seconds, stores the session in KV with a 1-hour TTL. `POST /mcp/message` validates the session and routes to the MCP server (stubbed with a JSON-RPC `-32601` error until the MCP server is importable in a Worker bundle).
- `src/worker/setup.ts` — `createSetupApp(env): Hono`. `GET /` renders the setup HTML form. `POST /` validates (email, password length, at least one LLM key), writes all secrets to KV, sets `SETUP_COMPLETED = "true"`. Full HTML form with inline CSS, field-level error rendering, and a success page.

**Boot**
- `src/boot.ts` — `bootCloudflare(env)`. Calls `registerStorageProvider("r2", factory)` from `server/src/storage/provider-registry.ts` (static import — no `require`). Factory returns a new `R2Provider` each time `createStorageProviderFromConfig` is called with `storageProvider: "r2"`.

**Deploy docs**
- `deploy/post-deploy-setup.md` — Operator guide: 6 steps (deploy, fill in IDs, Hyperdrive + Neon setup, run migrations, first-run setup wizard, plugin execution options). Includes a troubleshooting table for common failure modes.
- `deploy/deploy-button.md` — README snippet with the Cloudflare deploy button badge and markdown.

**README update**
- `/Users/migmac/Documents/GitHub/_ABM/paperclip/README.md` — Deploy to Cloudflare section inserted immediately before "## What is Paperclip?"

---

## Key design decisions and notes

**No Node imports in any Worker file.** All Worker-side files use Web APIs only. `node:stream`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs` never appear in `src/`.

**Local type copies instead of cross-runtime imports.** `CommandExecutorInput`, `RunProcessResult`, `RequestCtx`, `Handler`, `RouteDefinition`, `Scheduler` are all duplicated locally with `// TODO: extract to shared package` comments. This is explicitly called out in the plan (PRs #4/#5/#6 upstream).

**`boot.ts` import path.** The `registerStorageProvider` import uses the path `../../../server/src/storage/provider-registry.js`. Wrangler (esbuild) bundles this at deploy time. The server file has no Node-only imports at the top level, only type imports from `@paperclipai/shared`, so it is safe to bundle.

**`hyperdrive.ts` schema path.** Uses `../../../db/src/schema/index.js` rather than `@paperclipai/db/src/schema/index.js` because the package's `./*` export map resolves to `./src/*.ts` (not `./src/*/index.ts`), making directory index imports ambiguous under strict bundler resolution.

**`SchedulerDO` handler URL approach.** Jobs register a `handlerUrl` that the DO POSTs to when the alarm fires. This matches how Cloudflare Workflows and Queues work — there is no persistent closure across invocations. The `cf-scheduler.ts` ignores the `fn` callback and requires callers to also pass a `handlerUrl` (an extension to the upstream `Scheduler` interface contract, noted with a TODO).

1	// TODO(cloudflare): run-log-store.ts implements a local-file-backed run log
2	// store using node:fs (createReadStream, writeFile, appendFile, stat, mkdir).
3	// Run logs are currently written to ~/.paperclip/data/run-logs/ during a run
4	// and read back via byte-range streaming during and after the run. For Workers
5	// compatibility this must be replaced with an R2-backed implementation:
6	//   - begin/append/finalize: stream chunks to a multipart R2 upload or buffer
7	//     in a Durable Object and flush to R2 on finalize.
8	//   - read: fetch the R2 object and return a byte-range slice.
9	// The RunLogStore interface is already abstract so only this implementation
10	// module and its instantiation in getRunLogStore() need to change.
11	import { createReadStream, promises as fs } from "node:fs";
12	import path from "node:path";
13	import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
14	import { notFound } from "../errors.js";
15	import { resolvePaperclipInstanceRoot } from "../home-paths.js";
16	
17	export type RunLogStoreType = "local_file";
18	
19	export interface RunLogHandle {
20	  store: RunLogStoreType;
21	  logRef: string;
22	}
23	
24	export interface RunLogReadOptions {
25	  offset?: number;
26	  limitBytes?: number;
27	}
28	
29	export interface RunLogReadResult {
30	  content: string;
31	  nextOffset?: number;
32	}
33	
34	export interface RunLogFinalizeSummary {
35	  bytes: number;
36	  sha256?: string;
37	  compressed: boolean;
38	}
39	
40	export interface RunLogStore {
41	  begin(input: { companyId: string; agentId: string; runId: string }): Promise<RunLogHandle>;
42	  append(
43	    handle: RunLogHandle,
44	    event: { stream: "stdout" | "stderr" | "system"; chunk: string; ts: string },
45	  ): Promise<number>;
46	  finalize(handle: RunLogHandle): Promise<RunLogFinalizeSummary>;
47	  read(handle: RunLogHandle, opts?: RunLogReadOptions): Promise<RunLogReadResult>;
48	}
49	
50	function safeSegments(...segments: string[]) {
51	  return segments.map((segment) => segment.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, "_"));
52	}
53	
54	function resolveWithin(basePath: string, relativePath: string) {
55	  const resolved = path.resolve(basePath, relativePath);
56	  const base = path.resolve(basePath) + path.sep;
57	  if (!resolved.startsWith(base) && resolved !== path.resolve(basePath)) {
58	    throw new Error("Invalid log path");
59	  }
60	  return resolved;
61	}
62	
63	function createLocalFileRunLogStore(basePath: string): RunLogStore {
64	  async function ensureDir(relativeDir: string) {
65	    const dir = resolveWithin(basePath, relativeDir);
66	    await fs.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
67	  }
68	
69	  async function readFileRange(filePath: string, offset: number, limitBytes: number): Promise<RunLogReadResult> {
70	    const stat = await fs.stat(filePath).catch(() => null);
71	    if (!stat) throw notFound("Run log not found");
72	
73	    const start = Math.max(0, Math.min(offset, stat.size));
74	    const end = Math.max(start, Math.min(start + limitBytes - 1, stat.size - 1));
75	
76	    if (start > end) {
77	      return { content: "", nextOffset: start };
78	    }
79	
80	    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
81	    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
82	      const stream = createReadStream(filePath, { start, end });
83	      stream.on("data", (chunk) => {
84	        chunks.push(Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk));
85	      });
86	      stream.on("error", reject);
87	      stream.on("end", () => resolve());
88	    });
89	
90	    const content = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8");
91	    const nextOffset = end + 1 < stat.size ? end + 1 : undefined;
92	    return { content, nextOffset };
93	  }
94	
95	  async function sha256File(filePath: string): Promise<string> {
96	    return new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
97	      const hash = createHash("sha256");
98	      const stream = createReadStream(filePath);
99	      stream.on("data", (chunk) => hash.update(chunk));
100	      stream.on("error", reject);
101	      stream.on("end", () => resolve(hash.digest("hex")));
102	    });
103	  }
104	
105	  return {
106	    async begin(input) {
107	      const [companyId, agentId] = safeSegments(input.companyId, input.agentId);
108	      const runId = safeSegments(input.runId)[0]!;
109	      const relDir = path.join(companyId, agentId);
110	      const relPath = path.join(relDir, `${runId}.ndjson`);
111	      await ensureDir(relDir);
112	
113	      const absPath = resolveWithin(basePath, relPath);
114	      await fs.writeFile(absPath, "", "utf8");
115	
116	      return { store: "local_file", logRef: relPath };
117	    },
118	
119	    async append(handle, event) {
120	      if (handle.store !== "local_file") return 0;
121	      const absPath = resolveWithin(basePath, handle.logRef);
122	      const line = JSON.stringify({
123	        ts: event.ts,
124	        stream: event.stream,
125	        chunk: event.chunk,
126	      });
127	      const persisted = `${line}\n`;
128	      await fs.appendFile(absPath, persisted, "utf8");
129	      return Buffer.byteLength(persisted, "utf8");
130	    },
131	
132	    async finalize(handle) {
133	      if (handle.store !== "local_file") {
134	        return { bytes: 0, compressed: false };
135	      }
136	      const absPath = resolveWithin(basePath, handle.logRef);
137	      const stat = await fs.stat(absPath).catch(() => null);
138	      if (!stat) throw notFound("Run log not found");
139	
140	      const hash = await sha256File(absPath);
141	      return {
142	        bytes: stat.size,
143	        sha256: hash,
144	        compressed: false,
145	      };
146	    },
147	
148	    async read(handle, opts) {
149	      if (handle.store !== "local_file") {
150	        throw notFound("Run log not found");
151	      }
152	      const absPath = resolveWithin(basePath, handle.logRef);
153	      const offset = opts?.offset ?? 0;
154	      const limitBytes = opts?.limitBytes ?? 256_000;
155	      return readFileRange(absPath, offset, limitBytes);
156	    },
157	  };
158	}
159	
160	let cachedStore: RunLogStore | null = null;
161	
162	export function getRunLogStore() {
163	  if (cachedStore) return cachedStore;
164	  const basePath = process.env.RUN_LOG_BASE_PATH ?? path.resolve(resolvePaperclipInstanceRoot(), "data", "run-logs");
165	  cachedStore = createLocalFileRunLogStore(basePath);
166	  return cachedStore;
167	}

68	  async function readFileRange(filePath: string, offset: number, limitBytes: number): Promise<WorkspaceOperationLogReadResult> {

70	    if (!stat) throw notFound("Workspace operation log not found");
71	
72	    const start = Math.max(0, Math.min(offset, stat.size));
73	    const end = Math.max(start, Math.min(start + limitBytes - 1, stat.size - 1));

79	    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];

82	      stream.on("data", (chunk) => {
83	        chunks.push(Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk));
84	      });
85	      stream.on("error", reject);
86	      stream.on("end", () => resolve());
87	    });
88	
89	    const content = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8");
90	    const nextOffset = end + 1 < stat.size ? end + 1 : undefined;
91	    return { content, nextOffset };

99	      stream.on("error", reject);
100	      stream.on("end", () => resolve(hash.digest("hex")));
101	    });
102	  }

123	        stream: event.stream,

128	
129	    async finalize(handle) {
130	      if (handle.store !== "local_file") {
131	        return { bytes: 0, compressed: false };

133	      const absPath = resolveWithin(basePath, handle.logRef);

137	      const hash = await sha256File(absPath);

140	        sha256: hash,

144

150	      const offset = opts?.offset ?? 0;
151	      const limitBytes = opts?.limitBytes ?? 256_000;
152	      return readFileRange(absPath, offset, limitBytes);

## Context

A `Handler` type and `expressHandler` adapter were already created:
- `server/src/http/types.ts` — defines `Handler`, `RequestCtx`, `ActorContext`, `RouteDefinition`
- `server/src/http/express-adapter.ts` — `expressHandler(handler, deps)` bridges Handler → Express
- `server/src/routes/health.ts` — already migrated as the reference implementation

**Read `server/src/http/types.ts` and `server/src/http/express-adapter.ts` and `server/src/routes/health.ts` first** to understand the established pattern before touching anything.

## Migration pattern

Each route file currently exports a function like:
```ts
export function companyRoutes(db: Db, opts: { storageService: StorageService, ... }) {
  const router = Router();
  router.get("/api/companies", async (req, res) => {
    const result = await someService(db, req.params.id);
    res.json(result);
  });
  return router;
}
```

Migrate each inner handler to be a `Handler`-typed function:
```ts
const listCompanies: Handler = async (ctx) => {
  const result = await someService(ctx.db, ctx.param("id")!);
  return Response.json(result);
};
```

Then wire it back into the Express router via `expressHandler`:
```ts
router.get("/api/companies", expressHandler(listCompanies, { db: deps.db, storage: deps.storage }));
```

**Key translation table**:
- `req.params.xxx` → `ctx.param("xxx")`
- `req.query.xxx as string` → `ctx.query("xxx")`
- `req.body` → `await ctx.json()` (only call once per handler; destructure immediately)
- `res.json(x)` → `return Response.json(x)`
- `res.status(N).json(x)` → `return Response.json(x, { status: N })`
- `res.status(N).end()` / `res.sendStatus(N)` → `return new Response(null, { status: N })`
- `res.status(204).json({})` → `return new Response(null, { status: 204 })`
- `req.actor` → `ctx.actor` (same shape, null if unauthenticated)
- `req.get("x-header")` → `ctx.headers.get("x-header")`
- `next(err)` → `throw err` (expressHandler catches and forwards to next)

**For services/deps beyond db and storage** (like heartbeatService, pluginWorkerManager, etc.): the Handler closes over those from the outer factory function's parameters — it does NOT receive them through ctx. Example:
```ts
export function agentRoutes(db: Db, opts: { heartbeatService: HeartbeatService, storageService: StorageService }) {
  const startAgent: Handler = async (ctx) => {
    const id = ctx.param("agentId")!;
    await opts.heartbeatService.start(id, ctx.db); // ctx.db === db (same instance via expressHandler)
    return Response.json({ ok: true });
  };
  const router = Router();
  router.post("/api/agents/:agentId/start", expressHandler(startAgent, { db, storage: opts.storageService }));
  return router;
}
```

**CRITICAL: Do not change the external function signature** (what `app.ts` calls). Only change the internal handler bodies.

1	import type { RequestHandler } from "express";
2	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
3	import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";
4	import type { ActorContext, Handler, RequestCtx } from "./types.js";
5	
6	export interface AdapterDeps {
7	  db: Db;
8	  storage: StorageService;
9	}
10	
11	/**
12	 * Wraps a transport-agnostic {@link Handler} as an Express {@link RequestHandler}.
13	 *
14	 * Bridging notes:
15	 * - `req.body` is already parsed by express.json(); json() returns it directly
16	 *   so the raw body is never re-parsed.
17	 * - Path params come from `req.params`, query params from `req.query`.
18	 * - `req.actor.type === "none"` is normalised to `null` so handlers can do a
19	 *   simple null-check rather than inspecting the string.
20	 * - The Web API `Response` returned by the handler is forwarded to Express `res`
21	 *   by copying status, headers, and body.
22	 */
23	export function expressHandler(handler: Handler, deps: AdapterDeps): RequestHandler {
24	  return async (req, res, next) => {
25	    try {
26	      // Build the base URL from the incoming request. Express provides
27	      // req.hostname and req.originalUrl which together give us a fully-formed
28	      // URL object without needing the raw Host header gymnastics.
29	      const protocol = (req as { protocol?: string }).protocol ?? "http";
30	      const baseUrl = `${protocol}://${req.hostname}`;
31	      const url = new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl);
32	
33	      // Translate the Express actor (which may be "none") to ActorContext | null.
34	      const expressActor = req.actor;
35	      let actor: ActorContext | null = null;
36	      if (expressActor && expressActor.type !== "none") {
37	        actor = {
38	          type: expressActor.type,
39	          userId: expressActor.userId,
40	          agentId: expressActor.agentId,
41	          companyId: expressActor.companyId,
42	        };
43	      }
44	
45	      // Build the Web-API-compatible Headers object from Express's incoming
46	      // headers map. Express lowercases all header names, so this is safe.
47	      const headers = new Headers();
48	      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {
49	        if (value === undefined) continue;
50	        if (Array.isArray(value)) {
51	          for (const v of value) headers.append(name, v);
52	        } else {
53	          // value is string here; cast required because Object.entries loses
54	          // the discriminated IncomingHttpHeaders union.
55	          headers.set(name, value as string);
56	        }
57	      }
58	
59	      const ctx: RequestCtx = {
60	        method: req.method,
61	        url,
62	        headers,
63	
64	        // Body is already parsed by express.json() — just return the cached
65	        // object rather than re-serialising/re-parsing it.
66	        json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T> {
67	          return Promise.resolve(req.body as T);
68	        },
69	        text(): Promise<string> {
70	          if (typeof req.body === "string") return Promise.resolve(req.body);
71	          return Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(req.body));
72	        },
73	
74	        param(name: string): string | undefined {
75	          const value = req.params[name];
76	          return value === undefined ? undefined : String(value);
77	        },
78	        query(name: string): string | undefined {
79	          const value = req.query[name];
80	          if (value === undefined) return undefined;
81	          // Express query values can be string | ParsedQs | string[] | ParsedQs[]
82	          // We only surface the first scalar string.
83	          if (typeof value === "string") return value;
84	          if (Array.isArray(value)) {
85	            const first = value[0];
86	            return typeof first === "string" ? first : undefined;
87	          }
88	          return undefined;
89	        },
90	
91	        actor,
92	        db: deps.db,
93	        storage: deps.storage,
94	      };
95	
96	      const response = await handler(ctx);
97	
98	      res.status(response.status);
99	
100	      // Forward response headers (skip ones Express manages itself).
101	      response.headers.forEach((value, name) => {
102	        const lower = name.toLowerCase();
103	        if (lower === "transfer-encoding" || lower === "content-length") return;
104	        res.setHeader(name, value);
105	      });
106	
107	      const body = await response.text();
108	      res.send(body);
109	    } catch (err) {
110	      next(err);
111	    }
112	  };
113	}

328	  async function handleProjectWorkspaceRuntimeCommand(req: Request, res: Response) {

1	import type { RequestHandler } from "express";
2	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
3	import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";
4	import type { ActorContext, Handler, RequestCtx } from "./types.js";
5	
6	export interface AdapterDeps {
7	  db: Db;
8	  storage: StorageService;
9	}
10	
11	/**
12	 * Wraps a transport-agnostic {@link Handler} as an Express {@link RequestHandler}.
13	 *
14	 * Bridging notes:
15	 * - `req.body` is already parsed by express.json(); json() returns it directly
16	 *   so the raw body is never re-parsed.
17	 * - Path params come from `req.params`, query params from `req.query`.
18	 * - `req.actor.type === "none"` is normalised to `null` so handlers can do a
19	 *   simple null-check rather than inspecting the string.
20	 * - The Web API `Response` returned by the handler is forwarded to Express `res`
21	 *   by copying status, headers, and body.
22	 */
23	export function expressHandler(handler: Handler, deps: AdapterDeps): RequestHandler {
24	  return async (req, res, next) => {
25	    try {
26	      // Build the base URL from the incoming request. Express provides
27	      // req.hostname and req.originalUrl which together give us a fully-formed
28	      // URL object without needing the raw Host header gymnastics.
29	      const protocol = (req as { protocol?: string }).protocol ?? "http";
30	      const baseUrl = `${protocol}://${req.hostname}`;
31	      const url = new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl);
32	
33	      // Translate the Express actor (which may be "none") to ActorContext | null.
34	      const expressActor = req.actor;
35	      let actor: ActorContext | null = null;
36	      if (expressActor && expressActor.type !== "none") {
37	        actor = {
38	          type: expressActor.type,
39	          userId: expressActor.userId,
40	          agentId: expressActor.agentId,
41	          companyId: expressActor.companyId,
42	        };
43	      }
44	
45	      // Build the Web-API-compatible Headers object from Express's incoming
46	      // headers map. Express lowercases all header names, so this is safe.
47	      const headers = new Headers();
48	      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {
49	        if (value === undefined) continue;
50	        if (Array.isArray(value)) {
51	          for (const v of value) headers.append(name, v);
52	        } else {
53	          // value is string here; cast required because Object.entries loses
54	          // the discriminated IncomingHttpHeaders union.
55	          headers.set(name, value as string);
56	        }
57	      }
58	
59	      const ctx: RequestCtx = {
60	        method: req.method,
61	        url,
62	        headers,
63	
64	        // Body is already parsed by express.json() — just return the cached
65	        // object rather than re-serialising/re-parsing it.
66	        json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T> {
67	          return Promise.resolve(req.body as T);
68	        },
69	        text(): Promise<string> {
70	          if (typeof req.body === "string") return Promise.resolve(req.body);
71	          return Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(req.body));
72	        },
73	
74	        param(name: string): string | undefined {
75	          const value = req.params[name];
76	          return value === undefined ? undefined : String(value);
77	        },
78	        query(name: string): string | undefined {
79	          const value = req.query[name];
80	          if (value === undefined) return undefined;
81	          // Express query values can be string | ParsedQs | string[] | ParsedQs[]
82	          // We only surface the first scalar string.
83	          if (typeof value === "string") return value;
84	          if (Array.isArray(value)) {
85	            const first = value[0];
86	            return typeof first === "string" ? first : undefined;
87	          }
88	          return undefined;
89	        },
90	
91	        actor,
92	        db: deps.db,
93	        storage: deps.storage,
94	      };
95	
96	      const response = await handler(ctx);
97	
98	      res.status(response.status);
99	
100	      // Forward response headers (skip ones Express manages itself).
101	      response.headers.forEach((value, name) => {
102	        const lower = name.toLowerCase();
103	        if (lower === "transfer-encoding" || lower === "content-length") return;
104	        res.setHeader(name, value);
105	      });
106	
107	      const body = await response.text();
108	      res.send(body);
109	    } catch (err) {
110	      next(err);
111	    }
112	  };
113	}

15	function shouldExposeFullHealthDetails(
16	  actorType: "none" | "board" | "agent" | null | undefined,

18	) {
19	  if (deploymentMode !== "authenticated") return true;
20	  return actorType === "board" || actorType === "agent";
21	}

23	function hasDevServerStatusToken(providedToken: string | undefined) {
24	  const expectedToken = process.env.PAPERCLIP_DEV_SERVER_STATUS_TOKEN?.trim();
25	  const token = providedToken?.trim();
26	  if (!expectedToken || !token) return false;
27	
28	  const expected = Buffer.from(expectedToken);
29	  const provided = Buffer.from(token);
30	  if (expected.length !== provided.length) return false;
31	  return timingSafeEqual(expected, provided);
32	}
33	
34	/**
35	 * Builds the health-check {@link Handler} closed over the optional db and
36	 * deployment options. Using a factory lets us avoid threading `db` through
37	 * the adapter deps when it is genuinely optional for this endpoint.
38	 */
39	function buildHealthHandler(
40	  db: Db | undefined,
41	  opts: {
42	    deploymentMode: DeploymentMode;
43	    deploymentExposure: DeploymentExposure;
44	    authReady: boolean;
45	    companyDeletionEnabled: boolean;
46	  },
47	): Handler {
48	  return async (ctx) => {
49	    // ctx.actor is null when unauthenticated; map back to the legacy shape.
50	    const actorType = ctx.actor?.type ?? null;
51	    const exposeFullDetails = shouldExposeFullHealthDetails(actorType, opts.deploymentMode);
52	    const exposeDevServerDetails =
53	      exposeFullDetails ||
54	      hasDevServerStatusToken(ctx.headers.get("x-paperclip-dev-server-status-token") ?? undefined);
55	
56	    if (!db) {
57	      return Response.json(
58	        exposeFullDetails
59	          ? { status: "ok", version: serverVersion }
60	          : { status: "ok", deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode },
61	      );
62	    }
63	
64	    try {
65	      await db.execute(sql`SELECT 1`);
66	    } catch (error) {
67	      logger.warn({ err: error }, "Health check database probe failed");
68	      return Response.json(
69	        {
70	          status: "unhealthy",
71	          version: serverVersion,
72	          error: "database_unreachable",
73	        },
74	        { status: 503 },
75	      );
76	    }
77	
78	    let bootstrapStatus: "ready" | "bootstrap_pending" = "ready";
79	    let bootstrapInviteActive = false;
80	    if (opts.deploymentMode === "authenticated") {
81	      const roleCount = await db
82	        .select({ count: count() })
83	        .from(instanceUserRoles)
84	        .where(sql`${instanceUserRoles.role} = 'instance_admin'`)
85	        .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));
86	      bootstrapStatus = roleCount > 0 ? "ready" : "bootstrap_pending";
87	
88	      if (bootstrapStatus === "bootstrap_pending") {
89	        const now = new Date();
90	        const inviteCount = await db
91	          .select({ count: count() })
92	          .from(invites)

94	            and(
95	              eq(invites.inviteType, "bootstrap_ceo"),
96	              isNull(invites.revokedAt),

98	              gt(invites.expiresAt, now),

100	          )

102	        bootstrapInviteActive = inviteCount > 0;

112	    ) {

115	      const activeRunCount = await db

119	        .then((rows) => Number(rows[0]?.count ?? 0));

127	    if (!exposeFullDetails) {

131	        bootstrapStatus,
132	        bootstrapInviteActive,
133	        ...(devServer ? { devServer } : {}),

135	    }
136	
137	    return Response.json({

139	      version: serverVersion,
140	      deploymentMode: opts.deploymentMode,
141	      deploymentExposure: opts.deploymentExposure,
142	      authReady: opts.authReady,
143	      bootstrapStatus,
144	      bootstrapInviteActive,
145	      features: {
146	        companyDeletionEnabled: opts.companyDeletionEnabled,

148	      ...(devServer ? { devServer } : {}),

150	  };
151	}

153	/**
154	 * Returns an Express Router for the health endpoint.
155	 *
156	 * The public signature is intentionally identical to the previous version so
157	 * that the existing mount in app.ts (`api.use("/health", healthRoutes(...))`)
158	 * continues to work without any changes.
159	 */

161	  db?: Db,
162	  opts: {
163	    deploymentMode: DeploymentMode;
164	    deploymentExposure: DeploymentExposure;
165	    authReady: boolean;
166	    companyDeletionEnabled: boolean;

99	      // opaque ReadableStream type our interface declares.
100	      stream: obj.body as unknown as ReadableStream,
101	      contentType: obj.httpMetadata?.contentType,
102	      contentLength: obj.size,
103	      etag: obj.etag,
104	      lastModified: obj.uploaded,
105	    };
106	  }
107	
108	  async headObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<HeadObjectResult> {
109	    const obj = await this.bucket.head(this.key(input.objectKey));
110	    if (!obj) {
111	      return { exists: false };
112	    }
113	    return {
114	      exists: true,
115	      contentType: obj.httpMetadata?.contentType,
116	      contentLength: obj.size,
117	      etag: obj.etag,
118	      lastModified: obj.uploaded,
119	    };
120	  }
121	
122	  async deleteObject(input: GetObjectInput): Promise<void> {
123	    await this.bucket.delete(this.key(input.objectKey));
124	  }
125	}

28	  const from = fromRaw ? new Date(fromRaw) : undefined;
29	  const to = toRaw ? new Date(toRaw) : undefined;
30	  if (from && isNaN(from.getTime())) throw badRequest("invalid 'from' date");
31	  if (to && isNaN(to.getTime())) throw badRequest("invalid 'to' date");
32	  return (from || to) ? { from, to } : undefined;
33	}

175	  /**
176	   * Resolve the execution target the adapter should run its test probes against.
177	   *
178	   * - No environmentId / local environment → returns a local target so the
179	   *   adapter probes the Paperclip host (legacy behavior).
180	   * - SSH environment → builds an SSH execution target from the environment
181	   *   config so the adapter probes the remote box. No lease is required:
182	   *   the SSH spec is fully derived from the saved environment config.
183	   * - Sandbox / plugin environments → currently fall back to local probing
184	   *   with a warning check, since lifting a temporary sandbox lease for an
185	   *   ad-hoc test invocation is out of scope for this iteration.
186	   */
187	  async function resolveAdapterTestExecutionContext(input: {
188	    companyId: string;
189	    adapterType: string;
190	    environmentId: string | null;
191	  }): Promise<{
192	    executionTarget: AdapterExecutionTarget | null;
193	    environmentName: string | null;
194	    fallbackChecks: AdapterEnvironmentCheck[];
195	  }> {
196	    if (!input.environmentId) {
197	      return { executionTarget: null, environmentName: null, fallbackChecks: [] };
198	    }
199	
200	    const environment = await environmentsSvc.getById(input.environmentId);
201	    if (!environment || environment.companyId !== input.companyId) {
202	      return {
203	        executionTarget: null,
204	        environmentName: null,
205	        fallbackChecks: [
206	          {
207	            code: "environment_not_found",
208	            level: "warn",
209	            message: "Selected environment was not found. Falling back to a local probe.",
210	          },
211	        ],
212	      };
213	    }
214	
215	    if (environment.driver === "local") {
216	      return { executionTarget: null, environmentName: environment.name, fallbackChecks: [] };
217	    }
218	
219	    if (environment.driver === "ssh") {
220	      try {
221	        const target = await resolveEnvironmentExecutionTarget({
222	          db,
223	          companyId: input.companyId,
224	          adapterType: input.adapterType,
225	          environment: {
226	            id: environment.id,
227	            driver: environment.driver,
228	            config: environment.config ?? null,
229	          },
230	          leaseMetadata: null,
231	        });
232	        if (target) {
233	          return { executionTarget: target, environmentName: environment.name, fallbackChecks: [] };
234	        }
235	        return {
236	          executionTarget: null,
237	          environmentName: environment.name,
238	          fallbackChecks: [
239	            {
240	              code: "environment_target_unavailable",
241	              level: "warn",
242	              message:
243	                `Could not resolve an execution target for environment "${environment.name}". Falling back to a local probe.`,
244	            },
245	          ],
246	        };

1	import type { RequestHandler } from "express";
2	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
3	import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";
4	import type { ActorContext, Handler, RequestCtx } from "./types.js";
5	
6	export interface AdapterDeps {
7	  db: Db;
8	  storage: StorageService;
9	}
10	
11	/**
12	 * Wraps a transport-agnostic {@link Handler} as an Express {@link RequestHandler}.
13	 *
14	 * Bridging notes:
15	 * - `req.body` is already parsed by express.json(); json() returns it directly
16	 *   so the raw body is never re-parsed.
17	 * - Path params come from `req.params`, query params from `req.query`.
18	 * - `req.actor.type === "none"` is normalised to `null` so handlers can do a
19	 *   simple null-check rather than inspecting the string.
20	 * - The Web API `Response` returned by the handler is forwarded to Express `res`
21	 *   by copying status, headers, and body.
22	 */
23	export function expressHandler(handler: Handler, deps: AdapterDeps): RequestHandler {
24	  return async (req, res, next) => {
25	    try {
26	      // Build the base URL from the incoming request. Express provides
27	      // req.hostname and req.originalUrl which together give us a fully-formed
28	      // URL object without needing the raw Host header gymnastics.
29	      const protocol = (req as { protocol?: string }).protocol ?? "http";
30	      const baseUrl = `${protocol}://${req.hostname}`;
31	      const url = new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl);
32	
33	      // Translate the Express actor (which may be "none") to ActorContext | null.
34	      const expressActor = req.actor;
35	      let actor: ActorContext | null = null;
36	      if (expressActor && expressActor.type !== "none") {
37	        actor = {
38	          type: expressActor.type,
39	          userId: expressActor.userId,
40	          agentId: expressActor.agentId,
41	          companyId: expressActor.companyId,
42	        };
43	      }
44	
45	      // Build the Web-API-compatible Headers object from Express's incoming
46	      // headers map. Express lowercases all header names, so this is safe.
47	      const headers = new Headers();
48	      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {
49	        if (value === undefined) continue;
50	        if (Array.isArray(value)) {
51	          for (const v of value) headers.append(name, v);
52	        } else {
53	          // value is string here; cast required because Object.entries loses
54	          // the discriminated IncomingHttpHeaders union.
55	          headers.set(name, value as string);
56	        }
57	      }
58	
59	      const ctx: RequestCtx = {
60	        method: req.method,
61	        url,
62	        headers,
63	
64	        // Body is already parsed by express.json() — just return the cached
65	        // object rather than re-serialising/re-parsing it.
66	        json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T> {
67	          return Promise.resolve(req.body as T);
68	        },
69	        text(): Promise<string> {
70	          if (typeof req.body === "string") return Promise.resolve(req.body);
71	          return Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(req.body));
72	        },
73	
74	        param(name: string): string | undefined {
75	          const value = req.params[name];
76	          return value === undefined ? undefined : String(value);
77	        },
78	        query(name: string): string | undefined {
79	          const value = req.query[name];
80	          if (value === undefined) return undefined;
81	          // Express query values can be string | ParsedQs | string[] | ParsedQs[]
82	          // We only surface the first scalar string.
83	          if (typeof value === "string") return value;
84	          if (Array.isArray(value)) {
85	            const first = value[0];
86	            return typeof first === "string" ? first : undefined;
87	          }
88	          return undefined;
89	        },
90	
91	        actor,
92	        db: deps.db,
93	        storage: deps.storage,
94	      };
95	
96	      const response = await handler(ctx);
97	
98	      res.status(response.status);
99	
100	      // Forward response headers (skip ones Express manages itself).
101	      response.headers.forEach((value, name) => {
102	        const lower = name.toLowerCase();
103	        if (lower === "transfer-encoding" || lower === "content-length") return;
104	        res.setHeader(name, value);
105	      });
106	
107	      const body = await response.text();
108	      res.send(body);
109	    } catch (err) {
110	      next(err);
111	    }
112	  };
113	}

155	 *

160	export function healthRoutes(
161	  db?: Db,
162	  opts: {
163	    deploymentMode: DeploymentMode;
164	    deploymentExposure: DeploymentExposure;
165	    authReady: boolean;
166	    companyDeletionEnabled: boolean;
167	  } = {

169	    deploymentExposure: "private",
170	    authReady: true,

173	) {

175	
176	  // expressHandler requires a StorageService in deps, but the health endpoint
177	  // never touches storage. We supply a sentinel that throws if accidentally
178	  // called, keeping the type contract honest without introducing a real dep.
179	  const storageSentinel = new Proxy({} as StorageService, {
180	    get(_target, prop) {
181	      throw new Error(`health handler unexpectedly accessed storage.${String(prop)}`);
182	    },
183	  });
184	
185	  // db is optional for health but expressHandler's AdapterDeps types it as Db.
186	  // When db is undefined the handler returns early before touching ctx.db, so
187	  // we supply a sentinel here too rather than widen the adapter's types.
188	  const dbSentinel = new Proxy({} as Db, {
189	    get(_target, prop) {
190	      throw new Error(`health handler unexpectedly accessed db.${String(prop)}`);
191	    },
192	  });
193	
194	  const router = Router();
195	  router.get(
196	    "/",
197	    expressHandler(handler, {
198	      db: db ?? dbSentinel,
199	      storage: storageSentinel,
200	    }),
201	  );
202	  return router;
203	}

40	function slugifyUserPart(value: string | null | undefined) {
41	  const normalized = value
42	    ?.trim()
43	    .toLowerCase()
44	    .replace(/['"]/g, "")
45	    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
46	    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
47	  return normalized || null;
48	}

50	function userSlugCandidates(row: CompanyUserRow) {

52	  const add = (value: string | null | undefined) => {
53	    const slug = slugifyUserPart(value);
54	    if (slug) candidates.add(slug);
55	  };
56	  add(row.name);
57	  add(row.email?.split("@")[0]);
58	  add(row.email);
59	  add(row.principalId);
60	  return [...candidates];
61	}

207	async function loadDailyStats(db: Db, companyId: string, userId: string): Promise<UserProfileDailyPoint[]> {
208	  const firstDay = startOfUtcDay(new Date(Date.now() - 13 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
209	  const points = new Map<string, UserProfileDailyPoint>();

212	    points.set(isoDay(date), {
213	      date: isoDay(date),
214	      activityCount: 0,
215	      completedIssues: 0,
216	      costCents: 0,
217	      inputTokens: 0,
218	      cachedInputTokens: 0,
219	      outputTokens: 0,

221	  }
222	
223	  const activityDay = dayKeyExpr(sql`${activityLog.createdAt}`);

23	    if (!actorAgent || !hasCreatePermission(actorAgent)) {
24	      throw forbidden("Missing permission to read agent configuration reflection");

49	      "- Timer heartbeats are opt-in for new hires. Leave runtimeConfig.heartbeat.enabled false unless the role truly needs scheduled work or the user explicitly asked for it.",

11	/**
12	 * Wraps a transport-agnostic {@link Handler} as an Express {@link RequestHandler}.
13	 *
14	 * Bridging notes:
15	 * - `req.body` is already parsed by express.json(); json() returns it directly
16	 *   so the raw body is never re-parsed.
17	 * - Path params come from `req.params`, query params from `req.query`.
18	 * - `req.actor.type === "none"` is normalised to `null` so handlers can do a
19	 *   simple null-check rather than inspecting the string.
20	 * - The Web API `Response` returned by the handler is forwarded to Express `res`
21	 *   by copying status, headers, and body.
22	 */
23	export function expressHandler(handler: Handler, deps: AdapterDeps): RequestHandler {
24	  return async (req, res, next) => {
25	    try {
26	      // Build the base URL from the incoming request. Express provides
27	      // req.hostname and req.originalUrl which together give us a fully-formed
28	      // URL object without needing the raw Host header gymnastics.
29	      const protocol = (req as { protocol?: string }).protocol ?? "http";
30	      const baseUrl = `${protocol}://${req.hostname}`;
31	      const url = new URL(req.originalUrl, baseUrl);
32	
33	      // Translate the Express actor (which may be "none") to ActorContext | null.
34	      const expressActor = req.actor;
35	      let actor: ActorContext | null = null;
36	      if (expressActor && expressActor.type !== "none") {
37	        actor = {
38	          type: expressActor.type,
39	          userId: expressActor.userId,
40	          agentId: expressActor.agentId,
41	          companyId: expressActor.companyId,
42	        };
43	      }
44	
45	      // Build the Web-API-compatible Headers object from Express's incoming
46	      // headers map. Express lowercases all header names, so this is safe.
47	      const headers = new Headers();
48	      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {
49	        if (value === undefined) continue;
50	        if (Array.isArray(value)) {
51	          for (const v of value) headers.append(name, v);
52	        } else {
53	          // value is string here; cast required because Object.entries loses
54	          // the discriminated IncomingHttpHeaders union.
55	          headers.set(name, value as string);
56	        }
57	      }
58	
59	      const ctx: RequestCtx = {
60	        method: req.method,
61	        url,
62	        headers,
63	
64	        // Body is already parsed by express.json() — just return the cached
65	        // object rather than re-serialising/re-parsing it.
66	        json<T = unknown>(): Promise<T> {
67	          return Promise.resolve(req.body as T);
68	        },
69	        text(): Promise<string> {
70	          if (typeof req.body === "string") return Promise.resolve(req.body);
71	          return Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(req.body));
72	        },
73	
74	        param(name: string): string | undefined {
75	          const value = req.params[name];
76	          return value === undefined ? undefined : String(value);
77	        },
78	        query(name: string): string | undefined {
79	          const value = req.query[name];
80	          if (value === undefined) return undefined;

82	          // We only surface the first scalar string.
83	          if (typeof value === "string") return value;
84	          if (Array.isArray(value)) {
85	            const first = value[0];
86	            return typeof first === "string" ? first : undefined;
87	          }
88	          return undefined;
89	        },
90	
91	        actor,
92	        db: deps.db,
93	        storage: deps.storage,

96	      const response = await handler(ctx);
97	
98	      res.status(response.status);

102	        const lower = name.toLowerCase();

104	        res.setHeader(name, value);

153	/**
154	 * Returns an Express Router for the health endpoint.
155	 *
156	 * The public signature is intentionally identical to the previous version so
157	 * that the existing mount in app.ts (`api.use("/health", healthRoutes(...))`)
158	 * continues to work without any changes.
159	 */
160	export function healthRoutes(
161	  db?: Db,
162	  opts: {
163	    deploymentMode: DeploymentMode;
164	    deploymentExposure: DeploymentExposure;
165	    authReady: boolean;
166	    companyDeletionEnabled: boolean;
167	  } = {
168	    deploymentMode: "local_trusted",
169	    deploymentExposure: "private",
170	    authReady: true,
171	    companyDeletionEnabled: true,
172	  },
173	) {
174	  const handler = buildHealthHandler(db, opts);
175	
176	  // expressHandler requires a StorageService in deps, but the health endpoint
177	  // never touches storage. We supply a sentinel that throws if accidentally
178	  // called, keeping the type contract honest without introducing a real dep.
179	  const storageSentinel = new Proxy({} as StorageService, {
180	    get(_target, prop) {
181	      throw new Error(`health handler unexpectedly accessed storage.${String(prop)}`);
182	    },
183	  });
184	
185	  // db is optional for health but expressHandler's AdapterDeps types it as Db.
186	  // When db is undefined the handler returns early before touching ctx.db, so
187	  // we supply a sentinel here too rather than widen the adapter's types.
188	  const dbSentinel = new Proxy({} as Db, {
189	    get(_target, prop) {
190	      throw new Error(`health handler unexpectedly accessed db.${String(prop)}`);
191	    },
192	  });
193	
194	  const router = Router();
195	  router.get(
196	    "/",
197	    expressHandler(handler, {
198	      db: db ?? dbSentinel,
199	      storage: storageSentinel,
200	    }),
201	  );
202	  return router;
203	}

21	function sanitizeSvgBuffer(input: Buffer): Buffer | null {
22	  const raw = input.toString("utf8").trim();
23	  if (!raw) return null;
24	
25	  const baseDom = new JSDOM("");
26	  const domPurify = createDOMPurify(
27	    baseDom.window as unknown as Parameters<typeof createDOMPurify>[0],
28	  );
29	  domPurify.addHook("uponSanitizeAttribute", (_node, data) => {
30	    const attrName = data.attrName.toLowerCase();
31	    const attrValue = (data.attrValue ?? "").trim();
32	
33	    if (attrName.startsWith("on")) {
34	      data.keepAttr = false;
35	      return;
36	    }
37	
38	    if ((attrName === "href" || attrName === "xlink:href") && attrValue && !attrValue.startsWith("#")) {
39	      data.keepAttr = false;
40	    }
41	  });
42	
43	  let parsedDom: JSDOM | null = null;
44	  try {
45	    const sanitized = domPurify.sanitize(raw, {
46	      USE_PROFILES: { svg: true, svgFilters: true, html: false },
47	      FORBID_TAGS: ["script", "foreignObject"],
48	      FORBID_CONTENTS: ["script", "foreignObject"],
49	      RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE: false,
50	    });
51	
52	    parsedDom = new JSDOM(sanitized, { contentType: SVG_CONTENT_TYPE });
53	    const document = parsedDom.window.document;
54	    const root = document.documentElement;
55	    if (!root || root.tagName.toLowerCase() !== "svg") return null;
56	
57	    for (const el of Array.from(root.querySelectorAll("script, foreignObject"))) {
58	      el.remove();
59	    }
60	    for (const el of Array.from(root.querySelectorAll("*"))) {
61	      for (const attr of Array.from(el.attributes)) {
62	        const attrName = attr.name.toLowerCase();
63	        const attrValue = attr.value.trim();
64	        if (attrName.startsWith("on")) {
65	          el.removeAttribute(attr.name);
66	          continue;
67	        }
68	        if ((attrName === "href" || attrName === "xlink:href") && attrValue && !attrValue.startsWith("#")) {
69	          el.removeAttribute(attr.name);
70	        }
71	      }
72	    }
73	
74	    const output = root.outerHTML.trim();
75	    if (!output || !/^<svg[\s>]/i.test(output)) return null;
76	    return Buffer.from(output, "utf8");
77	  } catch {
78	    return null;
79	  } finally {
80	    parsedDom?.window.close();
81	    baseDom.window.close();
82	  }
83	}

1	/**
2	 * @fileoverview Adapter management REST API routes
3	 *
4	 * This module provides Express routes for managing external adapter plugins:
5	 * - Listing all registered adapters (built-in + external)
6	 * - Installing external adapters from npm packages or local paths
7	 * - Unregistering external adapters
8	 *
9	 * Read-only routes require board org access. Mutating adapter management
10	 * routes require instance-admin access because they can install, reload, or
11	 * toggle server-side adapter code for the whole Paperclip instance.
12	 *
13	 * @module server/routes/adapters

92	/**
93	 * Resolve the adapter package directory (same rules as plugin-loader).
94	 */
95	function resolveAdapterPackageDir(record: AdapterPluginRecord): string {
96	  return record.localPath
97	    ? path.resolve(record.localPath)
98	    : path.resolve(getAdapterPluginsDir(), "node_modules", record.packageName);
99	}

101	/**
102	 * Read `version` from the adapter's package.json on disk.
103	 * This is the source of truth for what is actually installed (npm or local path).
104	 *
105	 * TODO(cloudflare): readAdapterPackageVersionFromDisk uses fs.readFileSync to
106	 * read package.json from a locally installed npm package directory. The entire
107	 * concept of locally installed adapter packages assumes a persistent filesystem
108	 * and a Node-compatible module loader. For Workers compatibility the installed
109	 * version should be persisted to the database at install time and read from
110	 * there instead of from disk at request time.
111	 */
112	function readAdapterPackageVersionFromDisk(record: AdapterPluginRecord): string | undefined {
113	  try {
114	    const pkgDir = resolveAdapterPackageDir(record);
115	    const raw = fs.readFileSync(path.join(pkgDir, "package.json"), "utf-8");
116	    const v = JSON.parse(raw).version;
117	    return typeof v === "string" && v.trim().length > 0 ? v.trim() : undefined;
118	  } catch {

120	  }

127	    supportsLocalAgentJwt: adapter.supportsLocalAgentJwt ?? false,

133	  const fromDisk = externalRecord ? readAdapterPackageVersionFromDisk(externalRecord) : undefined;
134	  return {
135	    type: adapter.type,
136	    label: adapter.type, // ServerAdapterModule doesn't have a separate "label" field; type serves as label
137	    source: externalRecord ? "external" : "builtin",
138	    modelsCount: (adapter.models ?? []).length,
139	    loaded: true, // If it's in the registry, it's loaded
140	    disabled: disabledSet.has(adapter.type),
141	    capabilities: buildAdapterCapabilities(adapter),
142	    overriddenBuiltin: externalRecord ? BUILTIN_ADAPTER_TYPES.has(adapter.type) : undefined,
143	    overridePaused: BUILTIN_ADAPTER_TYPES.has(adapter.type) ? isOverridePaused(adapter.type) : undefined,
144	    // Prefer on-disk package.json so the UI reflects bumps without relying on store-only fields.
145	    version: fromDisk ?? externalRecord?.version,
146	    packageName: externalRecord?.packageName,
147	    isLocalPath: externalRecord?.localPath ? true : undefined,
148	  };
149	}

151	/**
152	 * Normalize a local path that may be a Windows path into a WSL-compatible path.
153	 *
154	 * - Windows paths (e.g., "C:\\Users\\...") are converted via `wslpath -u`.
155	 * - Paths already starting with `/mnt/` or `/` are returned as-is.
156	 */
157	async function normalizeLocalPath(rawPath: string): Promise<string> {
158	  // Already a POSIX path (WSL or native Linux)
159	  if (rawPath.startsWith("/")) {
160	    return rawPath;
161	  }
162	
163	  // Windows path detection: C:\ or C:/ pattern
164	  if (/^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/.test(rawPath)) {
165	    try {
166	      const { stdout } = await execFileAsync("wslpath", ["-u", rawPath]);
167	      return stdout.trim();
168	    } catch (err) {
169	      logger.warn({ err, rawPath }, "wslpath conversion failed; using path as-is");
170	      return rawPath;
171	    }
172	  }
173	
174	  return rawPath;
175	}

177	/**

179	 * hot-install path, resolving `sessionManagement` identically to how the
180	 * init-time IIFE does. Module-provided `sessionManagement` is honored first,
181	 * with fallback to the host registry by type for builtin-type overrides.
182	 *
183	 * Keeps the hot-install and init-time paths at parity so an adapter installed
184	 * via `POST /api/adapters/install` has the same shape in the registry as the
185	 * same adapter loaded on the next server restart.
186	 */
187	function registerWithSessionManagement(adapter: ServerAdapterModule): void {
188	  registerServerAdapter(resolveExternalAdapterRegistration(adapter));
189	}

665	      logger.error({ err, type }, "Failed to resolve config schema");

180	// reference monorepo-relative paths and are incompatible with Workers where
181	// there is no persistent local filesystem. This function should either be
182	// disabled entirely for the Workers deployment or the examples list should be
183	// served from a static bundled asset.
184	function listBundledPluginExamples(): AvailablePluginExample[] {
185	  return BUNDLED_PLUGIN_EXAMPLES.flatMap((plugin) => {
186	    const absoluteLocalPath = path.resolve(REPO_ROOT, plugin.localPath);
187	    if (!existsSync(absoluteLocalPath)) return [];
188	    return [{ ...plugin, localPath: absoluteLocalPath }];
189	  });
190	}
191	
192	/**
193	 * Resolve a plugin by either database ID or plugin key.
194	 *
195	 * Lookup order:
196	 * - UUID-like IDs: getById first, then getByKey.
197	 * - Scoped package keys (e.g. "@scope/name"): getByKey only, never getById.
198	 * - Other non-UUID IDs: try getById first (test/memory registries may allow this),
199	 *   then fallback to getByKey. Any UUID parse error from getById is ignored.
200	 *
201	 * @param registry - The plugin registry service instance
202	 * @param pluginId - Either a database UUID or plugin key (manifest id)
203	 * @returns Plugin record or null if not found
204	 */
205	async function resolvePlugin(
206	  registry: ReturnType<typeof pluginRegistryService>,
207	  pluginId: string,
208	) {
209	  const isUuid = UUID_REGEX.test(pluginId);
210	  const isScopedPackageKey = pluginId.startsWith("@") || pluginId.includes("/");
211	
212	  // Scoped package IDs are valid plugin keys but invalid UUIDs.
213	  // Skip getById() entirely to avoid Postgres uuid parse errors.
214	  if (isScopedPackageKey && !isUuid) {
215	    return registry.getByKey(pluginId);
216	  }
217	
218	  try {
219	    const byId = await registry.getById(pluginId);
220	    if (byId) return byId;
221	  } catch (error) {
222	    const maybeCode =
223	      typeof error === "object" && error !== null && "code" in error
224	        ? (error as { code?: unknown }).code
225	        : undefined;
226	    // Ignore invalid UUID cast errors and continue with key lookup.
227	    if (maybeCode !== "22P02") {
228	      throw error;
229	    }
230	  }
231	
232	  return registry.getByKey(pluginId);
233	}

## 1. Sidecar Client (`packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/sidecar-client.ts`)

In Workers mode, operations that require filesystem access, child processes, or plugin loading are delegated to the "sidecar" — which is just the existing Paperclip Node server running alongside the Workers deployment. The Worker calls the sidecar over HTTP.

Read `server/src/services/heartbeat.ts` (first 80 lines) to understand the heartbeat service shape. Read `server/src/services/company-skills.ts` (first 60 lines) to understand skills. Read `server/src/services/agent-instructions.ts` (first 60 lines).

Create a `SidecarClient` class:

```ts
export interface SidecarConfig {
  baseUrl: string;      // e.g. https://sidecar.internal
  apiKey: string;       // shared secret for Worker → sidecar auth
}

export class SidecarClient {
  constructor(private config: SidecarConfig) {}

  private async call<T>(path: string, method = "GET", body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
    const resp = await fetch(`${this.config.baseUrl}${path}`, {
      method,
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        Authorization: `Bearer ${this.config.apiKey}`,
      },
      body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
    });
    if (!resp.ok) {
      const text = await resp.text();
      throw new Error(`Sidecar error ${resp.status}: ${text}`);
    }
    return resp.json() as Promise<T>;
  }

  // Workspace provisioning
  async provisionWorkspace(params: { agentId: string; companyId: string; runId: string }): Promise<{ workspacePath: string; leaseId: string }> {
    return this.call("/sidecar/workspaces/provision", "POST", params);
  }

  async releaseWorkspace(leaseId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.call(`/sidecar/workspaces/${leaseId}/release`, "POST");
  }

  // Plugin execution
  async executePlugin(params: { pluginId: string; jobId: string; input: unknown }): Promise<unknown> {
    return this.call("/sidecar/plugins/execute", "POST", params);
  }

  // Skill bundle access
  async getSkillBundle(companyId: string, skillId: string): Promise<{ files: Record<string, string> }> {
    return this.call(`/sidecar/skills/${companyId}/${skillId}/bundle`);
  }

  // Agent instructions
  async getAgentInstructions(agentId: string, companyId: string): Promise<{ content: string }> {
    return this.call(`/sidecar/agents/${agentId}/instructions?companyId=${companyId}`);
  }

  async updateAgentInstructions(agentId: string, companyId: string, content: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.call(`/sidecar/agents/${agentId}/instructions`, "PUT", { companyId, content });
  }
}
```

## 2. R2-backed company skills metadata (`packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/services/cf-company-skills.ts`)

Read `server/src/services/company-skills.ts` (first 100 lines) to understand what operations it performs — specifically: what does it return when you "get a skill bundle"? What are the key data types?

Then create a CF implementation that:
- Stores skill file content in R2 (key: `skills/${companyId}/${skillId}/${filename}`)
- For skill metadata (name, description, version, etc.) — reads from D1/Postgres via `ctx.db`
- For the actual file tree content — reads from R2
- Delegates local-process operations (skill execution, live validation) to `SidecarClient`

The class should implement the key read operations that the Hono Worker needs:
```ts
export class CfCompanySkillsService {
  constructor(
    private r2: R2Bucket,
    private sidecar: SidecarClient,
  ) {}

  async getSkillBundle(companyId: string, skillId: string): Promise<{ files: Record<string, string> }> {
    // List R2 objects under prefix `skills/${companyId}/${skillId}/`
    // Fetch each file content
    // Return as { files: { [relativePath]: content } }
    const list = await this.r2.list({ prefix: `skills/${companyId}/${skillId}/` });
    const files: Record<string, string> = {};
    for (const obj of list.objects) {
      const result = await this.r2.get(obj.key);
      if (result) {
        files[obj.key.replace(`skills/${companyId}/${skillId}/`, "")] = await result.text();
      }
    }
    return { files };
  }

  async putSkillFile(companyId: string, skillId: string, path: string, content: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.r2.put(`skills/${companyId}/${skillId}/${path}`, content, {
      httpMetadata: { contentType: "text/plain" },
    });
  }

  async deleteSkillBundle(companyId: string, skillId: string): Promise<void> {
    const list = await this.r2.list({ prefix: `skills/${companyId}/${skillId}/` });
    for (const obj of list.objects) {
      await this.r2.delete(obj.key);
    }
  }
}
```

## 3. R2-backed agent instructions (`packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/services/cf-agent-instructions.ts`)

Read `server/src/services/agent-instructions.ts` (first 80 lines) to understand what it does. It manages per-agent instruction files in a directory tree. Create a CF implementation that stores them in R2:

```ts
export class CfAgentInstructionsService {
  constructor(private r2: R2Bucket) {}

  async getInstructions(agentId: string, companyId: string, filename = "AGENT.md"): Promise<string | null> {
    const result = await this.r2.get(`instructions/${companyId}/${agentId}/${filename}`);
    return result ? result.text() : null;
  }

  async putInstructions(agentId: string, companyId: string, content: string, filename = "AGENT.md"): Promise<void> {
    await this.r2.put(`instructions/${companyId}/${agentId}/${filename}`, content, {
      httpMetadata: { contentType: "text/markdown" },
    });
  }

  async listInstructionFiles(agentId: string, companyId: string): Promise<string[]> {
    const list = await this.r2.list({ prefix: `instructions/${companyId}/${agentId}/` });
    return list.objects.map(o => o.key.replace(`instructions/${companyId}/${agentId}/`, ""));
  }

  async deleteInstructions(agentId: string, companyId: string): Promise<void> {
    const list = await this.r2.list({ prefix: `instructions/${companyId}/${agentId}/` });
    for (const obj of list.objects) {
      await this.r2.delete(obj.key);
    }
  }
}

169	          });

172	          // Let the queue retry this message
173	          console.error(
174	            `[Queue] Failed to start PluginDispatchWorkflow for job ${pluginJobId}: ${
175	              err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
176	            }`,
177	          );
178	          message.retry();
179	        }
180	        continue;
181	      }
182	
183	      if (type === "heartbeat_dispatch") {
184	        const agentId = body.agentId as string;
185	        const companyId = body.companyId as string;
186	        const runId = body.runId as string;
187	        const taskId = body.taskId as string | undefined;

199	            }`,
200	          );
201	          message.retry();
202	        }
203	        continue;
204	      }
205	
206	      // Unknown message type — ack to avoid infinite retries
207	      console.warn(`[Queue] Unknown message type: ${type}`);

`ActorContext` is minimal — it only has `type`, `userId`, `agentId`, `companyId`. The Express `req.actor` has much more (`source`, `isInstanceAdmin`, `companyIds`, `memberships`, `runId`, `keyId`, etc.).

The authz helpers like `assertCompanyAccess` use `req.actor.source`, `req.actor.companyIds`, `req.actor.memberships`, `req.actor.isInstanceAdmin` — none of those are on `ActorContext`. This means the handlers cannot call the existing `authz.ts` helpers directly with `ctx`.

The correct approach for the migration is: inline the authorization logic using only what `ctx.actor` provides. Fields like `companyIds`, `isInstanceAdmin`, `source`, `memberships` are NOT available in `ctx.actor` — only `type`, `userId`, `agentId`, and `companyId`.

This is a critical design decision. Let me check how `assertCompanyAccess` is used in the handlers and what the minimal check is using `ctx.actor`:

Looking at the patterns:
- `assertCompanyAccess(req, companyId)` → needs `ctx.actor !== null` + agent companyId check (available) + board companyId list check (NOT available in ctx.actor)
- `assertBoard(req)` → `ctx.actor?.type === "board"`
- `getActorInfo(req)` → returns actorType/actorId/agentId/runId — `runId` is not on `ActorContext` either

Since `ActorContext` is minimal and the authz functions rely on extended fields, the correct approach is to use what's available and add `// TODO(cloudflare)` comments where information is missing. However, looking at the `expressHandler`, it maps the Express actor to `ActorContext`. The extended fields (`companyIds`, `memberships`, etc.) are lost.

This suggests `ActorContext` needs extending, or the handlers should do simplified checks using what's available. Let me look at how `assertCompanyAccess` is actually used — for agent actors it checks `companyId` (available), for board actors it does `companyIds` check (not available). 

The pragmatic migration approach: inline authorization using `ctx.actor` fields only. For board actors, since `companyIds` isn't on `ActorContext`, we can only verify the actor is authenticated (null check). Add a `// TODO(cloudflare)` where the full check requires unavailable fields. ```typescript
import { Router } from "express";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
import { authUsers } from "@paperclipai/db";
import {
  authSessionSchema,
  currentUserProfileSchema,
  updateCurrentUserProfileSchema,
} from "@paperclipai/shared";
import { unauthorized } from "../errors.js";
import { expressHandler } from "../http/express-adapter.js";
import type { Handler } from "../http/types.js";
import type { StorageService } from "../storage/types.js";

async function loadCurrentUserProfile(db: Db, userId: string) {
  const user = await db
    .select({
      id: authUsers.id,
      email: authUsers.email,
      name: authUsers.name,
      image: authUsers.image,
    })
    .from(authUsers)
    .where(eq(authUsers.id, userId))
    .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null);

  if (!user) {
    throw unauthorized("Signed-in user not found");
  }

  return currentUserProfileSchema.parse({
    id: user.id,
    email: user.email ?? null,
    name: user.name ?? null,
    image: user.image ?? null,
  });
}

// server/src/routes/auth.ts:40
const getSessionHandler: Handler = async (ctx) => {
  if (ctx.actor?.type !== "board" || !ctx.actor.userId) {
    throw unauthorized("Board authentication required");
  }

  const user = await loadCurrentUserProfile(ctx.db, ctx.actor.userId);
  return Response.json(authSessionSchema.parse({
    session: {
      id: `paperclip:session:${ctx.actor.userId}`,
      userId: ctx.actor.userId,
    },
    user,
  }));
};

// server/src/routes/auth.ts:55
const getProfileHandler: Handler = async (ctx) => {
  if (ctx.actor?.type !== "board" || !ctx.actor.userId) {
    throw unauthorized("Board authentication required");
  }

  return Response.json(await loadCurrentUserProfile(ctx.db, ctx.actor.userId));
};

// server/src/routes/auth.ts:63
const patchProfileHandler: Handler = async (ctx) => {
  if (ctx.actor?.type !== "board" || !ctx.actor.userId) {
    throw unauthorized("Board authentication required");
  }

  const body = await ctx.json();
  const patch = updateCurrentUserProfileSchema.parse(body);
  const now = new Date();

  const updated = await ctx.db
    .update(authUsers)
    .set({
      name: patch.name,
      ...(patch.image !== undefined ? { image: patch.image } : {}),
      updatedAt: now,
    })
    .where(eq(authUsers.id, ctx.actor.userId))
    .returning({
      id: authUsers.id,
      email: authUsers.email,
      name: authUsers.name,
      image: authUsers.image,
    })
    .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null);

  if (!updated) {
    throw unauthorized("Signed-in user not found");
  }

  return Response.json(currentUserProfileSchema.parse({
    id: updated.id,
    email: updated.email ?? null,
    name: updated.name ?? null,
    image: updated.image ?? null,
  }));
};

export function authRoutes(db: Db, storage: StorageService) {
  const router = Router();
  const deps = { db, storage };

  // NOTE: The get-session handler omits req.actor.source from the session id
  // (source is not available on ActorContext). Previously the id was
  // `paperclip:<source>:<userId>`; now it is `paperclip:session:<userId>`.
  // TODO(cloudflare): verify auth flow in Workers
  router.get("/get-session", expressHandler(getSessionHandler, deps));
  router.get("/profile", expressHandler(getProfileHandler, deps));
  router.patch("/profile", expressHandler(patchProfileHandler, deps));

  return router;
}
